description: The key insight is that persistent homology — the backbone of topological data analysis — provides a natural framework for quantum error correction. Each bar in a persistence barcode corresponds to a topological feature that persists across scales, and these persistent features ARE the logical qubits of a topological quantum code. Conjecture: For any simplicial complex K, the first persistent homology bar with birth time epsilon and death time delta defines a quantum error-correcting code with distance d >= delta/epsilon and rate k/H_1(K). The barcode IS the code specification: birth times give stabilizer generators, death times give code distance. Why now: the surface code is just H_1 of a grid, and its distance equals the longest bar in the barcode. This generalizes immediately. Test: construct the barcode code for the torus (distance 4, rate 1/9) and verify it matches the toric code. Prove the distance bound for arbitrary complexes. Impact: every dataset with persistent topology becomes a quantum code, and the barcode distance theorem gives a systematic way to construct new codes from topology.
proof_strategy: Define the barcode code B(K) for a simplicial complex K: qubits = vertices, stabilizers = boundary maps of 1-simplices, logical operators = persistent 1-cycles. Prove: (1) the stabilizer group is Abelian and squares to identity, (2) the code distance equals the ratio delta/epsilon where epsilon and delta are birth and death of the longest bar, (3) the code rate equals dim(H_1(K))/|V(K)|. Test: for K = square lattice on torus, verify distance = min(L,W) and rate = 1/N matching the toric code.
title: Topological Quantum Error Correction from Homological Persistence

description: The key insight is that protein folding minimizes a topological energy: the persistent homology barcode of the protein's contact map. The native fold of a protein is the configuration that minimizes the total persistence of the contact filtration. Conjecture: The native state of a protein P minimizes sum_i (d_i - b_i) over all possible 3D configurations, where {b_i, d_i} is the persistent homology barcode of the distance matrix of P's C-alpha atoms. Why now: AlphaFold2 showed that contact maps are sufficient for structure prediction, but it used deep learning without understanding WHY contact maps work. Persistent homology provides the mathematical reason: the barcode captures the topological constraints (no self-intersection, hydrophobic core, etc.) that determine the fold. Test: compute the barcode for 100 proteins from the PDB and verify that the native fold has lower total persistence than 1000 random decoy folds for each protein. Impact: protein folding becomes a topological optimization problem with a provably unique minimum, explaining why folding is fast and reliable despite Levinthal's paradox.
proof_strategy: Define the contact filtration for protein P with N residues: for distance threshold t, build the Vietoris-Rips complex R_t from the pairwise C-alpha distances. Compute the persistent homology barcode PH(P, configuration) = {(b_i, d_i)}. Define TotalPersistence(P) = sum_i (d_i - b_i). Conjecture: the native fold minimizes TotalPersistence over all valid configurations. Test: for each of 100 PDB proteins, generate 1000 decoy configurations using Rosetta, compute TotalPersistence for each, and verify the native fold has the minimum. Prove that TotalPersistence is a Lyapunov function for folding dynamics in the simplified HP model.
title: Biological Topology: Protein Folding as Persistent Homology Optimization

description: The Riemann zeta function zeta(s) has non-trivial zeros at s = 1/2 + i*gamma_n on the critical line (assuming RH). These zeros encode deep arithmetic information. Conjecture: the zeros gamma_n are the spectrum of a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space, and this operator is the Casimir element of a quantum group G_q. Specifically, define the 'zeta quantum group' G_q as the q-deformation of SU(2) where q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} (using the first zero gamma_1 ~ 14.13). The Casimir element C_q of G_q has eigenvalues that are quadratic functions of the representation labels, and the spectrum of C_q is {n(n+1) : n in N}. Conjecture: the Riemann zeros gamma_n are related to the spectrum of C_q by gamma_n = f(spectrum(C_q)) for some function f. If f is linear, this would mean the zeros are evenly spaced, which is false (the zeros have Poisson-like spacings). If f is logarithmic, gamma_n ~ pi*n/log(n) which matches the average spacing. Conjecture: the spectral statistics of C_q match the GUE random matrix statistics of the Riemann zeros (Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture). Test: compute the spectrum of C_q for G_q with q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} and compare the spectral statistics with the Riemann zeros. Impact: the Riemann hypothesis is a representation-theoretic statement about quantum groups.
proof_strategy: Define the quantum group SU_q(2) with q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} where gamma_1 ~ 14.13 is the first Riemann zero. The representation theory: irreducible representations V_n of dimension n+1 for n = 0, 1, 2, .... The Casimir element C_q acts on V_n with eigenvalue [n]_q * [n+1]_q where [m]_q = (q^m - q^{-m})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer. For q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1}: [m]_q = sin(m * pi * gamma_1) / sin(pi * gamma_1). The eigenvalues of C_q on V_n are: lambda_n = [n]_q * [n+1]_q = sin(n*pi*gamma_1) * sin((n+1)*pi*gamma_1) / sin(pi*gamma_1)^2. Conjecture: the set {lambda_n : n >= 1} encodes the Riemann zeros in a way that preserves their statistical properties. Specifically, the level spacings {lambda_{n+1} - lambda_n} should follow the GUE distribution (Wigner-Dyson surmise). Test: compute lambda_n for n = 1..1000, compute the level spacings, and compare with the GUE distribution P(s) = (32/pi^2) * s^2 * exp(-4*s^2/pi^2). Also compare with the Riemann zero spacings. This requires numerical computation of q-deformed representations.
title: Quantum Groups from Number Theory: The Riemann Hypothesis as a Representation Problem

description: Formalize the Erdős-Rényi random graph model G(n,p). Prove the sharp threshold for connectivity at p = ln(n)/n. Prove the phase transition for giant components at p = 1/n. Formalize the second moment method for subgraph counting.

description: Formalize key results of Bishop's constructive analysis in Lean 4. Prove the constructive intermediate value theorem (with explicit modulus). Construct computable real numbers and prove completeness. Compare with classical results.
title: Constructive Mathematics: Bishop's Analysis

description: Formalize tropical convex sets and tropical polytopes. Prove the tropical analogue of the Minkowski-Weyl theorem. Show that tropical linear programming is solvable in polynomial time. Connect to mean payoff games.
title: Tropical Convexity and Linear Programming

description: Formalize the P vs NP problem (Clay Millennium): prove or refute that every language decidable in nondeterministic polynomial time is decidable in deterministic polynomial time, with the NP-completeness of SAT as the canonical witness. (Cook-Levin; Clay 2000)
title: P vs NP (Millennium): Are Verifiable Problems Always Solvable?

description: Huang proved the sensitivity conjecture. Extend: prove tighter bounds on degree-sensitivity relationship of Boolean functions. Formalize the spectral approach via signed adjacency matrices.
title: Sensitivity Conjecture Extensions

description: Prove that π, e, √2, or any fundamental constant is normal. Formalize the connection to equidistribution and algebraic independence.
title: Normality of Mathematical Constants

description: Formalize Tononi's Integrated Information Theory (IIT) as a rigorous mathematical framework. Prove that the maximum integrated information Phi of a system is the minimum information partition. Show that Phi is NP-hard to compute and construct polynomial-time approximations.
title: Consciousness as Integrated Information: Mathematical Foundations

description: For every integer k ≥ 2 and every ε > 0, there exist infinitely many n-vertex k-uniform uncrowded hypergraphs (girth ≥ 5) H with maximum degree Δ (where Δ → ∞) such that α(H) ≤ (1+ε) · n · ((1/(k-1)) · log(Δ)/Δ))^(1/(k-1)). This conjecture asserts that the shattering-threshold lower bound proven in this paper—which achieves the constant (1/(k-1))^(1/(k-1))—is asymptotically tight, meaning no larger leading constant is achievable for the class of uncrowded hypergraphs.
proof_strategy: Construct random k-uniform uncrowded hypergraphs (e.g., via the configuration model conditioned on girth ≥ 5) with maximum degree Δ and analyze their independence number using the second moment method. Show that typical instances of such random hypergraphs have independence number at most (1+o(1))·n·((1/(k-1))·log(Δ)/Δ))^(1/(k-1)), matching the lower bound from above. Alternatively, use explicit pseudorandom constructions from finite geometry to build families attaining the upper bound.
title: Asymptotic Tightness of the Shattering Threshold for Uncrowded Hypergraphs

description: For any tree graph, there exists a set of vertices that is simultaneously an isolating set and a packing (2-packing). An isolating set is a set S such that the subgraph induced by vertices outside the closed neighborhood of S has no edges. A packing is a set S such that the closed neighborhoods of the vertices in S are pairwise disjoint.
proof_strategy: Proceed by structural induction on the tree. For a leaf vertex, apply the inductive hypothesis on the subtree remaining after removing the leaf and its neighbor, and construct the packing isolating set by carefully adding the neighbor or maintaining the existing set to ensure both the packing and isolation properties hold.
title: Existence of Packing Isolating Sets in Trees

description: For any ε > 0, there exists a Δ₀ such that for all Δ ≥ Δ₀, any 3-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (girth ≥ 5) on n vertices with maximum degree at most Δ contains an independent set of size at least (1 - ε) * n * sqrt(log(Δ) / (2Δ)). This is the k=3 instantiation of the paper's main theorem that uncrowded hypergraphs attain the shattering threshold constant (1/(k-1))^(1/(k-1)).
proof_strategy: Formalize the definitions of k-uniform hypergraphs, girth, and independence number. Instantiate the probabilistic or algorithmic method used in the paper for k=3, carefully bounding the expected size of the independent set generated by the distributed/sequential algorithm and showing it meets the (1-ε) factor of the shattering threshold.
title: Shattering Threshold for 3-Uniform Uncrowded Hypergraphs

description: For any integer n > 2, the zero-sum constant s_1(n) equals 2n + 1, where s_1(n) is defined as the least positive integer k such that any sequence of k integers not divisible by n contains an n-subset whose sum is divisible by n but not by n^2.
proof_strategy: Formalize the definition of s_1(n) as the minimal k satisfying the subset sum divisibility condition. Prove the lower bound s_1(n) >= 2n+1 by exhibiting a specific sequence of 2n integers (e.g., n-1 copies of 1 and n-1 copies of -1) that lacks the required property. Prove the upper bound s_1(n) <= 2n+1 by showing that any sequence of 2n+1 integers not divisible by n must contain an n-subset with a sum having p-adic valuation exactly 1 for at least one prime p dividing n, leveraging extensions of the Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem or Chevalley-Warning type arguments.
title: Exact Formula for Zero-Sum Invariant s_1(n)

catalog_references: Universal probability bounds for partial Latin squares
description: For any partial Latin square P of order n with k entries occupying at most n/4 rows and n/4 columns, the probability that a uniformly random Latin square of order n contains P is bounded between (c₁/n)^k and (c₂/n)^k for some absolute constants c₁, c₂ > 0. This is a specific instance of the paper's main theorem (Theorem 1.1) with α=1/4 and β=1/4, which satisfies the condition 2α+β < 1.
proof_strategy: Define partial Latin squares and the uniform probability space of random Latin squares in Lean 4. Fix α = 1/4 and β = 1/4 in Theorem 1.1, which satisfies the required condition 2α + β < 1. Extract the absolute constants δ(1/4, 1/4) and Δ(1/4, 1/4) from the existential statement, and verify the bounds hold for all n ≥ 4.
title: Probability Bounds for Partial Latin Squares with Bounded Dimensions

description: The paper establishes an average-degree lower bound on the independence number of uncrowded uniform hypergraphs (those without Berge 2, 3, or 4-cycles). Since Verstraete and Wilson previously extended the maximum-degree bound from uncrowded to locally sparse hypergraphs (those without Berge 2 or 3-cycles), this conjecture proposes that the average-degree bound similarly extends to the broader class of locally sparse uniform hypergraphs.
proof_strategy: Adapt the trace nibble method and cleaning procedure from the paper to eliminate the dependency on the absence of Berge 4-cycles. This might involve a refined degree profile analysis or a modified cleaning phase that can control lower-order degrees without relying on the C4 restriction.
title: Average-Degree Bound for Locally Sparse Uniform Hypergraphs

description: The feasibility version of the Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem with Moving Obstacles (MT-TSP-MO) is PSPACE-hard. Specifically, given a set of targets each moving along a straight line with constant rational velocity and having an associated time window, and a set of obstacles each moving along a straight line with constant rational velocity, determining whether there exists a continuous trajectory from a static depot that visits all targets within their time windows while avoiding all obstacles is PSPACE-hard. This holds even when the number of obstacles is polynomial in the number of targets. The conjecture bridges the known PSPACE-hardness of motion planning with moving obstacles (Reif 1979) and the NP-hardness of TSP variants with time windows, establishing that MT-TSP-MO inherits the hardest aspects of both subproblems.
proof_strategy: Reduce from a known PSPACE-hard problem (e.g., the mover problem or quantified Boolean formula satisfiability). Encode QBF variables as target-visiting order choices and QBF quantifier alternations as obstacle configurations that force specific visitation sequences. The key insight is that moving obstacles can encode adversarial choices corresponding to universal quantifiers, while the agent's path choices correspond to existential quantifiers. Construct polynomial-size instances where feasibility of the MT-TSP-MO tour corresponds exactly to the truth of the QBF formula, leveraging the continuous time dimension to simulate the game tree of alternating quantifiers.
title: PSPACE-Hardness of MT-TSP-MO Feasibility with Linearly Moving Obstacles

description: Every Zariski-dense geometrically finite thin subgroup Γ of an arithmetic lattice in SO(n,1) with positive critical exponent δ_Γ > 0 admits a uniform spectral gap over its congruence covers: there exists η = η(n, δ_Γ) > 0 such that for all square-free q ≥ 1, the Laplace–Beltrami operator on (Γ ∩ Γ₀(q))\ℍⁿ has no eigenvalues in ((n−1)²/4 − η, (n−1)²/4). This extends Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak (δ_Γ > 1/2, n = 2) and the present paper's result (δ_Γ ∈ (1/2, n−2] with cusps, n ≥ 3) to the full range δ_Γ > 0, and would imply that the affine sieve for Γ-orbits saturates at a finite level regardless of δ_Γ.
domain_bridges: Representation theory of semisimple Lie groups
proof_strategy: Extend the Bourgain–Gamburd–Sarnak expansion machinery to δ_Γ ≤ 1/2 by developing an effective counting theory for return trajectory subgroups without the δ_Γ > 1/2 condition that guarantees non-local integrability of the Patterson–Sullivan measure. The key obstacle is that for δ_Γ ≤ 1/2, the Bowen–Margulis–Sullivan measure on the frame bundle no longer controls the spectral projector near the base of the continuous spectrum. A potential approach replaces the δ_Γ > 1/2 condition with a combinatorial thickness criterion on the return trajectory subgroups, leveraging their Zariski density (established in the present paper) together with a refined L²-flattening lemma adapted to the small-critical-exponent regime.
title: Uniform Spectral Gap for Thin Subgroups at Arbitrary Critical Exponent

description: For every natural number k, the directed binary structure consisting of the strict order relation of any finite poset of width at most k has twin-width at most 2*k+1. Equivalently, every finite poset whose largest antichain has size at most k admits a contraction sequence in which every intermediate part has at most 2*k+1 red out-/in-neighborhood types induced by the strict order relation.
domain_bridges: bounded-width posets ↔ oriented graphs with bounded independence number
Dilworth chain decompositions ↔ twin-width contraction sequences
finite model theory monadic dependence ↔ structural graph parameters
proof_strategy: Use Dilworth's theorem to partition the finite poset into at most k chains. Construct a contraction sequence by repeatedly merging adjacent intervals inside the chains. At every stage, each contracted block is an interval in one chain. For any other chain, transitivity of the partial order implies that the set of blocks comparable to a fixed interval changes only at two boundary positions, so each block has at most two red-neighbor contributions per chain, plus a bounded contribution from its own chain. This should yield a uniform red-degree bound of 2*k+1. The Lean formalization would first define twin-width for finite binary relations via contraction trees/partitions, then formalize the interval-chain invariant and the red-degree estimate.
title: Linear twin-width bound for finite posets of bounded width

description: For the preferential attachment random multigraph with edge steps and parameter p ∈ (0,1), started from any fixed finite connected multigraph with positive total degree, the clique number has the same logarithmic growth exponent as in the one-loop initial condition: for every ε > 0, the probability that |log(ω(G_t))/log(t) - (1-p)/(2-p)| > ε tends to 0 as t tends to infinity.
domain_bridges: random graph process to finite multigraph formalization
multigraph simplification to SimpleGraph clique number
asymptotic probability convergence to real-analysis limits
proof_strategy: Couple the process started from an arbitrary fixed finite connected seed to the standard one-loop seed after a deterministic burn-in period, using preferential attachment urn estimates to show that seed-dependent degree offsets are negligible on the logarithmic scale. Prove matching high-probability lower and upper bounds of the form t^α/polylog(t) ≤ ω(G_t) ≤ t^α polylog(t), where α = (1-p)/(2-p), uniformly over fixed seeds. Then derive convergence in probability of log(ω(G_t))/log(t) to α.
title: Initial-condition universality of the clique-number exponent in preferential attachment with edge steps

catalog_references: ZMod and finite subsequence sums in Mathlib
Nat.Prime and integer divisibility in Mathlib
description: For every odd prime p, every sequence of 2p+1 integers none divisible by p contains a subsequence of exactly p terms whose sum is divisible by p but not divisible by p^2. Equivalently, the prime case of the paper's constant satisfies s_1(p) <= 2p+1; combined with the known lower bound this gives s_1(p)=t_1(p)=2p+1 for odd primes.
domain_bridges: Translate p-adic valuation exactly 1 into integer divisibility: p ∣ sum and not p^2 ∣ sum.
Model a length-(2p+1) sequence as Fin (2*p+1) -> Int and a p-term subsequence as a Finset with cardinality p.
Use EGZ-type zero-sum combinatorics over ZMod p, then refine the chosen zero-sum class modulo p^2.
proof_strategy: Start from the EGZ theorem over ZMod p to force many p-term subsequences with sum 0 mod p. Partition the input by residues modulo p and study the lifted sums modulo p^2. Show that if all p-term zero-sums modulo p lifted to 0 modulo p^2, then the multiset has an impossible rigidity: residue classes and first p-adic digits must satisfy incompatible affine constraints. A Lean proof would separate the finite combinatorial selection arguments from the arithmetic lifting lemma p ∣ S and p^2 ∣ S.
title: Sharp valuation-EGZ bound for odd primes

description: For every integer r ≥ 2 and every η > 0, there is a threshold d* such that every finite (r+1)-uniform hypergraph H with no Berge 2-cycle and no Berge 3-cycle, average degree d ≥ d*, and vertex set V satisfies α(H) ≥ (1 - η) * r^(-1/r) * (log d / d)^(1/r) * |V|. This conjectures that the paper's average-degree result for uncrowded hypergraphs remains true under the weaker local-sparsity condition, removing the assumption of no Berge 4-cycles.
domain_bridges: hypergraph extremal theory to finite set systems in Lean
asymptotic average-degree bounds to quantified real inequalities
probabilistic nibble arguments to finite combinatorial existence theorems
proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's cleaning-plus-trace-nibble framework, but replace the use of Berge-4-cycle exclusion by a locally sparse codegree/triangle control lemma. First clean high r-degrees while preserving a positive fraction of vertices and the average-degree scale. Then run the trace nibble tracking all induced lower-layer maximum degrees. Prove that the binomial-type recurrence for the degree profile is unaffected, up to o(1), by the possible presence of Berge 4-cycles. The final accumulated selected set is independent and has the same leading constant r^(-1/r).
title: Average-degree Shearer bound for locally sparse uniform hypergraphs

description: For every nonzero ideal I of the Gaussian integers ℤ[i], the rank-2 Euclidean lattice obtained by applying the canonical embedding a+bi ↦ (a,b) to I is well-rounded: its shortest nonzero vectors span ℝ². Equivalently, if I = (α), then the shortest vectors are precisely the unit multiples ±α and ±iα under the embedding, giving two linearly independent equal-length minimal vectors.
domain_bridges: canonical embedding of number-field ideals as Euclidean lattices
well-rounded lattices from algebraic integer ideals
multiplicative norm in ℤ[i] versus Euclidean vector norm
proof_strategy: Use that Gaussian integers form a Euclidean domain, hence every nonzero ideal is principal, say I = (α). Under the canonical embedding ℤ[i] → ℝ², multiplication by α is a rotation-scaling similarity of the square lattice ℤ². For any nonzero β ∈ ℤ[i], the squared Euclidean norm of αβ is normSq(α) * normSq(β), and normSq(β) ≥ 1, with equality exactly for the units ±1, ±i. Therefore the minimal vectors of the embedded ideal are the images of ±α and ±iα. The vectors α and iα are orthogonal and nonzero, hence span ℝ², proving well-roundedness.
title: Nonzero Gaussian integer ideal lattices are well-rounded

catalog_references: Mohammadi-Oh and Oh-Winter uniform exponential mixing for thin groups
Selberg lemma: finitely generated linear groups have torsion-free finite-index subgroups
description: Conjecture: Let n >= 3 and let Γ be a geometrically finite, discrete, Zariski-dense thin subgroup of an arithmetic lattice Γ0 < SO(n,1)^∘ with critical exponent δ_Γ > 1/2. The uniform congruence spectral gap theorem for the congruence covers of Γ\H^n remains true without assuming that Γ is torsion-free. Equivalently, after excluding finitely many primes, there is ε > 0 such that every square-free congruence cover has no new complementary-series spectrum with parameter in (δ_Γ - ε, δ_Γ). This is falsifiable by producing a geometrically finite arithmetic thin orbifold subgroup with δ_Γ > 1/2 whose congruence covers have new spectrum accumulating at δ_Γ.
domain_bridges: geometrically finite hyperbolic orbifolds ↔ finite-index torsion-free manifold covers
critical exponent invariance ↔ finite-index subgroup growth equivalence
uniform spectral gap ↔ uniform exponential mixing of frame flow
thin arithmetic groups ↔ congruence expansion and superstrong approximation
proof_strategy: Use Selberg's lemma to choose a torsion-free finite-index normal subgroup Γ' ≤ Γ. Geometric finiteness, Zariski density, arithmetic containment, thinness, and the critical exponent condition δ_{Γ'} = δ_Γ are preserved under finite index. Apply the torsion-free theorem of the paper to Γ'. Compare congruence covers of Γ and Γ' after enlarging the finite set of excluded primes; the Γ-orbifold spectrum embeds as the finite deck-invariant part of the Γ'-manifold spectrum. Therefore any sequence of new complementary-series eigenvalues for Γ accumulating at δ_Γ would give such a sequence for Γ', contradicting the theorem for Γ'.
title: Orbifold version of the uniform congruence spectral gap for geometrically finite thin subgroups of SO(n,1)

description: Let K = 𝔽_{p^n} with p odd, regarded as an 𝔽_p-vector space, and let W ≤ K be an 𝔽_p-linear subspace of dimension e. Write its subspace polynomial as P_W(X) = ∏_{w ∈ W} (X - w) = ∑_{i=0}^e c_i X^{p^i}. Define the reversed Frobenius-twisted linearized polynomial F_W(X) = ∑_{i=0}^e c_i^{p^{-i}} X^{p^{e-i}}, where p^{-i} denotes the inverse Frobenius power on K. Conjecture: the image of the 𝔽_p-linear map x ↦ F_W(x) is exactly the trace-orthogonal complement W^⊥ = { z ∈ K | Tr_{K/𝔽_p}(z w) = 0 for all w ∈ W }. This is a finite-field linear algebra statement underlying the paper’s adjoint-factorization construction and avoids formalizing algebraic curves.
domain_bridges: linearized polynomials ↔ finite-dimensional linear maps over ZMod p
subspace polynomials ↔ kernels of additive polynomial maps
field trace pairing ↔ adjoint linear maps
factorizations R + R* = F* ∘ aF ↔ radicals of quadratic forms controlling Artin-Schreier point counts
proof_strategy: Formalize P_W as the monic additive polynomial with root set W. Show that the map induced by P_W has kernel W. Identify F_W as a Frobenius shift of the trace-adjoint of P_W. Use the finite-dimensional identity range(T†) = ker(T)^⊥ for a linear map T with respect to the nondegenerate trace pairing. Since Frobenius powers are automorphisms preserving dimensions and compatible with the coefficient twist in F_W, conclude range(F_W) = W^⊥.
title: Image of the reversed subspace polynomial is the trace-orthogonal complement

description: For a positive integer n and a subgroup H of the automorphism group of the cyclic group C_n, the orbit Schur ring S(C_n,H) has an almost commutative Terwilliger algebra if and only if H is trivial, or n is a prime power and H is the full automorphism group, or n = p^a for an odd prime p and H has order p^(a-1). Equivalently, for non-prime-power n, only the trivial orbit Schur ring has this property.
domain_bridges: Schur rings over cyclic groups can be represented by orbit partitions under subgroups of Aut(C_n)
Aut(C_n) is equivalent to the unit group of ZMod n, turning the classification into arithmetic of units modulo n
Almost commutativity of the Terwilliger algebra is encoded as a predicate on the orbit Schur ring generated by H
proof_strategy: Formalize orbit Schur rings over ZMod n as partitions induced by subgroups of AddAut (ZMod n). Introduce an abstract predicate AlmostCommutativeOrbitTerwilliger for the Terwilliger algebra of such an orbit Schur ring. Prove the forward direction by showing that any nontrivial H satisfying almost commutativity forces n to be a prime power, then use the structure of Aut(C_{p^a}) ≃ (ZMod (p^a))ˣ to restrict H to either the full automorphism group or, for odd p, the unique subgroup of order p^(a-1). Prove the reverse direction by constructing the required orbit structure in each listed case and verifying Tanaka's almost-commutativity criterion.
title: Orbit Schur rings over finite cyclic groups with almost commutative Terwilliger algebra

catalog_references: Guo, Modular Heights of Unitary Shimura Varieties III, Introduction §1.1: incoherent Hermitian space and nearby coherent Hermitian space
description: Model the local invariant signs of an incoherent Hermitian space by a finite sign vector ε_v ∈ {±1} whose product over all relevant places is −1. The nearby coherent Hermitian space with respect to a distinguished archimedean place ι is obtained by flipping exactly the sign at ι. The conjecture states that this single flip changes the global product to +1. This formalizes, in a Lean-friendly finite-product abstraction, the parity mechanism behind the paper’s passage from an incoherent Hermitian space to the nearby coherent Hermitian space.
domain_bridges: CM Hermitian spaces -> finite sign invariants
local-global coherence obstruction -> product formula in a commutative monoid
unitary Shimura variety setup -> Lean formalization of finite parity data
proof_strategy: Abstract away the analytic and adelic geometry to the finite set of local sign invariants. Define the nearby sign vector by negating the distinguished component and leaving all others fixed. Use the Finset product identity showing that changing one factor to its negative multiplies the total product by −1. Since the incoherent product is −1, the nearby product is +1.
title: Parity of the nearby coherent Hermitian sign vector

catalog_references: Irwin-Solecki: Projective Fraïsse categories for continua
Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic: Ramsey property for Polish groups
description: Let 𝓕 be the projective Fraisse category associated with the dyadic solenoid's inverse limit construction. We conjecture that 𝓕 satisfies the approximate Ramsey property, which by the main theorem of 'Universal minimal flows of homeomorphism groups of continua' implies the homeomorphism group of the dyadic solenoid is extremely amenable.
proof_strategy: Prove the approximate Ramsey property for the dyadic solenoid's Fraisse category by showing that for any finite coloring of embeddings of finite structures, there exists a monochromatic substructure in the limit. This would involve analyzing the bonding maps' structure in the dyadic solenoid's construction.
title: The dyadic solenoid's Fraisse category has the approximate Ramsey property

description: Conjecture that for every integer k ≥ 3 and every rational ε > 0 there exist two k‑uniform hypergraphs F₁, F₂ such that the positive codegree Turán density γ⁺(F₁, F₂) is positive but satisfies γ⁺(F₁, F₂) < ε·min{γ⁺(F₁), γ⁺(F₂)}.
proof_strategy: Construct families probabilistically using entropy compression to make the pairwise positive codegree arbitrarily small while keeping individual densities bounded away from zero.
title: Arbitrarily small positive codegree Turán density for pairs of k-graphs

description: Conjecture that any pair of cross-intersecting families of k-subsets of [n] with diversity at least binomial(n-u-1, n-k-1) and total size exceeding (1-1/(k+1))*binomial(n,k) must be isomorphic to one of the known extremal constructions: either a full star pair, a product of a Hilton–Milner family with a star, or a maximal cross‑intersecting extension of such a pair.
proof_strategy: Use the S_{U,V}^{Q}-shift to iteratively transform the pair into a canonical form while preserving diversity, then classify the possible terminal configurations and show they match the proposed constructions.
title: Canonical structure of large cross-intersecting families

description: For a d-dimensional convex lattice polytope P, define S_0(P,t) to be its Ehrhart polynomial and define the r-fold summatory Ehrhart polynomial recursively by S_{r+1}(P,t)=sum_{i=0}^{t-1} S_r(P,i). Define the relative-interior analogue by S_0(P^circ,t)=E(P^circ,t) and S_{r+1}(P^circ,t)=sum_{i=1}^{t-1} S_r(P^circ,i). The conjecture is that for every integer r >= 0 and every positive integer t, the polynomial extensions satisfy S_r(P^circ,t)=(-1)^(d+r) S_r(P,r-t). The paper proves the case r=1; r=0 is classical Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity.
domain_bridges: Formal polynomial identities over Q in Lean 4
proof_strategy: Prove by induction on r. The base case r=0 is Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity. For the induction step, use the discrete-antiderivative characterization: S_{r+1}(P,x+1)-S_{r+1}(P,x)=S_r(P,x) and S_{r+1}(P,0)=0. Similarly, the interior summatory polynomial vanishes at t=1 and has forward difference S_r(P^circ,t). Substitute the induction hypothesis S_r(P^circ,t)=(-1)^(d+r) S_r(P,r-t), then verify that the polynomial (-1)^(d+r+1) S_{r+1}(P,r+1-t) has the same forward difference and same initial value as S_{r+1}(P^circ,t). Polynomial extensionality over Q then gives the identity.
title: Iterated summatory Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity

description: Conjecture: Let 𝔽 be a field of characteristic p>0, λ∈𝔽, and (𝔤,[−,−],R,λ) a restricted Rota-Baxter Lie algebra over 𝔽. Then there exists a restricted Rota-Baxter associative algebra (A,R_A,λ) over 𝔽 such that 𝔤 is isomorphic to a Lie subalgebra of the commutator Lie algebra A^− and the restriction of R_A to 𝔤 equals R.
proof_strategy: Use the PBW theorem for restricted Lie algebras to embed 𝔤 into its restricted enveloping algebra u(𝔤), which is an associative algebra. Define a Rota-Baxter operator on u(𝔤) by extending R via the splitting property and verifying the axioms of weight λ. Show that u(𝔤) equipped with this operator becomes a restricted Rota-Baxter associative algebra. Finally, consider the commutator Lie algebra u(𝔤)^−; the canonical embedding of 𝔤 into u(𝔤) induces an embedding into u(𝔤)^− preserving the Rota-Baxter structure.
title: Embedding of restricted Rota-Baxter Lie algebras into commutator Lie algebras of restricted Rota-Baxter associative algebras

catalog_references: JLY, 'On the Zarankiewicz problem for affine plane configurations', J Math.Schweizeracz., 2015.'

title: Explicit bounds on Turán numbers for structured graph families

proof_strategy: Attempt a proof by induction on separator systems and use Sageev–Roller duality to show uniqueness; if a counterexample is found, construct a minimal graph violating the equality.
title: Median-width equals clique number for all graphs

description: Conjecture: A finite partial cube G is a daisy cube if and only if it does not contain, as a pc-minor, any graph H_{r,s} obtained from the Cartesian product of r copies of the 3-vertex path P_3 with a hypercube Q_s by deleting two opposite corners, for any integers r ≥ 2 and s ≥ 1. Equivalently, G has all peripheral Theta-classes iff it admits no such pc-minor obstruction. This statement is falsifiable for finite instances by exhaustive search of pc-minors and can be expressed in Lean as a theorem with a sorry placeholder.
proof_strategy: Prove the forward direction by showing that any non-peripheral Theta-class yields a pc-minor isomorphic to some H_{r,s}; prove the backward direction by assuming no such pc-minor exists and deducing that all Theta-classes must be peripheral, using the half-space orientation argument from the paper. The proof would combine structural pc-minor theory with combinatorial analysis of Theta-coordinates.
title: Characterizationof Daisy Cubes via Peripheral Theta-Classes and Forbidden pc-Minors

description: An interval hypergraphic polytope Δ_I is simple if and only if no point of [n] is contained in three or more hyperedges of I.
proof_strategy: Use the known characterization of simplicity of hypergraphic polytopes via acyclic orientations and the fact that interval hypergraphs satisfy the Helly property; show that a vertex fails to be simple exactly when there exists a point covered by ≥3 hyperedges, which creates a non-simple vertex in the Minkowski sum.
title: Simplicity criterion for interval hypergraphic polytopes via point multiplicity

description: The coefficients a_n in the q-expansion f(q) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n q^n satisfy the recurrence (n+3) a_{n+3} = (3n+4) a_{n+2} - (3n+1) a_{n+1} + n a_n for all n ≥ 0, with initial values a_0 = 1, a_1 = 0, a_2 = 1.
proof_strategy: Use the vector-valued Rankin-Cohen bracket of the completed mock theta series f̂ and its shadow ψ_f, apply the holomorphic projection operator to obtain a modular form of weight 2. Expand both sides as q-series, compare coefficients, and deduce the recurrence. The vanishing of certain vector-valued cusp form spaces ensures the projected form is a linear combination of Eisenstein series, whose coefficients are explicit.
title: Linear recurrence for coefficients of Ramanujan's third order mock theta function f(q)

description: The conjecture asserts that the ratio of determinant to cofactor simplifies to a combination of trace terms and Laplacian contributions, verified for arbitrary subsets S.
proof_strategy: Formal algebraic verification
title: Equality of Resistance Ratios

description: Let B and S be subsets of the nonnegative integers such that B+S = N0 (additive complements). Define A = {2^b : b ∈ B} and M = {∑_{d∈D} 2^d : D ⊆ S, D finite and nonempty}. Then the restricted partition function p(n,A,M) has polynomial growth (i.e., ∃ C,k∈N, ∀ n≥1, p(n,A,M) ≤ C·n^k) if and only if there exists a constant C>0 such that for all sufficiently large x, |B∩[0,x]|·|S∩[0,x]| ≤ C·x.
proof_strategy: The 'if' direction is the main theorem of the paper. For the 'only if' direction, assume p has polynomial growth and use the injective map from representations to pairs (s,b) with s+b ≤ log₂ n, as in the paper's proof of polynomial growth. This yields a bound on the number of such pairs, which implies B(N)S(N) = O(N).
title: Necessity of the counting condition for polynomial growth in restricted partition functions via powers of two

description: For every odd prime base B > 5, the length of the longest terminal cycle in the four-digit Kaprekar routine equals (B-1)/2 if and only if the multiplicative order of 2 modulo B is (B-1)/2.
proof_strategy: Formalize the convergence to the triangular region T_B, then analyze the projective doubling conjugacy to derive cycle lengths using Lean's arithmetic and group theory capabilities.
title: Terminal Cycle Length in Four-Digit Kaprekar Dynamics Equals (B-1)/2 for Prime Bases

catalog_references: Tree-independence number of K_{1,d}-free graph classes
Hajebi--Spirkl characterization of finite forbidden induced-subgraph classes with bounded tree-independence number
description: For every integer d >= 1 and every finite planar graph H, there exists a natural number B(d,H) such that every finite simple graph G that is K_{1,d}-free and has no induced minor isomorphic to H satisfies alpha-tw(G) <= B(d,H). A counterexample would be an infinite family of K_{1,d}-free graphs excluding H as an induced minor whose tree-independence numbers are unbounded.
domain_bridges: tree-independence number and tree decompositions with bounded independence in bags
induced minors and induced-subgraph preservation under deletions and contractions
star-free graphs and bounded local neighborhood independence
planar excluded induced minors and structural decomposition obstructions
proof_strategy: Formalize finite simple graphs, induced minors, K_{1,d}-freeness, planarity, and tree-independence number in Lean. Prove auxiliary lemmas showing that unbounded tree-independence in a K_{1,d}-free induced-minor-closed class forces arbitrarily large planar induced-minor obstructions. Then use induction on the size or block structure of the excluded planar graph H to extract a uniform bound B(d,H).
title: Bounded tree-independence for K_{1,d}-free graphs excluding a planar induced minor

description: Conjecture that for any integers r≥2 and any collection of r pairwise non‑isomorphic Shimura curves, any sequence of CM points with a common CM field and two distinct primes splitting in each field, if the points are strict (no proper special subvariety contains infinitely many of them), then the Galois orbits of the sequence become equidistributed in the product with respect to the Haar measure as the discriminants tend to infinity.
proof_strategy: Apply the adelic toral‑packet equidistribution theorem of Aka–Luethi–Michel–Wieser to the product space, show that the only positive‑dimensional special subvarieties are CM‑fibers, and deduce weak convergence of Galois orbit measures to Haar measure; the argument is unconditional under the given splitting hypothesis.
title: Equidistribution of Galois orbits of CM points on products of non‑isomorphic Shimura curves

description: Conjecture that for any oriented matroid, the e-embracing exchange distance between two e-embracing bases equals the graph distance between their corresponding e-positive fundamental circuits in the oriented matroid polyhedron P_{M^*,e}. This would strengthen Theorem 1.3 which only proves inequality and equality for uniform oriented matroids.
proof_strategy: Investigate the structure of the map from e-embracing bases to e-positive circuits. Use the fact that the map is r-Lipschitz and non-contractive. Attempt to show that any path in the polyhedron graph can be lifted to a path of embracing bases of the same length. Consider using topological methods or shellability arguments.
title: Equality of Embracing Exchange Distance and Polyhedral Graph Distance

description: For a tree graph Γ, the Fitting ideal I_Γ is a complete intersection ideal in the polynomial ring k[x_1,...,x_n].
proof_strategy: Construct explicit Koszul resolutions for tree graphs and verify monomial complete intersection property via Lean 4's algebraic tools
title: Complete intersectionproperty of Fitting ideals for tree graphs

description: For every positive integer q and natural number n, let P(n,q) denote the probability that the Random player wins the q-game. We conjecture that P(n,q) satisfies the recurrence relation: P(n,q) = 1/n + (1/n) * Σ_{k=q+1}^n P(n−k, q), with base case P(0,q) = 0. This recurrence captures the probabilistic structure of the game coupled to random permutations' cycle decompositions.
proof_strategy: Formalize the recurrence relation in Lean using the coupling between the game and permutation cycles. Prove the recurrence by induction on n, using the uniformity of the first cycle length and the recursive structure of permutations.
title: Recurrence for the Winning Probability in the Generalized Game

description: We conjecture that the exponential growth rate γ of unlabelled cubic planar graphs is equal to the reciprocal of the radius of convergence of their ordinary generating function G(z), and that the number of such graphs on n vertices satisfies an asymptotic formula of the form C · γ^n · n^(-5/2) for some computable constant C > 0. This conjecture arises from the interplay between generating series analysis and probabilistic symmetry considerations outlined in the paper.
proof_strategy: Establish the ordinary generating function G(z) via structural decompositions, apply singularity analysis to identify the dominant singularity at z = 1/γ, and use probabilistic local limit theorems to control the influence of small symmetric subgraphs on the asymptotic enumeration.
title: Asymptotic Growth Constant for Unlabelled Cubic Planar Graphs

description: To formalize the concept of graph linear notation as a complete graph invariant in Lean 4, we propose defining it as the maximum binary encoding of adjacency matrices across all vertex orderings. This encoding uniquely represents a graph up to isomorphism by capturing its structure through lexicographic maximization.
proof_strategy: Construct a Lean 4 type for graphs, define adjacency matrix encoding, and implement an algorithm to compute the lexicographically maximal encoding under all permutations of vertex labels. Verify invariance under automorphisms and isomorphism checks via encoding comparison.
title: Formalizing Graph Linear Notation in Lean 4

description: Let B_n be the Birkhoff polytope, the convex hull in R^(n x n) of all n x n permutation matrices. Conjecture: B_n satisfies the clique-face property, meaning every clique in the 1-skeleton of B_n is exactly the vertex set of a face, if and only if n <= 2.
domain_bridges: permutation matrices to vertices of transportation polytopes
polytope skeletons to Cayley-type graphs on symmetric groups
clique-face obstructions to quadratic generation of toric ideals
proof_strategy: For n <= 2, B_n is respectively a point or a segment, so the clique-face property is immediate. For n = 3, two permutation vertices are adjacent exactly when their quotient permutation has a single nontrivial cycle; every nonidentity element of S_3 has this property, so the 1-skeleton of B_3 is complete on six vertices. However B_3 is 4-dimensional and its facets are given by equations x_ij = 0, each containing only four permutation vertices, so a five-vertex clique is not the vertex set of any face. Thus B_3 fails the property. For n >= 3, B_n contains a face isomorphic to B_3 by fixing n-3 rows and columns to the corresponding identity entries. Since the clique-face property passes to faces, B_n also fails it.
title: Birkhoff polytopes have the clique-face property only in dimensions n <= 2

description: For any odd base B > 3, the length of the longest nonconstant terminal cycle of the Kaprekar map is at most (B-1)/2. Furthermore, this upper bound is achieved if and only if B is prime and the multiplicative order of 2 modulo B equals (B-1)/2.
proof_strategy: Show the Kaprekar map on the triangular region is conjugate to doubling, then analyze cycle lengths via properties of 2 modulo B. For equality, establish that B must be prime and 2^{(B-1)/2} ≡ -1 mod B.
title: Maximum Cycle Length in Kaprekar Maps for Odd Bases

description: If a projective Fraisse category associated with a continuum F has the approximate Ramsey property, then there exists a ultrafilter on the Fraisse category that witnesses extreme amenability of Homeo(F) by satisfying partition relations for all finite graphs.
proof_strategy: Construct a ultrafilter in the Fraisse category that uniformly satisfies the conditions required for extreme amenability, leveraging the approximate Ramsey property to enforce uniformity across all finite graphs.
title: Existence of an ultrafilter witness for extreme amenability

description: Conjecture that the Ω(r^-3) lower bound achieved in the paper is optimal up to constants, specifically that there exists a universal constant c > 0 such that for every r ≥ 2 and n ≥ 4r^2, any n-vertex r-graph where every (r+1)-set spans exactly 0 or 2 edges has at most c·r^-3·(n choose r) edges. This would prove that the polynomial improvement from 2^(1-r) to r^-3 is tight in terms of the r-dependence, establishing the true order of magnitude for this extremal problem.
proof_strategy: Approach via entropy-compression or hypergraph container methods to establish upper bounds matching the r^-3 scaling. The strategy would involve analyzing the local structure constraints imposed by requiring every (r+1)-set to span exactly 0 or 2 edges, then applying double-counting with refined Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities. Alternatively, develop a geometric stability argument showing that constructions achieving higher densities must converge to specific algebraic or geometric templates, and prove these templates cannot exceed the r^-3 bound.
title: Optimality of the r^-3 density bound for (r+1)-sets spanning 0 or 2 edges

catalog_references: Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic Ramsey property for Polish groups
description: We conjecture that the projective Fraisse category of finite linear orders with the standard morphisms does NOT have the approximate Ramsey property, implying that its automorphism group (the infinite symmetric group) is NOT extremely amenable. This provides a concrete, falsifiable target for formalization in Lean 4, leveraging known results about the infinite symmetric group.
proof_strategy: Construct a counterexample structure in the category of finite linear orders that violates the approximate Ramsey condition, leveraging the non-amenability of the infinite symmetric group. Use Lean's finite set libraries to formalize the category and the combinatorial properties.
title: Approximate Ramsey Property for Finite Linear Orders Implies Extreme Amenability

description: For every finite K5-free simple graph G on n vertices, assign weight 1/2 to every edge contained in a triangle and weight 1 to every other edge. Then G has a bipartition whose monochromatic edge-weight is at most n^2/16. Equivalently, deleting edges of total such weight at most n^2/16 always makes G bipartite. The balanced complete 4-partite graph shows that the constant 1/16 would be best possible.
domain_bridges: Translates a Ramsey-Turan style forbidden-clique problem into a weighted max-cut inequality.
Extends the paper's weighted K4-free triangle-discounted cut result to the next clique size K5.
Connects Sudakov-type bipartization bounds with edge weights determined by local clique membership.
proof_strategy: A plausible route is to combine a weighted Turan symmetrization argument with a stability analysis for near-extremal K5-free graphs. First show that an extremal counterexample may be assumed to have a bounded number of vertex types under weighted twin-symmetrization. Then reduce the resulting finite weighted optimization problem to complete multipartite templates plus sparse exceptional triangle-free structure. The complete 4-partite template gives the extremal value n^2/16, while triangle-free exceptional parts should be controlled by known max-cut lower bounds for triangle-free graphs.
title: Weighted K5-free max-cut conjecture with triangle-discounted edges

description: For every integer d ≥ 10 there exist at least two pairwise non‑isomorphic line arrangements A and A' in ℓ² such that they have the same intersection lattice L(A) ≈ L(A'), the same minimal degree of a Jacobian relation mdr(A) = mdr(A'), and the same Hilbert function of their Milnor algebras M(A) and M(A'). Moreover, the minimal graded free resolutions of M(A) and M(A') are not isomorphic, so (A, A') is a Ziegler pair that does not satisfy condition (SPEC) (i.e., it is not a constant‑lattice specialization). The number of such inequivalent pairs is expected to grow without bound as d increases, indicating an abundance of non‑special Ziegler pairs beyond the known examples for d = 9 and d = 10.
proof_strategy:
The conjecture can be approached by a systematic computational search for each degree d ≥ 10.  
1. **Enumerate intersection lattices**: For a fixed d, list all combinatorial types of reduced line arrangements (i.e., all possible multisets of multiplicities at ordinary double points) that give rise to a lattice L.  
2. **Parameterise line arrangements**: For each lattice, set up a system of linear equations for the coefficients of the linear forms λ_i (up to scaling) that realize the required intersection multiplicities.  
3. **Compute invariant data**: Using a computer algebra system (e.g., Macaulay2, Singular) compute the Jacobian ideal J_f, the Milnor algebra M(f)=S/J_f, the module AR(f) of logarithmic derivations, the degree sequence (exponents), the minimal degree mdr, and the Hilbert function of M(f).  
4. **Filter by the conjecture’s conditions**: Keep pairs (A, A') with identical L, identical mdr, and identical Hilbert function.  
5. **Compare resolutions**: Compute the minimal
title: Abundance of non‑special Ziegler pairs for all degrees ≥ 10

description: Conjecture that for every integer k≥3 there exist two k-uniform hypergraphs F1 and F2 such that 0<γ⁺(F1,F2)<½·min{γ⁺(F1),γ⁺(F2)}.
proof_strategy: Use probabilistic constructions to produce families with a strictly bounded gap between γ⁺(F1,F2) and half the smaller of γ⁺(F1),γ⁺(F2); combine density increment and stability arguments.
title: Strong quantitative non-principality for positive codegree Turán density

description: For every finite-dimensional vector space E over a finite field F and every rank r with 0 <= r <= dim E, the map sending a sparse-paving q-matroid M of rank r on E to its set of r-dimensional circuit-hyperplanes is a bijection onto the stable sets of the q-Johnson graph J_q(E,r), whose vertices are r-dimensional subspaces and whose edges join pairs with intersection dimension r-1. Equivalently, a set S of r-subspaces defines a sparse-paving q-matroid precisely when any two distinct members of S intersect in dimension at most r-2.
domain_bridges: sparse-paving q-matroids to independent sets in the q-Johnson graph
finite vector-space submodule lattice to graph-theoretic stable sets
proof_strategy: Formalize q-matroids by rank functions on the submodule lattice satisfying the q-matroid rank axioms. Define paving and sparse-paving in terms of circuit dimensions and dual paving, or equivalently by the circuit-hyperplane characterization. Prove first that in any sparse-paving q-matroid, two distinct r-dimensional circuit-hyperplanes cannot meet in dimension r-1, since their sum would violate the sparse-paving circuit elimination/dual-paving condition. Conversely, given a stable set S of r-subspaces, define a rank function by declaring subspaces contained in members of S to have the expected ranks, declaring members of S to be dependent hyperplanes of rank r-1, and all other r-subspaces to be bases; then extend by truncation to all subspaces. Verify the rank axioms R1-R3 by splitting on dimensions below r, equal to r, and above r, using the stable-set intersection bound for the only nontrivial submodularity case. Show the two constructions are inverse.
title: Sparse-paving q-matroids are exactly stable sets in the q-Johnson graph

catalog_references: Frankl and Füredi (1984) – lower bound 2^{1-r} for r‑graphs with 0/2 edges

description: For every integer r≥2 there exists a constant C>0 such that for all sufficiently large n the maximum number of edges in an n‑vertex r‑uniform hypergraph in which each (r+1)-set spans exactly 0 or 2 edges is at least C·n^r / r³, and no such hypergraph can have more than C'·n^r / r² edges. Equivalently, the Turán density π(H^r_3)=Θ(1/r³).
proof_strategy: Use a probabilistic construction placing n points uniformly on the unit sphere S^{r-2} and declaring an r‑set an edge iff its convex hull contains the origin; analyze the probability that a random (r+1)-set spans 0 or 2 edges, then apply entropy compression or hypergraph container methods to show any such hypergraph cannot exceed O(n^r / r²) edges, yielding the Θ(1/r³) density conjecture.
title: Conjecture: Turán density of the 3‑edge r‑graph is Θ(1/r³)

description: Formalize the structural characterization of large cross-intersecting families (F, G) where F ⊆ {[n] choose k} and G ⊆ {[n] choose l}. Specifically, prove that for n sufficiently large relative to k and l, if the diversity γ(F) + γ(G) exceeds a specific threshold, then the pair (F, G) must be contained in a specific class of maximal cross-intersecting extensions derived from the S_{U,V}^{Q}-shift operation, extending the Kupavskii-Zakharov stability framework to the cross-intersecting setting.
proof_strategy: Implement the S_{U,V}^{Q}-shift as a function on families of sets that preserves the cross-intersecting property (∀ A ∈ F, B ∈ G, A ∩ B ≠ ∅). Use an induction on the diversity γ(F) + γ(G) to show that the shift reduces the diversity while preserving the family size until the family reaches a canonical structure. Finally, prove that the resulting stable structure matches the predicted extremal families.
title: Cross-Intersecting Stability via Diversity and S_{U,V}^{Q}-Shifting

description: In the context of projective Fraisse categories for continua, we conjecture that the pseudo-arc's category has the approximate Ramsey property, thereby implying its homeomorphism group is extremely amenable. This connects the combinatorial structure of the category to the dynamical property of the group via the framework established in the paper.
proof_strategy: Leverage the known extreme amenability of the pseudo-arc's homeomorphism group. Construct the projective Fraisse category for the pseudo-arc, then demonstrate the approximate Ramsey property by showing that for any finite coloring of substructures, there exists a monochromatic extension in the category. This would mirror the paper's equivalence while focusing on a canonical example of extreme amenability.
title: Approximate Ramsey Property for the Pseudo-Arc's Projective Fraisse Category

description: We conjecture that the approximate Ramsey property of a projective Fraïssé category implies that the dense image of its automorphism group in a homeomorphism group of a continuum is extremely amenable. This establishes a formal link between combinatorial Ramsey-theoretic properties and topological amenability in the study of homeomorphism groups of continua.
proof_strategy: We will proceed by embedding the combinatorial structure of the Fraïssé limit into a topological dynamics framework, translating Ramsey-theoretic conditions into constraints on the amenability of the group action. This will involve leveraging existing characterizations of extreme amenability in non-archimedean Polish groups and extending them to the topological group of homeomorphisms of a continuum, using the projective Fraïssé structure to induce a suitable Ramsey-like property.
title: Ramsey Theory in Projective Fraïssé Limits Implies Extreme Amenability of Homeomorphism Groups of Continua

description: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a projective Fraisse category and $\mathbb{F}$ be its projective Fraisse limit. Let $G$ be a closed subgroup of $\text{Homeo}(F)$ (where $F = \mathbb{F}/R^{\mathbb{F}}$) such that $\text{Aut}(\mathbb{F})$ is dense in $G$. We conjecture that $G$ is extremely amenable if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the approximate Ramsey property. This formalization requires encoding the approximate Ramsey property as a combinatorial property of the category and the extreme amenability as a fixed-point property for continuous actions on compact spaces.
domain_bridges: Combinatorial Ramsey Theory to Fixed Point Theory
proof_strategy: The proof involves establishing a bridge between the 'Approximate Ramsey Property' (a condition on the existence of monochromatic sub-objects in finite structures) and the 'Fixed Point on Compacta' property. The strategy is to lift the action of $G$ on a compact space $X$ to an action of $\text{Aut}(\mathbb{F})$, then use the Ramsey property to construct a sequence of approximate fixed points that converge to a global fixed point via the compactness of $X$.
title: Characterization of Extreme Amenability for Homeomorphism Groups of Projective Fraisse Limits

description: For every integer d ≥ 9, there exist two line arrangements of d lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, identical Hilbert functions of their Milnor algebras, identical minimal degree of a Jacobian relation, but distinct graded Betti numbers of the minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras (i.e., a Ziegler pair satisfying conditions (HF) and (MDR)).
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families of line arrangements using degenerations of known Ziegler pairs (e.g., the classical d=9 example) by adding generic lines through points of high multiplicity, preserving intersection lattice and Hilbert function while altering syzygy modules via controlled deformation; alternatively, use computer-assisted search to produce examples for each d and then prove stability under deformation.
title: Existence of Ziegler pairs for all degrees at least nine

description: For prime bases p>5, the paper reduces the longest terminal cycle length of the four-digit Kaprekar map to the least positive m such that 2^m ≡ ±1 mod p. Conjecture: there are infinitely many primes p>5 for which this least m is exactly (p-1)/2, equivalently the Kaprekar map in base p has a terminal cycle attaining the universal upper bound (p-1)/2.
domain_bridges: Kaprekar terminal cycles ↔ projective doubling on P^1(Z/(B-1))
Prime-base projective doubling ↔ multiplicative order of 2 modulo p
Maximal Kaprekar cycle length ↔ weak Artin-type infinitude for powers of 2
proof_strategy: Formalize the paper's odd-base reduction and terminal-cycle length formula in Lean. For prime p, prove equivalence between maximal Kaprekar cycle length and the stated modular-order condition. A conditional proof follows from Artin's primitive-root conjecture for base 2, since primitive-root primes have 2^((p-1)/2) ≡ -1 mod p. An unconditional proof would require new analytic number theory.
title: Infinitely many prime bases with maximal four-digit Kaprekar cycles

description: We conjecture that for any odd prime power q, and any non-zero constant c in the finite field F_q, the polynomial f_c(x) = c x^{q-1} + t ∈ F_q(t)[x] has arboreal Galois image equal to the full iterated wreath product of the cyclic group C_{q-1} at every level n ≥ 1. This asserts that the Galois groups G_n ≃ (C_{q-1} ≀)^n for all n, generalizing the explicit families established in the paper to all non-zero c ∈ F_q^*.
proof_strategy: Leverage the connection between the twisted Carlitz module's torsion structure and the arboreal tower, combined with induction on the iteration level using properties of cyclic wreath products and primitive prime divisors in positive characteristic.
title: Arboreal Maximality for Twisted Carlitz Polynomials over Function Fields

catalog_references: Thang Pang Ern and Malcolm Tan Jun Xi, "On the asymptotic density of the ordered pairs $(a,b)$ of positive integers such that $\gcd(ab,a+b)=\gcd(a,b)$", arXiv:2025.xxxxx [math.NT].
description:
Conjecture that the number of ordered pairs $(a,b)$ of positive integers with $a,b\le x$ and $\gcd(ab,a+b)=\gcd(a,b)$ satisfies
$$\sum_{\substack{a,b\le x \ \gcd(ab,a+b)=\gcd(a,b)}} 1 = C\,x^{2}+O\bigl(x(\log x)^{3}\bigr),$$
where $C=\displaystyle\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{2}(p+1)}\right)\approx 0.881513$ is the quadratic class number constant.
proof_strategy: Apply Dirichlet series techniques to the generating function of $(\mu*h)(n)$ with $h(m)=\mathbf{1}_{m=1}$, control the error term via contour integration, and exploit the known bound $R_{\beta}(x)\ll x^{1+\beta}(\log x)^{2}$ for $0<\beta<1$ to sharpen the exponent from $4$ to $3$ in the logarithmic factor.
title: Improved error term for the density of pairs with $f(a,b)=1$

description: Let \(\mathcal S_1,\dots,\mathcal S_r\) be pairwise non‑isomorphic Shimura curves attached to quaternion algebras over \(\mathbb Q\) (or more generally to forms of \(\mathrm{PGL}_2\)). For each \(n\) let \(z_n=(z_{n,1},\dots,z_{n,r})\) be a CM point whose coordinates all have the same CM field \(E_n\). Assume the sequence \((z_n)_n\) is strict (its intersection with any proper special subvariety is finite). Then the Galois orbits \(\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)\cdot z_n\) become equidistributed in \(\mathcal S_1\times\dots\times\mathcal S_r\) with respect to the product of the natural hyperbolic probability measures, **without any hypothesis that two fixed primes split in each \(E_n\)**. This conjecture extends Theorem 1 of the cited paper by removing the Linnik‑type splitting condition, thereby providing an unconditional equidistribution statement for arbitrary sequences of CM points on such products.
proof_strategy: Combine the adelic toral‑packet equidistribution theorem of Aka–Lüethi–Michel–Wieser with a refined analysis of the splitting conditions: (1) Show that the Linnik‑type splitting hypothesis can be removed by exploiting the spectral gap for the action of the diagonal torus on \(\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb A)\) and establishing uniform polynomial decay of matrix coefficients independent of the discriminant. (2) Use the joining classification of Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss to prove that any non‑trivial joining would force a Hecke correspondence between two distinct Shimura curves, which is impossible by the non‑isomorphism hypothesis. (3) Apply an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem to produce, for each large discriminant, auxiliary primes that split with controlled norm, allowing a limiting argument that removes the need for a fixed pair of split primes. (4) Finally, invoke the equidistribution of toral packets for all discriminants, deducing that the empirical measures of Galois
title: Equidistribution of Galois orbits of CM points on products of non‑isomorphic Shimura curves without auxiliary splitting conditions

description: For all n ≥ 0, the number of (4,0)-colored Frobenius partitions of weight n equals twice the sum of Lin-Liu minimal excludants over all 4-partitions of n, i.e., ψ_{4,0}(n) = 2σ_{mex,4}(n). This conjecture extends the proven identities ψ_{2,0}(n) = 2σ_{mex,2}(n) and ψ_{2,1}(n) = 2σ_{mex,2}(n) - E_2(n) to the four-colored case.
domain_bridges: minimal excludant statistics to difference equations
proof_strategy: Establish a sign-reversing involution on (4,0)-colored Frobenius partitions that pairs each partition with a weight contribution of twice its minimal excludant value. The involution would cancel all but the mex-related contributions, generalizing the Andrews/Göllnitz-type bijections used in the two-colored case.
title: Generalized two-colored Frobenius identities to four-colored case

proof_strategy: algebraic_characterization_using_graph_subalgebra_and_p_map_properties
title: Conjecture on Idempotent Up to Scalar Property of Restricted Rota-Baxter Operators
