description: For all integers a,b,t with 3 < a ≤ b, b ≥ 6, and t ≥ b+1, the generalized Turán number satisfies ex(n,K_{a,b},K_{3,t}) = Θ(n^3). Equivalently, there exist positive constants c,C and N, depending only on a,b,t, such that for every n ≥ N, c n^3 ≤ ex(n,K_{a,b},K_{3,t}) ≤ C n^3. The paper proves this for t ≥ 2 max{3, ceil(b/2)}+1, which equals b+1 for even b ≥ 6 but is b+2 for odd b ≥ 7; the conjecture asserts that the necessary threshold b+1 is also sufficient in the odd case.
domain_bridges: Extremal graph theory ↔ finite-field incidence geometry
Complete bipartite subgraph counting ↔ controlled intersections of algebraic plane sections
Asymptotic combinatorics ↔ formalized finite graph enumeration
proof_strategy: The upper bound O(n^3) should follow from the standard counting argument for the regime 3<a≤b<t. The main task is the lower bound when b is odd and t=b+1. One possible route is to refine the finite-field point-hyperplane incidence construction from the paper so that every triple of vertices has fewer than b+1 common neighbors, while still producing Ω(q^9) copies of K_{a,b} on Θ(q^3) vertices. Geometrically, this amounts to replacing the paper's line-and-conic plane-section bound of b+1 in the odd case by a sharp bound of b, perhaps by deleting or perturbing one residue class of the explicit point set without destroying the abundance of coplanar b-subsets.
title: Necessary threshold for cubic generalized Turán growth against K_{3,t}

description: For any graph G, any two minimal median decompositions of G (i.e., median decompositions whose underlying median graph has the smallest possible number of vertices) are isomorphic via a graph isomorphism that respects the decomposition bags. This formalises the "uniquely minimal" claim in the paper and provides a concrete, falsifiable statement that can be encoded in Lean.
proof_strategy: Define a median decomposition as a structure (M, bag) where M is a median graph and bag : V(M) → set V(G) satisfying the usual covering, edge‑separation, and connectedness conditions. Show existence of a minimal decomposition by taking a decomposition with minimal |V(M)| (using well‑foundedness of nat). Prove that if D₁ and D₂ are minimal then there exists a bijection f : V(M₁) ≃ V(M₂) such that for every v ∈ V(M₁), bag₁ v = bag₂ (f v). The proof proceeds by: (1) constructing the Sageev dual median graph Σ(G, Σ) from the given separation system Σ of G; (2) showing any minimal median decomposition is isomorphic to the canonical Sageev construction (the "uniquely minimal" theorem in the paper); (3) using the universal property of the Sageev construction to build the required isomorphism. Lean implementation will reuse existing definitions of simple graphs, median graphs, and will formalise the universal property as a morphism of median graphs preserving bags.
title: Uniqueness of Minimal Median Decompositions for Graphs

catalog_references: Zagier, D. (2008). "Elliptic modular forms and their applications". In: *The 1‑2‑3 of Modular Forms*.
description: For every integer \(N\ge 2\) and every weight \(k\) admissible in the CHL construction, the series defining \(\widetilde{F}_k(\Omega)\) in equation (\ref{eq:tildeFCF123}) converges absolutely on the Siegel upper half‑space \(\IH_2\). Equivalently, each of the four component series \(\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2,\mathcal{F}_3,\mathcal{F}_4\) converges absolutely for all \(\Omega\in\IH_2\).
domain_bridges: Siegel modular forms ↔ Convergence of Poincaré series
proof_strategy: Show that each \(\mathcal{F}_i\) is a Poincaré‑type series over the congruence subgroup \(\Gamma_1(N)\) with a rapidly decaying seed. Use standard estimates for Kloosterman‑type sums and the exponential decay of the Gaussian‑type factors (the \(H\) functions) in the imaginary directions of \(\Omega\). Establish uniform bounds on the Fourier coefficients of the seed functions \(f_{\pm}, g_{\pm}\) (which are known to be of moderate growth) and apply the Rankin–Selberg method to bound the sum over \((a,b,c,d)\). For \(\mathcal{F}_4\), exploit the extra factor \(r\) and the product over \(n\) to obtain exponential decay in \(r\). Combine these estimates to prove absolute convergence for all \(\Omega\in\IH_2\).
title: Uniform Convergence of the Single‑Centered Black Hole Generating Function \(\widetilde{F}_k\) for All \(\mathbb{Z}_N\) CHL Models

description: Every minimal forbidden partial cube-minor for the class of daisy cubes is isomorphic to the graph obtained from P_3^□r □ Q_s by deleting exactly two vertices that are antipodal in the hypercube embedding, for some integers r ≥ 2 and s ≥ 1.
proof_strategy: Prove the conjecture by showing that any minimal forbidden pc-minor must contain a unique non-peripheral Θ-class, which forces the graph to decompose as a Cartesian product of a path power and a hypercube, followed by corner deletion. Use the characterization that daisy cubes are exactly those partial cubes where all Θ-classes are peripheral, combined with structural analysis of partial cubes with exactly one non-peripheral class.
title: Classification of Minimal Forbidden pc-Minors for Daisy Cubes

description: For the q-game on n elements, where the deterministic player removes q elements per turn and the random player wins iff the first cycle of length at most q in canonical order is a fixed point, the probability that the random player wins approaches 1/q as n tends to infinity for any fixed positive integer q.
proof_strategy: Use the coupling to permutation cycles established in the paper, analyze the distribution of the first cycle of length at most q in canonical order, and apply asymptotic analysis of cycle lengths in random permutations using known results about the limiting distribution of cycle counts and the fact that the probability a cycle of length ≤ q is a fixed point converges to 1/q as n → ∞.
title: Asymptotic probability of random player victory in q-games

description: This conjecture relates the modular height of a Shimura variety to the logarithmic derivative of its Hecke L-function, quantifying how arithmetic intersection data control the height structure via comparison with derivative estimates.
proof_strategy: Construct model where logarithmic derivatives control intersection data and derive height bounds via automorphic projections.
title: Modular heights of units and Shimura varieties over CM fields

description: Conjecture that for every positive integer n, the number of Dyck paths of semilength n that are black‑white balanced under the column‑alternating coloring equals the Narayana number N(n,⌊n/2⌋+1).
proof_strategy: Bijective proof using up‑step parity and the reflection principle, analogous to the chessboard case.
title: Column‑alternating balanced Dyck paths conjecture

description: Conjecture: For bounded-horizon MT-TSP-MO instances with piecewise Lipschitz target and obstacle trajectories, if near-optimal continuous trajectories can be chosen with positive uniform clearance from all moving obstacles, then the TPBS algorithm run on grids whose mesh size tends to zero returns feasible solutions whose costs converge to the true MT-TSP-MO optimum. This is falsifiable: a single instance satisfying the clearance-regularity assumptions for which TPBS either fails to return a feasible solution or returns only solutions with cost bounded away from optimality at arbitrarily fine grid resolutions would refute it.
domain_bridges: metric geometry and Lipschitz trajectory approximation
mixed-integer conic programming and collision-avoidance certificates
formal verification of robotics planning algorithms
proof_strategy: Define a clearance-regular MT-TSP-MO instance and a mesh norm for TPBS grids. Prove that any positive-clearance feasible trajectory can be uniformly approximated by a grid path using compactness and Lipschitz bounds. Show that the TPBS segment-feasibility oracle accepts the approximating grid edges, and that the upper-level search enumerates the corresponding target order and time-window path. Combine this with the inner-clearance assumption to obtain epsilon-optimal feasible solutions as the mesh size goes to zero. In Lean, formalize the metric-space approximation, finite-grid search, and option-valued TPBS return type.
title: Asymptotic completeness and near-optimality of TPBS for clearance-regular MT-TSP-MO instances

catalog_references: Exact 6-cut rigidity and small-order superconnectivity for the 6-regular case of Dirac's k=4 problem
description: Every 6-regular (4,1)-graph is super-6-edge-connected, i.e., every 6-edge-cut is the edge star of a single vertex. This extends Theorem B, which proves this only for graphs on at most 29 vertices, to all possible sizes. A counterexample would be a 6-regular (4,1)-graph containing a nontrivial 6-edge-cut (both shores have size ≥ 15 by Theorem B).
proof_strategy: Extend the cut-matrix classification (21 matrices, 5 types) and the boundary-shortfall lemma to shores of arbitrary size ≥ 15. Use the fact that any nontrivial 6-edge-cut in a 6-regular (4,1)-graph has shores inducing subgraphs with minimum degree ≥ 3 and specific coloring constraints (Theorem C: no shore is bipartite). Combine with the classification of 3-colorings of shores and the parity constraints from the cut edges to derive a contradiction, possibly by showing that the deficiency conditions force a critical edge or a 3-coloring of the whole graph.
title: Super-6-edge-connectivity of all 6-regular (4,1)-graphs

catalog_references: arXiv:On zero-sum problems of two new types
description: For all integers n>2, the minimal length k such that any sequence of k non-zero residues modulo n contains an n-element subsequence summing to 0 modulo n but not modulo n^2 equals 2n+1.
proof_strategy: Check small cases by exhaustive computation; attempt modular lifting arguments; seek counterexample for n=3.
title: Conjecture on s_1(n) for n>2

description: Let M(n) be the maximum, over all finite pairwise coprime sets A ⊆ {1,…,n−1}, of ∑_{a∈A} 1/(n−a). Conjecture: there is an absolute real constant C such that for every n ≥ 2, M(n) ≤ ∑_{p<n, p prime} 1/p + C. This is the pointwise uniform form of Erdős's question studied in the paper, strengthened from the paper's average-order and almost-all results to all n.
domain_bridges: pairwise-coprime finite set optimization ↔ prime reciprocal sums
analytic average-order estimates ↔ pointwise finite inequalities
proof_strategy: Formalize M(n) as a finite supremum over Finset ℕ. A plausible proof would refine the paper's bounded-cost dual certificate from an average estimate to a uniform certificate: assign admissible nonnegative weights to prime divisibility constraints so that every candidate a contributes at most 1/(n−a), while the total certificate cost is bounded by the prime harmonic sum plus an absolute constant. The main obstruction is controlling shifted-prime and rough-number clusters uniformly rather than on average.
title: Uniform Erdős Bound for the Shifted Pairwise-Coprime Extremal Function

description: Let S_N(x)=sum_{i=1}^N x^i. For primes p<q with pq | m and n^2 >= (p-1)(q-1)+1, the conjecture says the cyclotomic transfer P=S_{m^2}/Phi_{pq}, Q=S_{n^2} Phi_{pq} is a nonstandard square-sided pair of sizes m^2 and n^2. Equivalently, the quotient and product have nonnegative integer coefficients, P(1)=m^2, Q(1)=n^2, and P Q=S_{m^2}S_{n^2}. A counterexample would be any admissible p,q,m,n for which one of these two explicit polynomials has a negative coefficient.
domain_bridges: Nonnegative coefficient criteria for products with Phi_{pq}
proof_strategy: Use S_N=x(x^N-1)/(x-1)=x prod_{d|N,d>1} Phi_d. Since pq | m, Phi_{pq} divides S_{m^2}; write S_{m^2}/Phi_{pq}=x(1+x^{pq}+...+x^{m^2-pq})(1+...+x^{p-1})(1+...+x^{q-1}), which is visibly nonnegative. For S_{n^2}Phi_{pq}, prove a prefix-sum bound for coefficients of Phi_{pq}: its partial sums up to degree (p-1)(q-1) are 0 or 1, so convolution with a length n^2 block of ones is nonnegative when n^2 >= (p-1)(q-1)+1. Then verify evaluations at 1 and the product identity.
title: Semiprime cyclotomic transfer for square-sided dice

catalog_references: Dallard, Milanič, Štorgel 2024 – Conjecture on bounded tree‑independence
Hajebi & Spirkl 2026 – Characterization of bounded α‑tw by excluded families
Yolov 2018 – Definition and properties of tree‑independence number
description: Conjecture: For every integer d ≥ 1 and every planar graph H, there exists a constant C = C(d, H) such that any graph G that is K_{1,d}-free and does not contain H as an induced minor satisfies α‑tw(G) ≤ C, i.e., the class of K_{1,d}-free graphs without H as an induced minor has bounded tree‑independence number.
proof_strategy: Apply the excluded minor structure theorem to bound the independence number within each bag of a tree decomposition, using the K_{1,d}-free condition to limit local density, and combine with planar minor restrictions to obtain a uniform constant C(d, H).
title: Bounded tree-independence in K_{1,d}-free graphs excluding a planar minor

description: Let 𝒜⊆[n] choose k and ℬ⊆[n] choose ℓ be a cross‑intersecting pair (every A∈𝒜 meets every B∈ℬ). Define the diversity γ(𝒜)=|𝒜|‑Δ(𝒜) where Δ(𝒜) is the maximum degree of 𝒜, and analogously γ(ℬ). For n≫k,ℓ, suppose γ(𝒜)≥{n‑u‑1 \\choose k‑1} and γ(ℬ)≥{n‑v‑1 \\choose ℓ‑1} for some integers u,v with u+v≤n‑k‑ℓ. The conjecture states that the only families attaining the maximal possible product |𝒜|·|ℬ| under these diversity constraints are the "canonical" constructions obtained by taking a full star on a common element together with the unique maximal extensions described by the S_{U,V}^Q‑shift. This gives a sharp structural characterisation extending the Frankl‑Kupavskii‑Zakharov theorem to the cross‑intersecting setting.
proof_strategy: 1. Formalise families of k‑sets as finsets of finsets in Lean. 2. Prove basic lemmas about degree, diversity and cross‑intersection. 3. Implement the S_{U,V}^Q‑shift operator and show it preserves cross‑intersection and does not decrease diversity. 4. Adapt the shifting argument of Frankl‑Kupavskii to obtain a canonical shifted extremal pair. 5. Use compression to show any extremal pair must be isomorphic to the canonical one, relying on counting lemmas for binomial coefficients. 6. Derive the product bound and the uniqueness statement via a combinatorial optimisation argument formalised with Lean's `linarith`/`norm_num` tactics.
title: Uniqueness of extremal large cross‑intersecting families via diversity

description: Proposes that n_k surpasses an exponential growth threshold, confirming asymptotic properties untested yet.
proof_strategy: sieve-theoretic analysis
title: n_k Exceeds Exponential Bound

description: We conjecture that for any finite set S of primes with |S| ≥ k, the elementary symmetric partition function pre_k is injective on the set of integer partitions whose parts are S‑smooth (i.e., each part’s prime factors lie in S). This generalizes the proven result for m‑ary partitions (S = {m}) to arbitrary finite prime sets.
proof_strategy: Develop a reconstruction algorithm for partitions from pre_k(λ) using the unique factorization property of S‑smooth numbers. Show that the elementary symmetric sums determine the multiset of parts uniquely by iteratively solving for the largest part via a polynomial equation whose roots are S‑smooth numbers, then induct on the number of parts. This requires establishing that the set of S‑smooth numbers is closed under multiplication and that the elementary symmetric function e_k is strictly monotone in each argument when restricted to this set.
title: Injectivity of pre_k on S‑smooth partitions

description: Conjecture: For any oriented matroid of rank r, any element e∈E, and any two e‑embracing bases B and B′, the e‑embracing distance d_e(B,B′) equals the graph distance d_{G(P_{M^*,e})}(C(B,e),C(B′,e)) in the 1‑skeleton of the oriented matroid polyhedron P_{M^*,e}.
proof_strategy: Attempt to prove the equality by showing a non‑contractive, r‑Lipschitz mapping between e‑embracing bases and their e‑positive fundamental circuits, or find a counterexample violating the equality.
title: Equality of e‑embracing distance and polyhedron graph distance

description: For any finite multiset M of natural numbers, let S_M be the set of all distinct permutations of M. Define tc(w) as the number of terminal closers (right‑to‑left minima) of w, i.e., indices i such that w_j > w_i for all j > i. Define cp(w) as the number of cyclic points of w, i.e., vertices i in [|M|] that lie on a directed cycle of the functional digraph i → w_i. The conjecture states that the total sum of tc(w) over w∈S_M equals the total sum of cp(w) over w∈S_M.
proof_strategy: Use the augmented cycle index Z_{S_M} and its expression in terms of power‑sum symmetric functions. Specialize the symmetric functions to extract the statistics tc and cp via appropriate scalar products. Show that the resulting generating functions coincide by applying Lemma lm:partition and the symmetry of the power‑sum basis, yielding an identity that implies equality of the total sums. A sign‑reversing involution on pairs (w, i) where i is either a terminal closer or a cyclic point can also be constructed to give a bijective proof.
title: Equidistribution of Terminal Closers and Cyclic Points in Multiset Permutations

description: The paper constructs explicit modular forms to establish Ramanujan-type congruences. We conjecture that for the partition function p(n), the explicit construction using the Rankin-Cohen bracket yields a modular form of weight 4 on SL(2,Z) whose Fourier expansion explicitly demonstrates that p(5n+4) ≡ 0 (mod 5) for all n ≥ 0. Specifically, let f(τ) be the explicit modular form constructed via the bracket operator satisfying f(τ) ≡ (η(5τ)/η(τ))^5 (mod 5) in M_4(SL(2,Z)). Then the Fourier coefficients of f(τ) should provide a direct proof that p(5n+4) ≡ 0 (mod 5).
proof_strategy: Construct the explicit modular form f ∈ M_4(SL(2,Z)) using the Rankin-Cohen bracket on the eta-quotient (η(5τ)/η(τ))^5, compute its first several Fourier coefficients, and verify they match the pattern a(5n+4) ≡ 0 (mod 5) for the partition function.
title: Verification of Ramanujan's modulo 5 congruence via explicit modular form construction

description: The paper asserts precisely 57 nonnegative integer solutions (a, b, x) satisfy the inequality, confined by Diophantine approximation constraints.
proof_strategy: Direct enumeration under bounded exponents
title: Exact Solution Count Confinement

description: Let a_n be the number of isomorphism classes of finite simple connected planar 3-regular graphs with n vertices. The conjecture is that a_{2m+1}=0 for every m, and that there exist real constants C>0 and gamma>1 such that a_{2m} / (C (2m)^(-7/2) gamma^(2m)) tends to 1 as m tends to infinity. This isolates the main enumerative shape of the paper in a Lean-formalizable form without committing to the paper-specific numerical values of C and gamma.
domain_bridges: graph isomorphism quotients to finite cardinal enumeration
planar graph decomposition to analytic combinatorics
Burnside/Pólya symmetry enumeration to unlabelled counting
local large deviation estimates to coefficient asymptotics
proof_strategy: Define a_n as the cardinality of the quotient of finite simple connected planar cubic graphs on n vertices by graph isomorphism. The parity assertion follows from the handshaking lemma. For the asymptotic part, formalize the network and 3-connected decompositions used for cubic planar graphs, prove the relevant functional equations for the ordinary generating functions, establish their dominant square-root/singularity schema with computable error bounds, and then apply a formalized transfer theorem giving coefficient asymptotics with exponent -7/2. The final Lean proof would combine the coefficient theorem with the quotient-cardinality interpretation of the ordinary generating function.
title: Universal n^{-7/2} asymptotic for unlabelled connected cubic planar graphs

description: This conjecture asserts that if a continuum admits a projective Fraisse category whose automorphism group has a certain density condition, then its homeomorphism group behaves in a way tied to the exceptional amenability of its closed subgroups, formalizable within Lean 4 via exact properties of group flows.
proof_strategy: Constructive existence with density conditions via extremal combinatorics
title: Universal minimal flows in projective Fraisse categories

description: For bidegree (2,3) line arrangements in P^2, constructing Ziegler pairs (isomorphic intersection lattices) with distinct minimal graded free resolutions of their Jacobian algebras while preserving the minimal degree of Jacobian syzygies.
proof_strategy: Exploit parameterized families of arrangements with controlled intersection multiplicities, combined with Gröbner basis computations to distinguish free resolutions.
title: Existence of Ziegler Pairs with Same Minimal Degree of Jacobian Relation but Different Minimal Free Resolutions

description: For any locally finite multigraph G, there exists a linked, componental, rooted tree-cut decomposition (T, V) of finite adhesion such that each bag V_t is finite and the map phi: Omega_E(G) -> V(T) U Omega(T) restricts to a bijection between the set of ends Omega(G) and the ends of the decomposition tree Omega(T).
proof_strategy: The proof involves constructing a rooted tree-cut decomposition and iteratively refining it to achieve the 'linked' property using a Menger-type argument for edge-cuts in infinite graphs. For locally finite graphs, the 'undominated edge-ends' are exactly the ends of the graph, and the finiteness of bags follows from the finite adhesion and the fact that every end must be displayed, forcing the decomposition to split the graph into finite components.
title: Existence of Linked Tree-Cut Decompositions for Locally Finite Graphs

description: Let X be the universal pseudo-solenoid. Let F be the projective Fraisse limit of the natural projective Fraisse category associated to X (as constructed in the paper), and let R be the equivalence relation on F such that F/R is homeomorphic to X. Let Phi: Aut(F) -> Homeo(X) be the induced map. We conjecture that the image of Phi is dense in Homeo(X) with respect to the uniform topology.
proof_strategy: Show that for any homeomorphism h of X and any epsilon>0, there exists an automorphism of F that induces a homeomorphism within epsilon of h. This can be done by approximating h by a map that preserves the equivalence classes of the projective Fraisse limit and then lifting to an automorphism of F using the homogeneity and approximation properties of the Fraisse limit.
title: Density of the automorphism group of the projective Fraisse limit in the homeomorphism group of the universal pseudo-solenoid

description: Conjecture that for any two reduced line arrangements of degree d ≥ 12 in ℙ², if their intersection lattices are isomorphic and their Milnor algebras have identical Hilbert functions, then the minimal graded free resolutions of their Jacobian algebras are identical.
proof_strategy: Show that the intersection lattice determines the Poincaré polynomial of the Milnor algebra, which forces the graded Betti numbers of the minimal free resolution to be identical; use spectral sequence or local cohomology arguments to link lattice invariants to resolution data.
title: Equality of minimal free resolutions for Ziegler pairs of line arrangements of degree ≥12

catalog_references: Main theorem: every graph admits a linked componental finite-adhesion rooted tree-cut decomposition displaying all undominated edge-ends
description: Conjecture: Every connected locally finite multigraph G admits a rooted tree-cut decomposition (T,V) into finite bags, of finite adhesion, which is componental and linked, displays every end of G bijectively as an end of T, and is degree-normalized as follows. If a tree-end alpha of T displays the graph end omega, and e_n is the nth adhesion edge on the root-to-alpha ray of T, then: (i) if the edge-degree of omega is a finite natural number d, then |F_{e_n}| = d for all sufficiently large n; (ii) if the edge-degree of omega is infinite, then for every k : Nat, |F_{e_n}| >= k for all sufficiently large n. This strengthens the paper's displayed-edge-degree conclusion by asking for eventual exact stabilization along finite-degree ends and divergence along infinite-degree ends.
domain_bridges: Freudenthal-style end theory for locally finite graphs
Lean formalization of finite cuts via Finset edge sets
withTop Nat formulation of finite versus infinite edge-degree
rooted tree rays as sequences indexed by Nat
proof_strategy: Start from the linked componental finite-adhesion decomposition given by the paper for locally finite graphs. Refine the construction along each displayed tree ray by choosing nested finite edge-cuts that are minimal representatives of the corresponding end whenever the end has finite edge-degree, using edge-Menger to maintain linkedness after contractions/refinements. For infinite-degree ends, diagonalize over k and choose the nth sufficiently far cut to have size at least k, again preserving componentality by taking the end-side component and preserving linkedness via the minimum-cut characterization of the linked condition. The main technical point is a simultaneous refinement argument over all tree rays that does not destroy previously normalized adhesion values.
title: Degree-normalized linked tree-cut decompositions for locally finite graphs

description: Conjecture: For every positive integer d and every planar graph H, there exists a constant B(d,H) such that the tree-independence number of any K_{1,d}-free graph that does not contain H as an induced minor is at most B(d,H).
proof_strategy: Use the Hajebi–Spirkl characterization of bounded tree-independence number via forbidden induced subgraphs. Show that the class of K_{1,d}-free graphs with no induced minor H necessarily contains a member of each of the three required families (a complete bipartite graph, a graph from S, and the line graph of a graph from S). Consequently the class has bounded tree-independence number, and a bound can be extracted from the proof.
title: Bounded tree-independence number for K_{1,d}-free graphs excluding a planar induced minor

description: For sufficiently large n relative to k, if two families A, B ⊆ ([n] choose k) are cross-intersecting and each has diversity at least C(n-u-1, n-k-1) for some integer u with 1 ≤ u ≤ k-1, then up to isomorphism A and B are contained in the union of a star centered at 1 and the family of k-sets that contain 1 and intersect [2, u+1]; equivalently, they are subsets of the Hilton–Milner type construction for cross-intersecting pairs.
proof_strategy: Apply the S_{U,V}^{Q}-shift to compress the families while preserving cross-intersection and not decreasing diversity; iteratively obtain left-compressed families; then use a double counting argument on the diversity to bound the number of sets avoiding the most frequent element, leading to a structural description.
title: Extremal Structure of Large Cross-Intersecting Families via Diversity

description: Conjecture. Let F be a finite simple graph on r vertices with at least one edge and no isolated vertices, let p in (0,1), and let W be a graphon. Write W_U for the normalized restriction of W to a measurable set U of positive measure. If t_ind(F,W_U)=p^{e(F)}(1-p)^{binom(r,2)-e(F)} for every such U, then W=p almost everywhere. A counterexample would be a nonconstant graphon satisfying this induced-density identity on every positive-measure restriction.
domain_bridges: graph limits <-> induced subgraph density polynomials
finite quasi-random graph sequences <-> graphon rigidity
Hoeffding/irreducible chaos decomposition of symmetric L2 kernels
proof_strategy: Pass to the graphon limit. Expand the induced F-density on restrictions W_U as a polynomial in U-indicator functions and the Hoeffding chaos components of W-p. The all-subset hypothesis gives a polynomial identity for every measurable U. The lowest nonzero chaos component would produce a nonzero leading variation on some U, contradicting the identity; hence all chaos components vanish. Orthogonality of the chaos decomposition then gives W=p almost everywhere.
title: All-measurable induced F-count forcing for graphons

description: Prove that for any finite graph Gamma, if there exists a positive integer s such that for every potential s-clique characterized by average degree k and average common neighbor count lambda, the generalized clique adjacency polynomial CA_Gamma(x, s, k, lambda) is strictly negative for some integer x, then the clique number of Gamma is strictly less than s.
proof_strategy: The proof requires a formalization of the graph-theoretic properties of cliques (average degree and common neighbors) and the evaluation of the cubic polynomial CA_Gamma. The strategy involves showing that the existence of a clique of size s implies the existence of a root or non-negative value for the polynomial for specific integer values, contradicting the hypothesis via a proof by contradiction.
title: Formalization of the Generalized Clique Adjacency Polynomial Bound

description: For any finite set of pairwise non‑isomorphic Shimura curves s₁,…,s_r defined over number fields, let (z_n)_n be a sequence of CM points whose coordinates lie in extensions E_n with discriminants tending to infinity. Assume that two distinct odd primes p,q split completely in each E_n. Then the empirical measures of the Galois orbits of (z_n) converge weakly to the product of the normalized Haar measures on each s_i. This convergence holds without assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, only the splitting condition at p and q.
proof_strategy: Use adelic toral-packet equidistribution, combine with character-spectrum analysis and apply the joining classification; then pass to the limit of measures to obtain the weak convergence.
title: Equidistribution of CM Points on a Product of Non‑isomorphic Shimura Curves under Splitting Conditions

description: For any oriented matroid of rank r, the e‑embracing exchange distance between any two e‑embracing bases is at most 2·r^{log2(r)+3}.
proof_strategy: Exploit the r‑Lipschitz, non‑contractive mapping from e‑embracing bases to e‑positive fundamental circuits and analyze distances in the oriented matroid polyhedron skeleton.
title: Upper bound on e‑embracing distance between bases of oriented matroids

description: For multiset permutations, terminal closers (elements with no outgoing edges) and cyclic points (elements in cycles) are linearly equivalent: |terminal closers| + |cyclic points| = n for all w ∈ S_M. The bijection arises via digraph deconstruction, preserving combinatorial structure across arbitrary multiset permutations.
proof_strategy: Constructive bijection using digraph decomposition into cycles and rooted trees, formalized via species-theoretic functors in Lean 4.
title: Cyclic Points and Terminal Closers in Multiset Permutations Satisfy a Linear Equivalence

description: Prove an upper bound for the logarithmic ratio of the count of numbers up to x with Carmichael's lambda function λ(n) bounded by y, and establish its asymptotic sharpness under the assumption that the density of primes n ≤ x with λ(n) ≤ y equals the density of powersmooth integers in [2, y]
proof_strategy: Apply analytic number theory methods using the density of powersmooth integers and multiplicative group exponents, leveraging Dirichlet series and Tauberian theorems to relate the lambda function distribution to the primesmooth hypothesis
title: Upper Bound and Asymptotic Sharpness of Lambda Function Counts Under the Plausibility Hypothesis on Powersmooth Primes

catalog_references: Daisy cubes as induced subgraphs on Boolean-lattice down-sets
description: Conjecture: If G and H are finite nonempty partial cubes, then their Cartesian graph product G □ H is a daisy cube if and only if both G and H are daisy cubes. Equivalently, under the paper's characterization, every Θ-class of G □ H is peripheral exactly when every Θ-class of each factor is peripheral.
domain_bridges: Partial-cube Θ-coordinate embeddings translate Cartesian products into coordinate block sums.
Boolean down-sets are closed under direct product: if D⊆{0,1}^m and E⊆{0,1}^n are down-sets, then D×E⊆{0,1}^{m+n} is a down-set.
Peripheral Θ-classes in a product are exactly lifted peripheral Θ-classes from the factors.
proof_strategy: Show first that every Θ-class of G □ H is either a lift of a Θ-class of G or a lift of a Θ-class of H. For a lifted class θ_G × V(H), its two halfspaces are W_G^0 × V(H) and W_G^1 × V(H), and its boundary sets are U(θ_G,W_G^0) × V(H) and U(θ_G,W_G^1) × V(H). Hence the lifted class is peripheral iff θ_G is peripheral; similarly for H. Applying the paper's theorem that a finite partial cube is a daisy cube iff all Θ-classes are peripheral gives the result. Alternatively, using down-set models, if G=Q_m[D] and H=Q_n[E] with D,E down-sets, then G □ H is Q_{m+n}[D×E], again a down-set.
title: Cartesian products reflect and preserve daisy cubes

description: This paper presents a uniform method to generate Ramanujan-type congruences for sequences arising from combinatorial and modular constructions, aiming to transform theoretical results into concrete, verifiable expressions.
proof_strategy: Constructive transformation through Rankin-Cohen bracket and modular form weight identification
title: Explicit constructions for Ramanujan-type congruences

description: The arithmetic intersection number of the generating series of divisors on a unitary Shimura variety equals the logarithmic derivative at s=1 of the Hecke L-function attached to the CM extension.
proof_strategy: Show equality by comparing automorphic forms and using the exceptional correspondence of Shimura curves
title: Modular Height Formula for Unitary Shimura Varieties

catalog_references: Bugeaud–Laurent p‑adic lower bound for linear forms in logarithms
description: Conjecture that the largest value of $\max\{a,b\}\) among all non‑negative integer triples $(a,b,x)$ satisfying \(1\le |x^{2}-2^{a}3^{b}|<3\max\{a,b\}\) is exactly $2200$, i.e. no solutions exist with \(\max\{a,b\}>2200\).
proof_strategy: Apply the known Baker–Lang lower bound for linear forms in logarithms to obtain an explicit upper bound on \(\max\{a,b\}\); then use the LLL algorithm to verify that no solutions exist beyond the bound \(2200\).
title: Maximal exponent bound for solutions of $|x^{2} - 2^{a}3^{b}| < 3\max\{a,b\}$

description: Fix the column-alternating coloring in which every cell in column i has color (-1)^(i-1). Let B(n) be the number of Dyck paths of semilength n for which the number of black cells beneath the path equals the number of white cells beneath the path. The conjecture is: for every m >= 0, (2*m+1)*B(2*m) = binom(3*m,m), and (m+1)*B(2*m+1) = binom(3*m+1,m). Equivalently, B(2*m) is the ternary Fuss-Catalan number 1/(2*m+1)*binom(3*m,m), while B(2*m+1) is the Raney-type number 1/(m+1)*binom(3*m+1,m).
domain_bridges: Translate a Dyck path into the gap vector u_i counting up-steps between consecutive right-steps.
Use the column-alternating balance criterion: for n even, all odd-indexed gaps u_1,u_3,...,u_{n-1} vanish; for n odd, all even-indexed gaps u_2,u_4,...,u_{n-1} vanish.
Identify the remaining constrained gap vectors with Fuss-Catalan/Raney constrained compositions.
Formalize the count via a cycle-lemma or ballot-number argument and then discharge the binomial identities in Lean.
proof_strategy: Encode a Dyck path of semilength n by nonnegative gaps u_1,...,u_n, where u_i is the number of up-steps after the i-th right-step and before the next right-step, with total sum n and Catalan prefix constraints sum_{j<=i} u_j <= i for i<n. The column-alternating signed area is an alternating sum of column heights; telescoping gives the paper's criterion that balance forces u_odd=0 when n is even and u_even=0 when n is odd. For n=2*m, the surviving variables v_j=u_{2*j} have sum 2*m and constraints sum_{j<=r} v_j <= 2*r, giving the standard 2-Fuss-Catalan count. For n=2*m+1, the surviving variables v_j=u_{2*j-1}, together with the final gap, have sum 2*m+1 and constraints sum_{j<=r} v_j <= 2*r-1, giving the stated Raney number. In Lean, first prove the gap-vector bijection, then prove the two constrained-composition counts by a formal cycle lemma or by induction using the known ballot recurrence, and finally combine them.
title: Column-alternating balanced Dyck paths are counted by ternary Fuss-Catalan and adjacent Raney numbers

description: We conjecture that for every pair of distinct positive integers a,b the generating function of two standard 6‑sided dice can be factored as a product of two polynomials with non‑negative integer coefficients, each evaluating to a^2 and b^2 at x=1 respectively. In other words, there exist a dice of size a^2 and a dice of size b^2 whose label multisets give the same sum‑frequency distribution as two ordinary dice.
proof_strategy: Translate the problem to a factorisation of the frequency polynomial F(x)= (x+...+x^6)^2 = x^2 (x^6-1)^2/(x-1)^2. Use the factorisation of cyclotomic polynomials Φ_d(x) to express F as a product of irreducibles. Show that for any distinct squares a^2,b^2 there is a selection of these cyclotomic factors (with possible repetitions) whose product yields a polynomial P_a with P_a(1)=a^2 and non‑negative coefficients, and whose complementary factor P_b satisfies P_b(1)=b^2. The existence part reduces to solving a linear Diophantine system given by the degrees and constant terms of the chosen Φ_d. One can then employ the theory of integer cones (Hilbert bases) to prove the system always has a solution when a≠b, yielding the desired dice. Formalisation in Lean proceeds by: (1) defining generating functions of dice, (2) proving the cyclotomic factorisation of (∑_{i=1}^6 x^i)^2, (3) constructing the cone of admissible exponent vectors, (4) showing the cone contains a point with prescribed sum‑o
title: Existence of square‑sided dice pairs preserving the sum distribution of two standard dice

description: Let p > 5 be prime, and let mu(p) be the least positive integer m such that 2^m ≡ 1 or -1 mod p. The conjecture is that there are infinitely many primes p for which mu(p) = (p - 1) / 2. By the projective-doubling classification in the paper, this is equivalent to saying that infinitely many prime odd bases attain the maximal possible terminal four-digit Kaprekar cycle length (p - 1) / 2.
domain_bridges: Kaprekar digit dynamics to multiplication by 2 on projective residue classes
terminal cycle length to projective multiplicative order modulo p
extremal cycle length to Artin-type primitive root phenomena
proof_strategy: First formalize the paper's equivalence: for prime p > 5, the longest terminal four-digit Kaprekar cycle in base p has length (p - 1) / 2 iff the least m > 0 with 2^m = ±1 in ZMod p is (p - 1) / 2. Then prove that infinitely many primes satisfy this modular condition. A sufficient route is Artin's primitive root conjecture for 2, since if 2 is a primitive root modulo p then the projective order of 2 is exactly (p - 1) / 2. Conditional proofs could be obtained from Hooley's GRH-dependent theorem; an unconditional Lean proof would require major analytic number theory beyond current mathlib.
title: Infinitely many extremal prime odd bases for four-digit Kaprekar dynamics

description: For a given odd prime power $q=p^e$, let $K = \mathbb{F}_q(t)$. For a specific choice of $c \in K^*$, the arboreal Galois group $G_n = \Gal(\text{Spl}_K(f_c^{\circ n})/K)$ for the polynomial $f_c(x) = cx^{q-1} + t$ is isomorphic to the $n$-fold iterated wreath product of the cyclic group $C_{q-1}$ (the automorphism group of the $(q-1)$-ary tree $T_n$) for all $n \geq 1$.
domain_bridges: Function Field Arithmetic $\to$ Group Theory (Wreath Products)
proof_strategy: Formalize the construction of the twisted Carlitz module $\rho_t^c$ and its $t$-torsion. Use the recursive structure of the iterated wreath product $\text{Aut}(T_n) \cong 	ext{Aut}(T_{n-1}) \wr S_d$. Implement a criterion for surjectivity based on the existence of primitive prime divisors in the critical orbit of $f_c(x)$ in characteristic $p$, ensuring that the extensions at each level $n$ are linearly disjoint from the previous levels.
title: Maximality of Arboreal Galois Representations for Twisted Carlitz Polynomials

description: Conjecture that in Theorem 1.1 of the paper the error term O(‖μ̃‖^{3‑κ}) can be replaced by O(‖μ̃‖^{2+ε}) for every ε>0 (i.e. one can save a full power of ‖μ̃‖ beyond the square‑root barrier). This would imply, via the approximate functional equation, a bound of shape T^{2+ε} for the twisted first moment in the spectral aspect, matching the expected square‑root cancellation predicted by the random matrix model for a unitary ensemble.
proof_strategy: The conjecture would follow from establishing substantially stronger bounds for the archimedean integral transforms in the GL₃ Kuznetsov formula. One needs to exploit additional cancellation in the higher‑rank Kloosterman sums S(m₁,m₂;c) via Deligne’s bound adapted to the GL₃ setting, and to apply stationary phase / Mellin‑Barnes techniques to the Bessel‑type kernels appearing in the Kuznetsov trace formula. Combining these with a refined asymmetric approximate functional equation that isolates the diagonal contribution would yield the desired power saving of one full exponent.
title: Improved power‑saving error bound for the twisted first moment of GL₃ symmetric square L‑functions

proof_strategy:
1. Construct extremal families of graphs (e.g., joins of a complete graph with a carefully chosen path or threshold graphs) that achieve equality in the toughness condition.
2. Compute their adjacency and signless Laplacian spectra exactly, confirming \(\rho(G)=q(G)=(k-\eta)(n-1)/n\).
3. Show that any spanning \(k\)-tree would force a vertex of degree exceeding \(k\) due to the structural constraints imposed by the toughness and spectral equalities, yielding a contradiction.
4. Verify the construction for small parameters computationally and prove the general construction by induction on \(n\).
5. The existence of such counterexamples demonstrates that the conjectured bounds are sharp.
title: Sharp spectral bound for spanning k‑trees in τ‑tough graphs

description: Convergence of the generating function for the two-centered black hole index in $\mathbb{Z}_N$ CHL models is proven for $N=2,3$ by analyzing the analytic structure of the fundamental chamber $\CR_N$ and modular transformation properties of the matrix coefficients in the generating function decomposition. The proof leverages pole cancellation in the imaginary $\tau_2$-plane via black hole bound state metamorphosis.
domain_bridges: Black hole-bound state metamorphosis in CHL models → Generating function manipulation
Siegel modular forms → Convergence of sums over lattice points
proof_strategy: Modular analysis of the $\tau_2$-plane via the fundamental chamber $\CR_N$, demonstrating pole cancellations among CF1-CF4 terms through residue matching and modular transformation properties.
title: Convergence of Generating Function for Two-Centered Black Hole Index in CHL Models

description: Formalize the coupling between the 'q-game' (where a deterministic player removes q elements and a random player removes a uniform number of elements) and the cycle decomposition of a random permutation. Specifically, prove that the random player's winning probability is equal to the probability that the first cycle of length $\le q$ encountered in canonical cycle order is a fixed point (length 1).
proof_strategy: Implement the canonical cycle decomposition as a sequence of random variables. Define the game state as the number of remaining elements $m$. Use induction on $n$ to show that the transition probabilities of the game match the probabilities of encountering cycles of specific lengths in the permutation. Define a stopping time $\tau$ as the index of the first cycle with length $L \le q$. Prove that the event 'Random player wins' is equivalent to the event $L_{\tau} = 1$.
title: Equivalence of the q-Game Winning Probability and First Short Cycle Fixed-Point Probability

description: Conjecture: If P and Q are lattice polytopes in ℝ^p and ℝ^q that are very ample and satisfy the integer decomposition property, then their join P * Q ⊂ ℝ^{p+q+1} is also very ample.
proof_strategy: Use the description of very ampleness via the saturation of the affine semigroup of the cone over the polytope. Show that the cone over the join is the join of the cones over P and Q in one higher dimension. Under the integer decomposition property, the semigroups of the cones over P and Q are generated by their degree‑1 elements. Very ampleness of P and Q implies that these semigroups are already saturated in degree 1. A direct computation shows that the semigroup of the cone over the join is generated by the union of the generators of the two factors, hence is also saturated in degree 1, which exactly means that the join is very ample.
title: Very ampleness is preserved under join for lattice polytopes with the integer decomposition property

Kechris, A., Pestov, V., & Todorcevic, S. (2010). *Fraïssé Limits and Ramsey Theory*.

description: Conjecture that whenever a projective Fraïssé limit 𝔽 of finite structures has the approximate Ramsey property, the dense subgroup G ≤ Homeo(F) induced by Aut(𝔽) admits a universal minimal flow that is metrizable.
proof_strategy: Establish a correspondence between the combinatorial approximate Ramsey property of the projective Fraïssé limit and the topological dynamics of the dense automorphism group, adapting known characterizations of extreme amenability for non‑archimedean groups to dense subgroups of Homeo(F) and showing that such amenability forces the universal minimal flow to be metrizable.
title: Metrizability of the universal minimal flow for homeomorphism groups of continua via the approximate Ramsey property

description: For every integer r ≥ 2 there exists a constant C > 0 (e.g. C = 1/8) such that for all sufficiently large n there exists an n‑vertex r‑graph H in which each (r+1)-set of vertices spans either 0 or 2 edges and |E(H)| ≥ C / r^3 * binom(n, r).
proof_strategy: Random construction with dependent rounding combined with the Lovász Local Lemma to enforce the 0‑or‑2 condition, possibly refined by flag‑algebra techniques for upper bounds.
title: Conjecture on asymptotic density of r‑graphs with 0 or 2 edges per (r+1)-set

description: For any positive integer d and any planar graph H, the class of all K_{1,d}-free graphs without H as an induced minor has bounded tree-independence number. This conjecture generalizes the main result of Dallard et al. [2024], which proves it for outerstring graphs, to all planar graphs H.
proof_strategy: Extend the structural decomposition methods used for outerstring graphs to general planar graphs. Leverage the Robertson-Seymour graph minor theorem to handle induced minors and combine with K_{1,d}-freeness constraints to establish alpha-tw boundedness.
title: Dallard's Conjecture for Planar Graphs

description: Conjecture that in the setting of Theorem 1.1 of the paper, for any ε>0 there exists δ0>0 such that the asymptotic formula holds with error term O(‖μ̃‖^{3-ε}) instead of O(‖μ̃‖^{3-κ}) for some fixed κ>0. This would imply that the exponent in the error term can be taken arbitrarily close to 3.
proof_strategy: Refine the bounds for the archimedean integral transforms in the GL3 Kuznetsov formula by exploiting oscillatory cancellation and applying recent subconvexity bounds for GL3 Whittaker functions, aiming to save an additional power of the spectral parameter.
title: Improved power-saving error term for twisted first moment of symmetric square L-functions on GL(3)

description: Conjecture: For every prime power q, there exist infinitely many co‑edge‑regular graphs with exactly four distinct eigenvalues, smallest eigenvalue −2q−1, and coherent rank exactly q+4 (i.e., the lower bound q+4 from the paper is sharp).
proof_strategy: Leverage the known constructions from affine or projective planes of order q. Compute the intersection numbers for adjacent vertex pairs to show that the number of distinct common‑neighbour counts equals q+2. Then argue that the coherent algebra is generated by the adjacency matrix and these q+2 matrices, yielding coherent rank q+4. Verify that no additional relations arise, so the rank is exactly q+4.
title: Sharp coherent rank bound for co-edge-regular four‑eigenvalue graphs

description: The paper proves Frankl, Kiselev, and Kupavskii's conjecture that for any intersecting family \(\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}\) with \(n\ge 60k^{3/2}\) and \(k\ge 50\), the size of the symmetric difference family satisfies \(|\mathcal{SD}(\mathcal{F})|\le\sum_{\ell=0}^{k-1}\binom{n-1}{2\ell}\), with equality only for a specific class of stars. The proof relies on a concentration inequality and structural arguments on intersecting families.
proof_strategy: Apply a concentration inequality to control the distribution of set sizes within intersecting families, combine with shifting/compression to reduce the structure to stars, and enumerate symmetric differences via combinatorial counting.
title: Improved bound on symmetric differences of intersecting families

description: This work extends the stability results of the Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem to the setting of cross-intersecting families, characterizing extremal families via diversity constraints and providing a shift-based tool for construction.
proof_strategy: Constructive combinatorial argument with diversity-optimized families and a new shift operation.
title: Structural theorem for large cross-intersecting families

description: A graph sequence is quasi-random relative to a subgraph count function f if and only if the associated symmetric function in L²([0,1]^m) decomposes into irreducible subspaces under measure-preserving transformations in a way that satisfies specific orthogonality conditions with respect to the subgraph count's moment structure.
proof_strategy: Exploit the decomposition of symmetric functions into irreducible subspaces to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for quasi-randomness, contrasting with exceptions that violate these conditions.
title: Quasi-randomness via Symmetric Function Decomposition

description: Conjecture that for each fixed positive integer m, the set {(a,b) in N^2 : f(a,b)=m} has a natural density equal to C_m = (C / m^3) * product_{p|m} (1 - p^2/(p^3 + p^2 - 1)), where C = product_{p} (1 - 1/(p^2(p+1))) approx 0.881513.
proof_strategy: Prove the conjecture by evaluating the Dirichlet series sum_{a,b} 1_{f(a,b)=m} n^{-s}, showing it factors into an Euler product, and extracting the main term via a Delange-type Tauberian theorem; compare with the known constant C.
title: Asymptotic density of pairs with fixed f-value

description: Conjecture that for any pseudo-solenoid F, the closed group Homeo(F) is not extremely amenable, hence its universal minimal flow is non-metrizable.
proof_strategy: Use the dense embedding of Aut(𝔽) into Homeo(F) together with Veech’s theorem on non‑metrizability of universal minimal flows for non‑locally compact groups, and show that the approximate Ramsey property fails, implying non‑extreme amenability.
title: Non-extreme amenability of Homeomorphism Groups of Pseudo-Solenoids

description: Explores the existence and construction of Ziegler pairs using intersection lattices and motivates explicit examples with controlled geometric invariants.
proof_strategy: Constructive existence with convergence analysis
title: On Ziegler pairs of line arrangements: from non-existence to abundance

description: We conjecture that the Turán density $\pi(H^r_3)$ of the unique $(r+1)$-vertex $r$-graph with exactly two edges (the $(3,2)$-daisy) satisfies $\pi(H^r_3) = \Theta(r^{-3})$; i.e., there exist absolute constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that for every $r\ge2$, $c_1/r^3 \le \pi(H^r_3) \le c_2/r^3$. This would tighten the best known general lower bound $\Omega(r^{-3})$ (from the construction in the paper) and the general upper bound $O(1/r)$ from de Caen to a matching polynomial rate.
proof_strategy: Develop a stability analysis for near‑extremal $r$-graphs using flag algebras (or the recent “daisy” machinery) to show that any family with density $>C/r^3$ would force a forbidden $(r+1)$-configuration, yielding an $O(1/r^3)$ upper bound. One would first treat small $r$ by computer search, then prove a density increment / energy increment argument that improves de‟Caen’s double‑counting bound.
title: Polynomial upper bound for the maximum density of $r$-graphs with every $(r+1)$-set spanning $0$ or $2$ edges

Erdos--Ko--Rado theorem for intersecting uniform families

description: For all natural numbers n and k with n > 10k, every intersecting k-uniform family F of subsets of [n] has at most sum_{l=0}^{k-1} binom(n-1,2l) distinct pairwise symmetric differences. Equivalently, among all intersecting subfamilies of binom([n],k), the full star maximizes the cardinality of {A △ B : A,B in F}. This is falsifiable by a finite counterexample consisting of explicit n,k and a finite family F.
domain_bridges: Kneser graph independent sets: intersecting k-uniform families are independent sets in KG(n,k)
Johnson scheme: symmetric differences correspond to even Johnson distances
isoperimetric and shadow inequalities on the Boolean lattice
hypergeometric concentration inequalities for random k-subsets
proof_strategy: Formalize the problem as a finite extremal statement over Fin n. A plausible route is to combine shifting/compression to reduce to stable intersecting families, use an EKR-type stability theorem to separate near-star and far-from-star cases, and then count possible symmetric differences by Johnson-distance layers. The near-star case should be controlled by showing missing star structure cannot create more even layers than the full star; the far-from-star case should be bounded via concentration for intersections of random members, translating small intersection tails into a strict deficit in attainable symmetric differences.
title: Frankl--Kiselev--Kupavskii symmetric-difference bound for n > 10k

description: For every odd prime power q = p^e and every constant c in F_q^*, the polynomial f_c(x) = c*x^(q-1) + t in F_q(t)[x] has maximal arboreal Galois representation over F_q(t): for all n ≥ 1, the Galois group of the splitting field of f_c^{∘n} over F_q(t) is isomorphic to the n-fold iterated wreath product C_{q-1} ≀ C_{q-1} ≀ ⋯ ≀ C_{q-1} of the cyclic group of order q−1 with itself (with respect to the regular action). This extends the paper's result establishing maximality for two explicit families to all constant twists.
domain_bridges: Hilbert irreducibility over global function fields
proof_strategy: Induction on the level n, using the structure of the twisted Carlitz module torsion towers. The base case n=1 follows from the Kummer-theoretic analysis of x^(q-1) = -t/c over F_q(t). For the inductive step, one must show that each new level introduces the full cyclic wreath product extension by proving that the specialized polynomial f_c(x) - β has Galois group C_{q-1} over F_q(t)(β) for each (n-1)-th level root β, and that these extensions are sufficiently independent. The key tool is controlling ramification at the place (t) and at infinite places via the Drinfeld module structure, combined with a function-field analogue of Hilbert irreducibility to handle specialization.
title: Universal Arboreal Maximality for Constant Twists of Carlitz Polynomials

description: For the spectral family of level-one cuspidal automorphic representations π of PGL₃ with Langlands parameter μπ in a T^δ-ball around a generic μ̃, the second moment of central symmetric square L-values admits an asymptotic formula with power-saving error term: ∑_{π∈B} |L(1/2,π,sym²)|² · h(μπ)/N(π) = C · vol_spec(h) + O(‖μ̃‖^{3−κ}) for explicit C > 0 and κ > 0. This extends the authors' first moment result and is the key input needed for subconvexity bounds for these L-functions.
proof_strategy: Extend the GL₃ Kuznetsov-based first moment analysis to the second moment by squaring the asymmetric approximate functional equation and opening the Dirichlet series, then applying the GL₃ Kuznetsov formula twice. The main difficulty is controlling the off-diagonal contributions from the double Kloosterman sums and the archimedean integral transforms at higher depth. One must establish orthogonality of Fourier–Whittaker coefficients across the spectral family while managing the more severe analytic complications of the rank-3 Kloosterman sums arising in the dual sum.
title: Second Moment Asymptotic for Symmetric Square L-functions on GL₃

description: The paper establishes that for every prime power $q \ge 2$, there exist infinitely many co-edge-regular graphs with exactly four distinct eigenvalues, smallest eigenvalue $-2q-1$, and coherent rank at least $q+4$. We conjecture that these constructed graphs achieve coherent rank exactly $q+4$, which is equivalent to the number of common neighbours of adjacent vertex pairs taking exactly $q+2$ distinct values. This implies the existence of such graphs with exact coherent rank $q+4$.
proof_strategy: Analyze the intersection numbers of the constructed graphs (derived from affine or projective planes). Show that the number of distinct values for the common neighbours of adjacent pairs is exactly $q+2$, which bounds the coherent rank from above by $q+4$, matching the lower bound established in the paper.
title: Exact Coherent Rank of Co-edge-regular Graphs with Four Eigenvalues

Gallian-Rusin results on prime-product dice sizes
description: For any two distinct perfect squares a² and b², there exists at least one pair of square-sided dice with a² and b² sides whose sum frequency distribution matches that of two standard dice of the same sizes.
proof_strategy: Analyze cyclotomic polynomial decompositions of generating functions for square-sided dice and demonstrate constructive existence via factorization properties
title: Existence of Square-Sided Dice Pairs Replicating Standard Dice Sum Frequencies

description: For every integer k ≥ 3, there exist k-uniform hypergraphs F1 and F2 such that the positive codegree Turán density of the pair {F1,F2} is strictly positive, strictly less than each individual density, and equals exactly half of the minimum of the two individual densities.
proof_strategy: Construct F1 and F2 as specific small hypergraphs (e.g., a single edge and a pair of edges sharing (k-1) vertices) and use known exact values for their positive codegree densities; then apply a product construction to show the pair density is half the minimum.
title: Strong non-principality with exact ratio for positive codegree Turán density
