Hajebi--Spirkl characterization of finitely defined hereditary classes with bounded tree-independence number
Results on K_{2,d}-free graphs with no holes of length at least 5 from the cited paper
description: For every integer d ≥ 2, every finite simple graph G with no induced subgraph isomorphic to K_{2,d} and with no induced cycle of length at least 5 has tree-independence number at most 2d − 2. Equivalently, G admits a tree decomposition in which each bag induces a subgraph with independence number at most 2d − 2. This is a falsifiable strengthening of boundedness results for K_{2,d}-free graphs additionally forbidding long holes, replacing an unspecified or larger bound by an explicit linear bound.
domain_bridges: tree decompositions ↔ induced independence number of bags
forbidden induced complete bipartite graphs ↔ local common-neighborhood constraints
proof_strategy: Try to construct a clique-separator or minimal-separator decomposition for graphs with no induced cycles of length at least 5. Use induced-K_{2,d}-freeness to show that every separator bag can be enlarged so that any independent set inside the bag has size at most 2d−2: two nonadjacent vertices in a controlled separator should have fewer than d mutually independent witnesses on the opposite side, otherwise they induce K_{2,d}. Then combine the local separator bags recursively into a tree decomposition and verify that the maximum bag-independence is bounded by 2d−2.
title: Linear tree-independence bound for long-hole-free induced-K_{2,d}-free graphs

description: For integers n > 2k ≥ 2 and cross-intersecting families 𝒜, ℬ ⊆ ([n] choose k) with diversity γ(𝒜) ≥ C(n-k-1, k-1) and γ(ℬ) ≥ C(n-k-1, k-1), there exists an element x ∈ [n] such that both 𝒜 and ℬ are contained in the full star {F ∈ ([n] choose k) : x ∈ F}. This extends the Frankl–Kupavskii–Zakharov diversity stability theorem from intersecting to cross-intersecting families, and would provide a unified structural characterization implying cross-intersecting analogues of Hilton–Milner and Han–Kohayakawa as corollaries.
proof_strategy: Formalize the S_{U,V}^Q-shift operation in Lean and prove it preserves cross-intersection (the key lemma from the paper). Then establish that iterated shifting drives any cross-intersecting pair toward a canonical form. The diversity lower bounds constrain how far the pair can deviate from a common star, yielding the structural conclusion via a double-counting argument on the diversity terms.
title: Cross-Intersecting Diversity Stability Conjecture

description: The paper introduces a decomposition of the Hilbert space L²_sym([0,1]^m) of symmetric square-integrable functions on the m-dimensional unit cube into irreducible invariant subspaces V_{m,k} (k-th order interaction subspaces, analogous to the ANOVA decomposition) under the natural unitary action of the group Γ of measure-preserving bijections of [0,1]. The conjecture asserts that this decomposition is unique: the unitary representation of Γ on L²_sym([0,1]^m) is multiplicity-free, meaning each irreducible component appears with multiplicity at most one. Equivalently, if W ⊆ L²_sym([0,1]^m) is any closed subspace invariant and irreducible under the action of Γ, then W is contained in exactly one V_{m,k}. This would imply that the ANOVA-type decomposition is the only possible irreducible decomposition, strengthening the structural result in the paper and providing a representation-theoretic explanation for why certain subgraph count properties characterize quasi-randomness while others do not.
domain_bridges: Functional analysis (Hilbert space decompositions, L² theory on measure spaces)
Representation theory (irreducible unitary representations, multiplicity-free actions)
Combinatorics (graph limits, graphon theory, quasi-random graph properties)
proof_strategy: Prove multiplicity-freeness by showing the commutant algebra of the representation on L²_sym([0,1]^m) is abelian. This can be approached by identifying the commutant with the algebra of operators that commute with all U_γ (γ ∈ Γ), which should correspond to symmetric integral operators whose kernels are invariant under simultaneous measure-preserving permutations of their arguments. Show that such operators preserve the filtration by interaction order, and are diagonal with respect to the V_{m,k} decomposition, implying multiplicity-freeness via Schur's lemma type arguments. The key step is proving that any Γ-intertwinor between V_{m,k} and V_{m,k'} must vanish when k ≠ k'.
title: Uniqueness of the Irreducible Decomposition of Symmetric L² under Measure-Preserving Actions

description: For positive integers a and b, the arithmetic function f(a,b) = gcd(ab, a+b)/gcd(a,b) investigated in the paper can be expressed purely in terms of the greatest common divisor without division, specifically f(a,b) = gcd(gcd(a,b), a/gcd(a,b) + b/gcd(a,b)). This implies that gcd(a * b, a + b) is always divisible by gcd(a, b), and the quotient is exactly gcd(gcd(a,b), a/gcd(a,b) + b/gcd(a,b)).
proof_strategy: Let g = gcd(a, b), a = g*x, b = g*y with gcd(x, y) = 1. Then gcd(a*b, a+b) = gcd(g^2*x*y, g*(x+y)) = g * gcd(g*x*y, x+y). Since gcd(x, y) = 1, we have gcd(x*y, x+y) = 1. Thus gcd(g*x*y, x+y) = gcd(g, x+y) * gcd(x*y, x+y) = gcd(g, x+y). Therefore, gcd(a*b, a+b) = g * gcd(g, x+y), which completes the proof.
title: Simplified Expression for the Arithmetic Function f(a,b)

description: Conjectures that for a projective Fraïssé category 𝓕 with projective Fraïssé limit 𝔽, the universal minimal flow of the automorphism group Aut(𝔽) is metrizable if and only if 𝓕 admits a precompact expansion with the approximate Ramsey property. This generalizes the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence for metrizable UMFs from Fraïssé structures to projective Fraïssé categories and continua.
proof_strategy: Adapt the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic characterization of metrizable universal minimal flows for Fraïssé structures to the projective setting. Define precompact expansions of projective Fraïssé categories and prove that the approximate Ramsey property of such an expansion precisely controls the metrizability of the universal minimal flow of the corresponding topological group.
title: Metrizable Universal Minimal Flows via Approximate Ramsey Expansions

description: The Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence establishes that for a Fraissé class K with Fraissé limit F, Aut(F) is extremely amenable iff K has the Ramsey property, and the universal minimal flow M(Aut(F)) is metrizable iff some precompact expansion of K has the Ramsey property. The present paper extends the first equivalence to projective Fraissé categories via the approximate Ramsey property. This conjecture extends the second equivalence: for a projective Fraissé category F with limit 𝔽 and G the closure of Aut(𝔽) in Homeo(𝔽/R^𝔽), the universal minimal flow M(G) is metrizable if and only if there exists an approximate precompact expansion of F satisfying the approximate Ramsey property.
proof_strategy: Adapt the KPT metrizability criterion (Theorem 7.5 of Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic) to the projective Fraissé setting by replacing the Ramsey property with the approximate Ramsey property throughout. Construct the approximate precompact expansion as a category of finite graphs enriched with additional relational structure that approximates the precompact topology on G. Show that the universal minimal flow M(G) can be realized as the Samuel compactification of a suitable G-space, and that metrizability of this compactification corresponds to the existence of an approximate expansion with the approximate Ramsey property, mirroring the argument in the paper's Theorem 3.2 but for the non-trivial case.
title: Approximate Ramsey Property for Precompact Expansions Characterizes Metrizable Universal Minimal Flows

description: For every integer d ≥ 9, there exist line arrangements A and A' of degree d in P^2 that form a Ziegler pair satisfying both condition (HF) (same Hilbert function of the Milnor algebra) and condition (MDR) (same minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy). That is, they have isomorphic intersection lattices, the same Hilbert function and mdr value, but distinct graded Betti numbers in the minimal free resolutions of their Jacobian algebras M(f) and M(f').
proof_strategy: Construct infinite families of Ziegler pairs by deformation techniques (condition SPEC_0) extending the d=9 and d=10 examples, then show that the Hilbert function and mdr are preserved under these deformations while Betti numbers can be made to differ. A combinatorial argument on intersection lattices may establish that the lattice does not determine the full resolution structure for d ≥ 9, by showing that lattice automorphisms cannot account for all possible module structures on AR(f).
title: Ziegler Pairs Exist for All Sufficiently Large Degrees

description: The maximum asymptotic density of an n-vertex r-graph in which every (r+1)-set spans 0 or 2 edges is Θ(1/r). Specifically, there exists a constant c > 0 such that for all r ≥ 2 and sufficiently large n, there is an n-vertex r-graph with this property having at least (c/r) * C(n, r) edges. This would significantly improve the Ω(r^(-3)) lower bound established in the paper and match the known O(1/r) upper bound by de Caen, as well as the exact asymptotic densities for r=2 (1/2) and r=4 (1/4).
proof_strategy: Develop explicit algebraic or pseudorandom constructions generalizing the finite geometry and random tournament approaches that successfully achieved the 1/r density for r=4. This could involve defining edges over finite fields or vector spaces using quadratic forms or higher-dimensional orientations, ensuring that every (r+1)-set spans an even number of edges, and analyzing the spectral properties or pseudorandomness to verify the 0-or-2 condition.
title: Linear Density Conjecture for 0-or-2 Hypergraphs

description: For every pair of integers 2 ≤ a < b, there exists a unique pair of dice (D₁, D₂) such that D₁ has a² sides, D₂ has b² sides, and the sum frequencies of (D₁, D₂) equal those of two standard (ab)-sided dice. This extends the paper's study of square-sided dice pairs to a complete existence-and-uniqueness characterization, generalizing the classical Sicherman uniqueness result (where a = b = √6 is impossible, and the unique non-standard (2,6)-solution has dice of sizes 6 and 6).
proof_strategy: Use the cyclotomic polynomial factorization framework from the paper: the frequency polynomial F(x) = x²((x^m-1)/(x-1))² factors uniquely into cyclotomic polynomials. A (2,m)-solution with dice of sizes a² and b² (where m=ab) corresponds to a partition of the cyclotomic factors of F into two groups P₁, P₂ with P₁(1)=a² and P₂(1)=b² and non-negative integer coefficients. Prove existence by constructing the canonical factorization (reassigning cyclotomic factors Φ_d with d|m but d∤a to P₂, and d|a to P₁), and prove uniqueness by showing the cyclotomic factor assignment is forced by the degree and evaluation-at-1 constraints.
title: Unique Existence of Square-Sided (2,ab)-Solutions

description: For any integer $k \ge 2$ and any finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, the positive codegree Turán density $\gamma^+(\mathcal{F})$ is a rational number. This extends the recent breakthrough resolving the rationality of standard codegree Turán densities $\gamma(\mathcal{F})$ to the positive codegree setting, which restricts the minimum codegree to only those $(k-1)$-sets that lie in at least one edge.
proof_strategy: Adapt the algebraic and regularity-based framework of Gao, Pikhurko, Rong, and Sun for standard codegree densities. This involves using the hypergraph regularity lemma to show that asymptotically extremal configurations for the positive codegree can be approximated by blow-ups of a finite number of weighted hypergraphs, which implies the density must be a rational number.
title: Rationality of Positive Codegree Turán Densities

description: The projective Fraïssé category of finite pseudo-arc graphs (as constructed by Irwin-Solecki) has the approximate Ramsey property. By the main theorem of the paper, this is equivalent to the statement that the homeomorphism group of the pseudo-arc is extremely amenable. The pseudo-arc is the unique hereditarily indecomposable arc-like continuum, and determining whether its homeomorphism group is extremely amenable—and thus whether its universal minimal flow is trivial—remains a central open problem in the dynamics of continua.
proof_strategy: Following the methodology of the paper, construct the projective Fraïssé category for the pseudo-arc using Irwin-Solecki's finite graph framework, then establish the approximate Ramsey property by verifying the combinatorial condition on colorings of morphisms in the category. The key step is proving an approximate Ramsey theorem for colorings of surjective graph homomorphisms between finite pseudo-arc models, adapting the KPT correspondence to the projective (surjective morphism) setting. This requires developing a projective analogue of structural Ramsey theory for the specific class of graphs encoding pseudo-arc combinatorics.
title: Approximate Ramsey Property for the Pseudo-Arc Category

description: For every integer d ≥ 10, there exists a Ziegler pair of line arrangements of d lines satisfying conditions (HF) and (MDR), meaning they have isomorphic intersection lattices, the same Hilbert function of the Milnor algebra, the same minimal degree of a Jacobian relation, but distinct graded Betti numbers in the minimal free resolution of the Milnor algebra.
proof_strategy: Inductively extend the known Ziegler pairs for d=10 and specific higher degrees to all d ≥ 10 by adding lines in configurations that preserve the intersection lattice isomorphism, Hilbert function, and minimal derivation relation degree, while ensuring the minimal graded free resolution remains distinct.
title: Existence of Ziegler Pairs with Identical Hilbert Function and MDR for All Degrees d ≥ 10

description: The maximum asymptotic density of an n-vertex r-graph in which every (r+1)-set spans exactly 0 or 2 edges is Θ(r^{-2}) as r → ∞. Specifically, there exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every r ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large n, there exists an r-graph on n vertices where every (r+1)-set spans 0 or 2 edges, with at least c/r² · C(n,r) edges. This would improve the Ω(r^{-3}) construction in the paper and match the conjectured optimal order, complementing the trivial O(r^{-1}) upper bound from de Caen's double-counting argument.
proof_strategy: Improve the random subspace / parity-based construction from the paper (which yields Ω(r^{-3})) by using a more refined algebraic or probabilistic construction over finite fields to achieve Ω(r^{-2}). A promising approach: for r = 2k, use k-dimensional vector spaces over F_q with edges defined by affine conditions involving quadratic forms, where the 0-or-2 property follows from quadratic residue structure. For the upper bound, extend de Caen's double-counting with a more careful inclusion-exclusion or flag algebra argument to show O(r^{-2}).
title: Quadratic density conjecture for Frankl-Füredi 0-or-2 hypergraphs

description: For any odd prime power $q$ and nonzero constant $c \in \mathbb{F}_q^\times$, the polynomial $f_c(x) = cx^{q-1} + t$ is arboreally maximal over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$ (i.e., its $n$-th iterated Galois group is isomorphic to the $n$-fold iterated wreath product of $C_{q-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$) if and only if the Galois representation of the twisted Carlitz module $\rho_t^c(x) = tx + cx^q$ is surjective at the finite place $(t)$.
proof_strategy: Prove the contrapositive of the missing implication by demonstrating that any obstruction to arboreal maximality at level $n$ forces a corresponding drop in the size of the local Galois image at $(t)$, using the structural connection between the $t$-power torsion tower of $\rho_t^c$ and the iterated splitting fields of $f_c$.
title: Local-Global Arboreal-Adelic Equivalence for Twisted Carlitz Polynomials

description: For the spectral family of level-one cuspidal automorphic representations on PGL(3) with Langlands parameters in generic position of size T, the second moment of central symmetric square L-values satisfies the asymptotic formula: the spectral average of |L(1/2, π, sym²)|² equals C₂ · vol_spec(h) · log(‖μ̃‖)(1 + o(1)) as ‖μ̃‖ → ∞, where C₂ is an explicit positive constant and vol_spec(h) is the spectral volume. This extends the paper's first moment result and is consistent with the random matrix model prediction for a unitary ensemble of degree-6 L-functions, where the logarithmic factor arises from the diagonal contribution of the Rankin-Selberg L-function pole at s=1.
proof_strategy: Extend the GL(3) Kuznetsov spectral decomposition to handle the second moment. The diagonal contribution should yield the main term via a double application of the asymmetric approximate functional equation, producing a logarithm from the pole of ζ(s) at s=1 in the resulting Rankin-Selberg integral. The essential difficulty is controlling the off-diagonal terms: pairs (π, π') with π ≠ π' contribute via L(s, π ⊗ π̃'), requiring subconvexity bounds for GL(3)×GL(3) Rankin-Selberg L-functions and stationary phase analysis of the GL(3) Bessel integral transforms. The spectral large sieve on GL(3) should bound the off-diagonal below the main term, but the current state of GL(3) harmonic analysis makes this a formidable obstacle.
title: Second Moment Asymptotic for Symmetric Square L-functions on GL(3)

description: For each m ≥ 1, the Hilbert space L²_sym([0,1]^m) of symmetric square-integrable functions decomposes under the diagonal action of the group G of measure-preserving bijections of [0,1] into exactly m+1 isotypic components V_0 ⊕ V_1 ⊕ ... ⊕ V_m, where V_k consists of symmetric functions with genuine k-variable dependence. A restricted subgraph count property P for m-vertex graphs (specified by a graph F and a vertex-class restriction) characterizes quasi-random graph sequences of density p if and only if the G-invariant closed subspace generated by the associated test functional τ_P in L²_sym([0,1]^m) contains V_k for every k ∈ {1,...,m}. Equivalently, P fails to characterize quasi-randomness iff the subspace associated to P lies entirely within a proper G-invariant closed subspace.
proof_strategy: Establish the m+1 isotypic decomposition by induction on m, showing each V_k is generated by symmetrized tensor products of mean-zero L²([0,1]) functions with exact k-fold genuine dependence. For the characterization criterion: (⇒) If W_P lies in a proper G-invariant subspace, construct a non-quasi-random graphon satisfying P by taking any graphon whose deviation from p lies in the complementary invariant subspace. (⇐) If W_P generates all V_k for k≥1, then t(F,W)=p^{e(F)} forces the projection of W-p onto every V_k to vanish, implying W=p a.e.
title: Isotypic Decomposition Determines Quasi-Random Characterizations

description: Every graph on at least 3 vertices with toughness at least 9/4 contains a Hamilton cycle. This is the optimal form of Chvátal's toughness conjecture, as Bauer, Broersma, and Veldman demonstrated that 9/4 is the best possible threshold by constructing (9/4 - ε)-tough non-Hamiltonian graphs for arbitrary ε > 0.
proof_strategy: Assume for contradiction there exists a non-Hamiltonian 9/4-tough graph. Analyze the structural properties of vertex cuts and their resulting components in a maximal counterexample, leveraging spectral bounds or longest path/cycle arguments to constrain the graph's topology, ultimately deriving a contradiction to the 9/4-toughness condition.
title: Chvátal's 9/4-Toughness Implies Hamiltonicity

catalog_references: Chao, Gabel, Larson, and Nasr (dice relabeling via cyclotomic polynomials)
Gallian and Rusin (existence of nonstandard dice solutions)
description: For any positive integer m that is not a perfect square, there does not exist a pair of dice consisting of one die with p² sides and one die with q² sides (where p and q are positive integers) that produces the same sum frequency distribution as two standard m-sided dice. This conjecture generalizes the cyclotomic polynomial approach to dice relabeling by asserting that the generating function factorization required for such square-sided solutions cannot exist when m lacks square structure.
proof_strategy: Analyze the factorization of the frequency polynomial F(x) = (∑_{i=1}^m x^i)² = x²((x^m-1)/(x-1))² using cyclotomic decomposition. Show that any valid factorization into two polynomials P₁(x) and P₂(x) where P₁(1) = p² and P₂(1) = q² requires m to have a specific square-free factorization structure. Use properties of cyclotomic polynomials Φ_d(x) and their evaluations at x=1 to establish necessary divisibility conditions that cannot be satisfied when m is not a perfect square.
title: Nonexistence of Square-Sided Dice Solutions for Non-Square Orders

description: Let n > 2k ≥ 2 be positive integers. If F, G ⊆ ([n] choose k) are cross-intersecting families (every F ∈ F intersects every G ∈ G), and neither F nor G is a star (i.e., ∄x with x ∈ ⋂F, and ∄y with y ∈ ⋂G), then |F| · |G| ≤ (C(n-1,k-1) - C(n-k-1,k-1) + 1)². Equality holds if and only if (F, G) is isomorphic to (HM_{n,k}, HM_{n,k}), where HM_{n,k} = {[2,k+1]} ∪ {H ∈ C([n],k) : 1 ∈ H ∧ H ∩ [2,k+1] ≠ ∅} is the Hilton-Milner family.
proof_strategy: Use the S_{U,V}^Q-shift method introduced in the paper to reduce to shifted families, then apply diversity-based structural decomposition. The key steps are: (1) Show the S_{U,V}^Q-shift does not decrease |F|·|G| for cross-intersecting pairs, (2) Analyze the diversity structure of extremal pairs using the cross-intersecting analogue of Kupavskii's theorem established in the paper, (3) Show that if both families have positive diversity, the product is bounded by |HM_{n,k}|², (4) Verify uniqueness of the extremal configuration via stability arguments.
title: Product Hilton-Milner Bound for Cross-Intersecting Families

description: Let K be a field of characteristic p > 0, let f(x) ∈ K[x] be a monic irreducible polynomial with separable presentation f(x) = f^sep(x^{p^n}), and let L = K[x]/(f(x)). If m_f denotes the numerical field invariant defined via the coefficients of f (as in Definition 1 of the referenced paper), then the degree of L over the compositum L^{pi} · L^{sep} is given by [L : L^{pi} · L^{sep}] = p^{n - m_f}. In particular, L = L^{pi} · L^{sep} if and only if m_f = n.
proof_strategy: First formalize the numerical invariant m_f in terms of the coefficients of f(x) = Σ λ_i x^{ip^n} in its separable presentation. Then establish that L^{pi} = K(θ^{p^{m_f}}) where θ is the class of x in L, and compute the tower of degrees [L : L^{sep}] = p^n, [L^{pi} : K] = p^{m_f}, [L^{pi}L^{sep} : L^{sep}] = p^{m_f}, yielding [L : L^{pi}L^{sep}] = p^n / p^{m_f} = p^{n - m_f}. The equivalence L = L^{pi} · L^{sep} ↔ m_f = n follows immediately since the degree equals 1 iff n = m_f.
title: Degree Formula for the Compositum of Maximal Purely Inseparable and Separable Subfields

catalog_references: Co-edge-regular graphs with four eigenvalues and unbounded coherent rank
description: For every integer q ≥ 2, there exist infinitely many co-edge-regular graphs with exactly four distinct eigenvalues, smallest eigenvalue -2q-1, and coherent rank at least q+4. This extends the paper's main theorem by removing the requirement that q admits an affine or projective plane of order q.
proof_strategy: Modify the construction to bypass the requirement of finite planes of order q, possibly by using partial geometries, pseudo-geometric structures, or direct matrix constructions that satisfy the required spectral and regularity properties without relying on affine/projective planes.
title: Co-edge-regular graphs with four eigenvalues and high coherent rank for all orders

description: The natural density of ordered pairs of positive integers (a, b) such that gcd(ab, a+b) = gcd(a,b) is equal to the quadratic class number constant C = ∏_p (1 - 1/(p^2(p+1))). More generally, for any fixed positive integer m, the density of pairs (a,b) such that gcd(ab,a+b) = m * gcd(a,b) is C_m = (C / m^3) ∏_{p|m} (1 - p^2/(p^3+p^2-1)).
proof_strategy: First formalize the simplification of the arithmetic function f(a,b) = gcd(ab, a+b)/gcd(a,b) to gcd(gcd(a,b), (a+b)/gcd(a,b)). Then establish the Dirichlet series and Euler product for the characteristic function of f(a,b)=m. Finally, apply Tauberian theorems to derive the asymptotic density from the Euler product.
title: Asymptotic Density of Pairs with Coprime-like Condition

description: If the toric ideal of a lattice polytope is generated by quadratic binomials, then the polytope has the clique-face property; that is, every clique of its 1-skeleton is the vertex set of a face. The paper proves this under a mild condition on edges (condition (E)) and unconditionally for (0,1)-polytopes, but the general case for arbitrary lattice polytopes remains an open conjecture.
proof_strategy: Attempt to extend the algebraic and combinatorial techniques used for (0,1)-polytopes and polytopes satisfying condition (E) to arbitrary lattice polytopes, focusing on the structure of primitive edge directions. Alternatively, search for a counterexample by constructing a lattice polytope whose toric ideal is quadratically generated but whose 1-skeleton contains a clique that does not form a face.
title: Quadratic Generation Implies Clique-Face Property for Lattice Polytopes

description: If F₁ and F₂ are projective Fraïssé categories each satisfying the approximate Ramsey property (ARP), then their categorical product F₁ × F₂—whose objects are pairs (A₁, A₂) with Aᵢ ∈ Fᵢ and morphisms are pairs (f₁, f₂) of morphisms—is also a projective Fraïssé category satisfying ARP. On the dynamical side, this would imply that if G₁ and G₂ are extremely amenable groups realized as dense automorphism groups of projective Fraïssé limits, then the natural product group arising from the product category is also extremely amenable—consistent with the known fact that products of extremely amenable topological groups are extremely amenable. The conjecture bridges the combinatorial (ARP), categorical (products), and dynamical (extreme amenability) aspects of the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence extended to the projective Fraïssé setting.
proof_strategy: Adapt the product argument from classical Ramsey theory: given structures A ≤ B in F₁ × F₂ and a k-coloring of Emb(A, C), project onto each coordinate to obtain colorings of Emb(A₁, C₁) and Emb(A₂, C₂). Apply ARP in each factor to obtain approximate monochromatic embeddings, then combine them using a diagonalization or interleaving argument that respects the ε-approximation in the product. The key difficulty is controlling the simultaneous approximation in both coordinates. Alternatively, prove the dynamical side first: show that the product of the relevant topological groups inherits extreme amenability, then invoke the paper's main theorem (ARP ↔ extreme amenability) for the product category.
title: Approximate Ramsey Property is Preserved Under Categorical Products of Projective Fraïssé Categories

description: Let F be a projective Fraïssé category of finite reflexive graphs such that the quotient of its projective Fraïssé limit by the inherited edge relation is a hereditarily indecomposable continuum. Then F has the approximate Ramsey property if and only if this quotient continuum is the pseudo-arc. This extends the paper's equivalence between ARP and extreme amenability by predicting that, within the class of hereditarily indecomposable continua arising as projective Fraïssé limits, only the pseudo-arc yields an extremely amenable homeomorphism group.
proof_strategy: The 'if' direction follows from known results: Homeo(pseudo-arc) is extremely amenable, so by the paper's main theorem the corresponding projective Fraïssé category has ARP. The 'only if' direction requires showing that for any hereditarily indecomposable continuum other than the pseudo-arc (e.g., the pseudo-solenoid, circle-like continua), the associated projective Fraïssé category fails ARP. This could proceed by constructing explicit finite colorings of morphisms that witness the failure of ARP, generalizing the combinatorial obstructions used for the pseudo-solenoid case.
title: ARP Characterizes the Pseudo-Arc Among Hereditarily Indecomposable Continua

description: Every K_5-free graph on n vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most n^2/8 edges. Formally, for every epsilon > 0, there exists n_0 such that for all n >= n_0, every K_5-free graph on n vertices has a bipartition such that the number of edges within the parts is at most (1/8 + epsilon)n^2.
proof_strategy: Use flag algebras to establish the asymptotic bound, followed by stability analysis to identify extremal constructions as complete 4-partite graphs, similar to the proof for K_6 by Hu et al.
title: Sudakov's Conjecture for Bipartite Cuts in K_5-free Graphs

description: For any line arrangement of fewer than 9 lines in the projective plane, the intersection lattice determines the exponent data (degree sequence of minimal Jacobian syzygy generators). Equivalently, there are no Ziegler pairs of line arrangements of degree d < 9. This captures the main theoretical result of the paper, establishing that lattice-isomorphic arrangements of at most 8 lines have isomorphic modules of Jacobian syzygies AR(f) and hence identical graded Betti numbers in the minimal free resolution of the Milnor algebra M(f).
domain_bridges: homological algebra of minimal free resolutions
proof_strategy: Formalize intersection lattices of line arrangements as finite atomistic lattices, define the Jacobian syzygy module AR(f) and its graded structure over the polynomial ring S = ℂ[x,y,z], then proceed by case analysis on d = 2,...,8 using the combinatorial constraints on multiplicities n_k imposed by the lattice to show that the Hilbert function of M(f) and the degree sequence of AR(f) are uniquely recovered from L(A).
title: Intersection Lattice Determinacy for Small Line Arrangements

description: For any fixed prime power q, the logarithmic number of q-matroids of rank r on F_q^n satisfies log_2(m_q(n, r)) ~ GaussianBinomial(n, r, q) as n -> infinity with r = floor(n/2), where m_q(n, r) is the number of q-matroids of rank r on F_q^n. This is the q-analogue of the classical conjecture that sparse-paving matroids dominate all matroids, asserting that the lower bound from sparse-paving q-matroids (constructible via constant-dimension codes) is asymptotically tight, closing the gap identified between the entropy-based upper bounds and code-based lower bounds in the paper.
proof_strategy: Establish that sparse-paving q-matroids dominate by: (1) showing the number of circuit-hyperplane families (independent sets in the q-Kneser graph on r-dimensional subspaces sharing (r-1)-dimensional subspaces) is 2^{(1+o(1))GaussianBinomial(n,r,q)}, via a q-analogue of the Lovász local lemma or probabilistic method; (2) tightening the entropy-based upper bound from the paper to match this growth rate by refining the contraction-closure argument to show that any q-matroid class closed under contraction has logarithmic count O(GaussianBinomial(n,r,q)).
title: Asymptotic Dominance of Sparse-Paving q-Matroids

description: For every composite integer m ≥ 4 that admits a factorization m = ab with 1 < a < b, there exists a pair of dice with a² and b² sides respectively, each labeled with positive integers, whose sum frequency distribution is identical to that of two standard m-sided dice. Equivalently, the polynomial x²((x^m − 1)/(x − 1))² can be factored into two polynomials P₁ and P₂ with non-negative integer coefficients such that P₁(1) = a² and P₂(1) = b².
proof_strategy: Use the cyclotomic factorization of (x^m − 1)/(x − 1) into irreducible cyclotomic polynomials Φ_d(x) for d | m. Distribute these factors (along with the mandatory x factors) between P₁ and P₂ so that P₁(1) = a² and P₂(1) = b², then verify the resulting polynomials have non-negative integer coefficients. The key difficulty is showing that for each valid (a,b) with ab = m, at least one distribution of cyclotomic factors yields non-negative coefficients.
title: Existence of Square-Sided (2,m)-Solutions for Composite m

description: For any lattice polytope P, if the toric ideal I_P is generated by quadratic binomials, then P has the clique-face property: every clique of the 1-skeleton of P is the vertex set of a face. This conjecture strengthens the paper's main theorem (Theorem 1.1) by removing the 'mild condition on edges' hypothesis, which requires that for every edge {u,v} of P, the difference u-v has at most two nonzero entries. The (0,1)-polytope case already holds unconditionally, suggesting the edge condition may be an artifact of the proof technique rather than a genuine necessity.
proof_strategy: The paper's proof under the edge condition proceeds by showing that if a clique C is not a face, then one can construct a binomial in I_P of degree >= 3 that cannot be reduced by quadratic generators—a contradiction. To remove the edge condition, one would need to handle the case where edges have difference vectors with 3+ nonzero entries. A potential approach: (1) generalize the monomial divisibility argument from the condition-(E) case to arbitrary lattice polytopes by analyzing the lattice structure of edge directions; (2) use the secondary polytope or Gröbner basis theory to show that quadratic generation forces all higher-degree relations to decompose; (3) alternatively, find a counterexample among lattice polytopes with 'long' edges (difference vectors with many nonzero entries) to establish whether the edge condition is genuinely necessary.
title: Quadratic generation implies clique-face property without edge conditions

description: For a projective Fraïssé category F with limit 𝔽, quotient continuum F = 𝔽/R^𝔽, and G the closure of Aut(𝔽) in Homeo(F), the universal minimal flow M(G) is metrizable if and only if F has the fractional approximate Ramsey property: for all objects A, B in F, all r ∈ ℕ, and all finite colorings c: Emb(A,B) → {1,...,r}, there exists an object C in F, a morphism φ: C → B, and a subset S ⊆ {1,...,r} with |S| < r such that for every ψ ∈ Emb(A,C), c(φ∘ψ) ∈ S. This extends the paper's main theorem (where |S|=1 recovers ARP ↔ extreme amenability) and provides a combinatorial characterization of metrizable UMFs for homeomorphism groups of continua.
proof_strategy: Forward direction: if M(G) is metrizable, identify a compact metrizable G-flow X with a dense orbit and use the KPT correspondence to construct the fractional ARP witness by approximating colorings via the projective system structure, reducing to the fact that X provides a 'precompact expansion' of the category. Backward direction: fractional ARP implies the existence of a combinatorially defined compact metrizable G-flow (built from the projective limit with a 'reduced color' structure) that is universal among minimal metrizable flows. The key tool is an extension of the Ellis semigroup argument used in the paper's Theorem on ARP ↔ extreme amenability.
title: Fractional Approximate Ramsey Property Characterizes Metrizable Universal Minimal Flows

description: The paper proves that if a lattice polytope P satisfies condition (E) on its edges and the toric ideal I_P is generated by quadratic binomials, then P has the clique-face property: every clique of the 1-skeleton of P is the vertex set of a face. Condition (E) is automatically satisfied by (0,1)-polytopes but not by all lattice polytopes. The conjecture is that condition (E) can be entirely removed: for any lattice polytope P, quadratic generation of I_P alone implies the clique-face property.
proof_strategy: The paper's proof relies on condition (E) to control the structure of edges in the polytope. To remove it, one would need to show that quadratic generation of the toric ideal itself forces enough combinatorial rigidity that every clique in the 1-skeleton must span a face. A potential approach: analyze the Gröbner basis structure of quadratically generated toric ideals and show that any clique not corresponding to a face would produce a binomial relation of degree ≥ 3, contradicting quadratic generation. Alternatively, develop a direct combinatorial argument that quadratic generation implies condition (E), making condition (E) redundant.
title: Quadratic Generation Implies Clique-Face Property Without Condition (E)

description: Let F be a continuum arising as a quotient of a projective Fraïssé limit 𝔽 = lim(F), and let G be a closed subgroup of Homeo(F) such that Aut(𝔽) is dense in G. Then the universal minimal flow M(G) is metrizable if and only if G is extremely amenable. Equivalently: if the projective Fraïssé category F fails the approximate Ramsey property, then M(G) is non-metrizable. This extends the paper's result for the pseudo-solenoid to all continua arising from projective Fraïssé limits.
proof_strategy: The forward direction (extremely amenable ⟹ UMF metrizable) is trivial since M(G) is a singleton. For the reverse direction, assume M(G) is metrizable but G is not extremely amenable. By the paper's main theorem, the associated projective Fraïssé category F lacks the approximate Ramsey property. One must show this forces M(G) to be non-metrizable by analyzing the combinatorial structure of F's failure of ARP: construct an uncountable family of minimal subflows indexed by a perfect set of colorings that cannot be collapsed, leveraging the projective Fraïssé structure to embed the Cantor set into the flow's topology. This mirrors the pseudo-solenoid argument but requires a general construction from any ARP failure.
title: Metrizability Dichotomy for Universal Minimal Flows of Homeomorphism Groups of Projective Fraïssé Continua

description: A convex polytope P has the clique-face property if every clique of its 1-skeleton is the vertex set of a face of P. The paper verifies that every simple polytope has the clique-face property, meaning any clique of vertices in a simple polytope forms a simplex face.
proof_strategy: For a simple d-polytope, each vertex is the intersection of exactly d facets. A clique of size k in the 1-skeleton implies that any two vertices share an edge, which is the intersection of d-1 facets. By considering the intersection of the d - (k - 1) common facets containing all vertices of the clique, we get a face of dimension k - 1. The clique forms a complete graph K_k within this (k-1)-dimensional face. Since any (k-1)-dimensional face of a simple polytope is simple, its 1-skeleton has maximum degree k - 1. The presence of K_k forces this face to be a simplex, hence the clique is exactly the vertex set of this simplex face.
title: Clique-face property of simple polytopes

description: For every ε > 0, there exist N ∈ ℕ and δ > 0 such that for all n ≥ N, every K_5-free graph on n vertices with independence number at most δn can be made bipartite by removing at most (1/18 + ε) · n² edges. This formalizes the main result of the paper: the optimal constant for the bipartite deletion number of K_5-free graphs with sublinear independence number is exactly 1/18.
proof_strategy: The formalization should proceed in three stages: (1) formalize the basic framework of bipartite deletion numbers D₂(n, H) and independence number constraints; (2) formalize the flag algebra computational component, which requires certifying semidefinite programs (this is the hardest part—likely requiring a verified certificate checker or external computation trusted via IO); (3) combine the stability analysis (structural characterization of near-extremal graphs) with the flag algebra bounds to establish that no K_5-free graph with sublinear independence number requires deleting more than n²(1/18 + o(1)) edges to become bipartite. The lower bound construction (balanced blow-up of a specific weighted graph) should be formalized separately to establish tightness.
title: Bipartite deletion number for K_5-free graphs with sublinear independence number

description: Let F be a projective Fraïssé category with limit 𝔽 whose quotient by the inherited equivalence relation yields a continuum F, and let G be a closed subgroup of Homeo(F) with Aut(𝔽) dense in G. Then the universal minimal flow M(G) is metrizable if and only if there exists a precompact expansion F' of F (in the sense of an enriched projective Fraïssé category whose forgetful functor back to F is precompact) such that F' has the approximate Ramsey property and the automorphism group of the limit of F' is dense in G. This is the projective Fraïssé analog of the Kechris–Pestov–Todorcevic metrization theorem for universal minimal flows.
proof_strategy: The forward direction mirrors the KPT metrization strategy: assuming M(G) is metrizable, construct a precompact expansion F' of F by encoding the metrizable flow structure into the combinatorial data of the projective Fraïssé category, then verify the approximate Ramsey property via an ultrahomogeneity argument on the expanded limit. The reverse direction follows the pattern of this paper: given F' with the approximate Ramsey property, use the main theorem to conclude extreme amenability of an expanded group, then apply the precompactness condition to show the original group G has a metrizable universal minimal flow obtained as a quotient of the expanded group's singleton flow.
title: Projective Fraïssé Metrization Conjecture for Universal Minimal Flows

description: For every prime power q and every rank r ≥ 1, there exists n₀ such that for all n ≥ n₀, at least half of all q-matroids on 𝔽_q^n of rank r are sparse-paving. This is the q-analogue of the long-standing conjecture in classical matroid theory that most matroids are sparse-paving, and directly addresses the asymptotic growth questions identified in the paper's gap analysis between lower and upper bounds.
proof_strategy: Adapt the entropy-based counting framework developed in the paper to show non-sparse-paving q-matroids are exponentially fewer than sparse-paving ones. Key steps: (1) formalize that a q-matroid is sparse-paving iff every r-dimensional subspace is either a basis or a circuit; (2) use the contraction-closure property of the class of non-sparse-paving q-matroids to apply the entropy method; (3) establish that the dependent hyperplane structure of non-sparse-paving q-matroids reduces their count below 2^{(1-o(1))·[n choose r]_q / (q^r - 1)}, which is the lower bound for sparse-paving q-matroids from constant-dimension code constructions.
title: Most q-Matroids Are Sparse-Paving

description: For every matroid M on a finite ground set E with base set B, the toric ideal I_{P_M} of the matroid base polytope P_M is generated by quadratic binomials. Since the paper proves that matroid base polytopes satisfy the clique-face property, and for edge polytopes and cut polytopes the clique-face property is equivalent to quadratic toric ideal generation, this conjecture asserts that the equivalence extends: matroid base polytopes, which have the clique-face property, also have quadratically generated toric ideals.
proof_strategy: Leverage the clique-face property of matroid base polytopes (already established in the paper) combined with condition (E)-type characterizations. Show that every binomial in I_{P_M} of degree ≥ 3 is reducible modulo quadratic binomials arising from basis exchanges (symmetric exchanges of single elements between bases B1, B2), using the facial structure guaranteed by the clique-face property to construct degree-2 reductions.
title: Quadratic Generation of Toric Ideals of Matroid Base Polytopes

description: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a projective Fraïssé category with projective Fraïssé limit $\mathbb{F}$ and continuum $F = \mathbb{F}/R^\mathbb{F}$, such that $\text{Aut}(\mathbb{F})$ is dense in a closed subgroup $G \le \text{Homeo}(F)$. We conjecture that the universal minimal flow of $G$ is metrizable if and only if there exists an expansion of $\mathcal{F}$ by a linear order that has the approximate Ramsey property.
proof_strategy: Generalize the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence for non-archimedean Polish groups to projective Fraïssé categories. Construct a metrizable universal minimal flow as the completion of the orbit space of the limit of the ordered expansion, and conversely, show that a metrizable universal minimal flow induces a well-behaved linear order expansion satisfying the approximate Ramsey property.
title: Metrizable Universal Minimal Flows and the Ordered Approximate Ramsey Property for Projective Fraïssé Categories

description: Let G be a topological group and H ≤ G a dense subgroup with the subspace topology. If H is extremely amenable, meaning every continuous action of H on a nonempty compact Hausdorff space has a fixed point, then G is extremely amenable. This isolates the density step used when passing from the automorphism group of a projective Fraisse limit to the closure subgroup of the homeomorphism group of the quotient continuum.
domain_bridges: projective Fraisse limits to homeomorphism groups
combinatorial Ramsey properties to fixed point properties of compact flows
dense automorphism groups to closed homeomorphism groups
proof_strategy: Given a continuous G-action on a nonempty compact Hausdorff space X, restrict it to the dense subgroup H. Extreme amenability of H gives x ∈ X fixed by every h ∈ H. For arbitrary g ∈ G, the orbit map a ↦ a • x is continuous, and the equalizer of this map with the constant map a ↦ x is closed in G because X is Hausdorff. This closed set contains the dense subset H, hence is all of G. Therefore g • x = x for every g ∈ G.
title: Extreme amenability passes from a dense subgroup to its ambient topological group

description: For any ε > 0, there exists δ > 0 and N such that for any K_5-free n-vertex graph (n >= N) with independence number ≤ δn, there exists a bipartition of vertices such that at most (1/18 + ε)n^2 edges have both endpoints in the same part.
proof_strategy: Formalize the asymptotic bounds using epsilon-delta definitions. Extract and verify the flag algebra certificates within Lean for the finite core lemmas, and translate the edge-weighted Turán-type extensions into purely combinatorial bounds.
title: Ramsey-Turán Bipartite Cut for K5-free Graphs

description: For any fixed prime power q and fixed rank r ≥ 1, the proportion of q-matroids of rank r on F_q^n that are sparse-paving approaches 1 as n → ∞. Formally: if m_q(n,r) denotes the number of q-matroids and sp_q(n,r) the number of sparse-paving q-matroids on F_q^n with rank r, then sp_q(n,r)/m_q(n,r) → 1 as n → ∞. This is the q-analogue of the classical conjecture that almost all matroids are sparse-paving, and directly addresses the asymptotic gap identified in the paper between lower bounds (from sparse-paving constructions via constant-dimension codes) and upper bounds (from entropy and hyperplane-counting arguments).
proof_strategy: Follow the blueprint of the classical result by Keevash (and earlier partial results). The lower bound sp_q(n,r)/m_q(n,r) ≥ 1 - ε(n) requires showing that non-sparse-paving q-matroids are negligible, likely via entropy-based counting (as developed in the paper) combined with a q-analogue of the packing arguments for dependent hyperplane configurations. The key step is establishing that the number of q-matroids with a non-circuit dependent flat of rank < r-1 is exponentially smaller than the number of sparse-paving q-matroids, leveraging the Gaussian binomial structure of the subspace lattice.
title: Almost all q-matroids are sparse-paving

description: For any (0,1)-polytope P, the toric ideal I_P is generated by quadratic binomials if and only if P has the clique-face property (every clique of the 1-skeleton of P is the vertex set of a face of P). The forward direction is established in the paper; the converse remains open.
proof_strategy: The forward direction (quadratic generation implies clique-face property for (0,1)-polytopes) is proven in the paper using the mild edge condition. For the converse, one must show that the clique-face property forces all binomial relations in the toric ideal to be consequences of quadratic ones. This likely requires developing a Gröbner basis argument showing that higher-degree binomials in I_P are reducible by quadratic binomials when P has the clique-face property, leveraging the combinatorial structure of faces to control S-polynomial reductions.
title: Quadratic Generation Equivalence for (0,1)-Polytopes

description: For any two line arrangements A and A' in P^2 consisting of d ≤ 8 lines, if their intersection lattices L(A) and L(A') are isomorphic, then the graded Betti numbers of the minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras M(f) and M(f') are identical. Equivalently, there are no Ziegler pairs of line arrangements with d ≤ 8. This is the main result of the paper, establishing that d = 9 is the minimal degree for which Ziegler pairs can exist.
proof_strategy: The proof requires formalizing: (1) line arrangements as products of linear forms in C[x,y,z], (2) intersection lattices as ranked atomistic lattices recording incidence structure, (3) Milnor algebras S/J_f as graded quotients, (4) minimal graded free resolutions and Betti numbers. The key step is an exhaustive case analysis showing that for d ≤ 8, the intersection lattice uniquely determines the exponent sequence of the module of Jacobian syzygies AR(f). The classical Ziegler pair at d=9 shows this bound is tight.
title: No Ziegler pairs exist for line arrangements of degree at most 8

description: The homeomorphism group of the Menger universal curve is extremely amenable. By the paper's characterization theorem, this is equivalent to the projective Fraïssé category whose limit yields the Menger curve having the approximate Ramsey property. This would extend the known extreme amenability result for the pseudo-arc homeomorphism group to the one-dimensional Menger curve, the natural one-dimensional analog of the Cantor set, and would contrast with the paper's result that the homeomorphism group of the pseudo-solenoid has a non-metrizable universal minimal flow.
proof_strategy: Construct a projective Fraïssé category of finite graphs whose projective Fraïssé limit, quotiented by the canonical equivalence relation, yields the Menger universal curve. Then establish the approximate Ramsey property for this category by proving that for every finite graph A in the category and every ε > 0, there exists a finite graph B such that for any 2-coloring of copies of A in B, there exists a copy of A on which the coloring is ε-approximately monochromatic. This requires adapting the combinatorial partition arguments from the pseudo-arc case to handle the one-dimensional connectivity structure of the Menger curve approximants.
title: Extreme Amenability of the Menger Universal Curve Homeomorphism Group

description: For every composite integer m ≥ 6, there exist distinct positive integers a, b with ab = m and polynomials P₁, P₂ with non-negative integer coefficients such that P₁(1) = a², P₂(1) = b², and P₁·P₂ = (x + x² + ··· + xᵐ)². Equivalently, there exists a (2,m)-solution consisting of two dice with different square numbers of sides (a² and b²) that reproduce the sum frequency of two standard m-sided dice.
proof_strategy: Factor the frequency polynomial (x(xᵐ−1)/(x−1))² into cyclotomic components Φ_d(x)². For each valid factorization m = ab with a ≠ b, attempt to redistribute the cyclotomic factors into two groups such that the resulting polynomials P₁, P₂ have non-negative coefficients, evaluate to a² and b² respectively at x = 1, and satisfy the degree constraints. The cyclotomic factorization provides a finite search space for each m; the challenge is proving existence uniformly.
title: Existence of Square-Sided Sicherman Pairs for All Composite m ≥ 6

description: If the toric ideal of a (0,1)-polytope is generated by quadratic binomials, then the polytope possesses the clique-face property, meaning every clique of its 1-skeleton forms the vertex set of a face.
proof_strategy: Formalize (0,1)-polytopes, their 1-skeletons as graphs, toric ideals as kernels of specific ring homomorphisms, and the property of being quadratically generated. Then establish that quadratic generation implies every clique in the 1-skeleton corresponds to a face of the polytope.
title: Clique-Face Property for Quadratic (0,1)-Polytopes

description: For every integer d ≥ 9, there exist line arrangements A and A' in P²(C) of degree d with isomorphic intersection lattices L(A) ≅ L(A') but with different graded Betti numbers in the minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras M(f) and M(f'). This extends the known existence for d = 9 (the classical Ziegler pair) and d = 10 (six pairs constructed in the paper), and contrasts with the paper's result that for d < 9 the intersection lattice determines the exponent data.
domain_bridges: Commutative algebra of minimal free resolutions
Homological algebra of graded Betti numbers
proof_strategy: Construct infinite families of Ziegler pairs for all d ≥ 9 by extending the d = 9 and d = 10 examples using addition-deletion techniques for line arrangements, or by identifying suitable specialization/deformation families that preserve the intersection lattice while altering the minimal graded free resolution of the Milnor algebra. One approach: show that adding lines in specific configurations to known Ziegler pairs preserves the Ziegler pair property.
title: Universal Existence of Ziegler Pairs for Large Degrees

description: Every multigraph admits a linked, componental, rooted tree-cut decomposition of finite adhesion that displays all undominated edge-ends. This is the main theorem (Theorem 1.1) of the paper, asserting the existence of a well-behaved edge-connectivity decomposition that faithfully reflects the structure of undominated edge-ends of infinite graphs. The decomposition simultaneously ensures linkedness (Menger-type edge-connectivity between adhesion sets), componentality (connected parts), and a bijective correspondence between undominated edge-ends and ends of the decomposition tree.
domain_bridges: Topology of ends (end compactifications of locally finite graphs)
proof_strategy: First formalize the prerequisite infrastructure: multigraphs allowing parallel edges, edge-ends as equivalence classes of one-way infinite edge-sequences, undominated edge-ends, rooted tree-cut decompositions with adhesion sets, the natural map from edge-ends to the tree boundary, and the notions of linkedness, componentality, and displaying. The proof then proceeds by constructing the decomposition, likely via a maximal-separator argument or transfinite induction, and verifying linkedness using edge-connectivity (Menger-type) results. The key technical bridge is showing that the separability properties of undominated edge-ends combine with edge-connectivity to yield the linked property along tree-paths.
title: Linked tree-cut decompositions displaying undominated edge-ends

description: For every integer k ≥ 3 and every integer s ≥ 2, there exist k-graphs F₁, F₂, ..., Fₛ such that 0 < γ⁺({F₁, F₂, ..., Fₛ}) < min{γ⁺(F₁), γ⁺(F₂), ..., γ⁺(Fₛ)}. This generalizes the paper's Theorem 1.1 (which proves the case s = 2) and mirrors the analogous result established for codegree Turán density by Gao, Pikhurko, Rong, and Sun.
domain_bridges: Extremal combinatorics → Order theory (subadditivity of density functionals)
Hypergraph theory → Asymptotic analysis (limit definitions of densities)
proof_strategy: Inductive construction on family size s: use the s=2 case established in the paper as the base, then iteratively apply a substitution/amalgamation argument. For the inductive step, given a non-principal family of size s, combine it with an appropriately chosen auxiliary k-graph using the same blow-up and replacement techniques that work for s=2, ensuring the joint density drops below the minimum of all individual densities while remaining positive.
title: Arbitrary-size non-principal families for positive codegree Turán density

description: For a projective Fraïssé category $\mathcal{F}$ with limit $\mathbb{F}$, quotient continuum $F = \mathbb{F}/R^\mathbb{F}$, and a closed subgroup $G \le \operatorname{Homeo}(F)$ in which the image of $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{F})$ is dense, $G$ is extremely amenable if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ has the approximate Ramsey property.
proof_strategy: Formalize projective Fraïssé categories and their limits, define the approximate Ramsey property for morphisms, define extreme amenability for topological groups, and adapt the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic proof strategy to the projective setting by demonstrating that the universal minimal flow of the group is trivial precisely when the category satisfies the approximate Ramsey property.
title: Projective Fraïssé KPT Correspondence

description: For every integer k ≥ 2, there exists at least one unordered pair of dice (A, B) such that: (1) A and B together produce the same sum frequency distribution as two standard k²-sided dice (i.e., they form (2, k²)-solutions); (2) the number of sides of A and B are distinct perfect squares; and (3) neither A nor B is the standard k²-sided die. Equivalently, the generating function (x + x² + ⋯ + x^{k²})² admits at least one factorization P·Q where P(1) = a², Q(1) = b² for distinct positive integers a, b, both polynomials have non-negative integer coefficients, and neither P nor Q equals the standard die generating function.
proof_strategy: Use the cyclotomic polynomial factorization of the frequency polynomial F(x) = x²·((x^{k²} − 1)/(x − 1))². The factorization of F into irreducible cyclotomic components admits nontrivial rearrangements. Show that for each k ≥ 2, the divisor structure of k² always permits at least one regrouping of these cyclotomic factors into two polynomials P, Q with non-negative integer coefficients, where P(1) and Q(1) are distinct perfect squares. The key step leverages that k² has multiple distinct divisor pairs, and the cyclotomic factors of (x^{k²} − 1)/(x − 1) can be partitioned along these divisor boundaries to produce valid die-generating polynomials with square numbers of sides.
title: Existence of Square-Sided Sicherman-Type Pairs for All Perfect Square Die Sizes

description: For every odd base B > 3, the four-digit Kaprekar map has a unique nonconstant terminal cycle (i.e., a unique fixed point, as in the classical base-10 case where 6174 is the sole attractor) if and only if B−1 is a power of 2. This extends the paper's projective-doubling conjugacy by predicting that the orbit structure of multiplication-by-2 on P¹(Z/(B−1)Z) collapses to a single fixed point exactly when (B−1) is a power of 2, connecting Kaprekar dynamics to the multiplicative structure of (Z/nZ)×.
proof_strategy: Use the paper's result that the Kaprekar map on T_B is conjugate to projective doubling {[r],[s]} ↦ {[2r],[2s]} on P¹(Z/(B−1)Z). The number of terminal cycles equals the number of cycles of this projective doubling map. Analyze the orbit structure of multiplication by 2 on P¹(Z/nZ) via CRT decomposition: when n = 2^k, the group (Z/2^kZ)× and the {±1}-quotient force all orbits to collapse to a single fixed point. When n has an odd prime factor p, the action on P¹(Z/p^aZ) produces multiple orbits by properties of ord_p(2). The forward direction uses the specific structure of (Z/2^kZ)× ≅ Z/2 × Z/2^{k−2}; the backward direction uses that for odd prime p | (B−1), ord_p(2) > 1 produces distinct orbits under doubling.
title: Unique Kaprekar fixed point iff base-minus-one is a power of two

description: For any intersecting family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$ with $n > 10k$, the size of the family of symmetric differences $|\mathcal{SD}(\mathcal{F})|$ is at most $\sum_{\ell=0}^{k-1} \binom{n-1}{2\ell}$. Equality holds if and only if $\mathcal{F}$ is a full star.
proof_strategy: Extend the concentration inequality approach used for $n \ge 60k^{3/2}$ to tighter bounds, potentially by developing stronger variance bounds or refined shifting arguments, to cover the range $n > 10k$.
title: Frankl-Kiselev-Kupavskii Conjecture on Symmetric Differences

description: For any lattice polytope P, if its toric ideal is generated by quadratic binomials, then P possesses the clique-face property (i.e., every clique of the 1-skeleton of P is the vertex set of a face of P). The paper proves this under a mild condition on edges (condition (E)), and the general case is a natural extension.
proof_strategy: Analyze the structure of quadratic binomials in the toric ideal to show that any clique in the 1-skeleton must correspond to a face, potentially by adapting the local-to-global arguments used for (0,1)-polytopes satisfying condition (E) or by demonstrating that a minimal non-face clique would necessitate higher-degree generators.
title: Quadratic Toric Ideals Imply the Clique-Face Property

description: For any two line arrangements of at most 9 lines, if they have isomorphic intersection lattices, the same minimal degree of a Jacobian relation (condition MDR), and the same Hilbert function of the Milnor algebra (condition HF), then they must have the same graded Betti numbers. This implies that no Ziegler pair of line arrangements of degree d ≤ 9 satisfies both condition (MDR) and condition (HF), making degree 10 the minimal degree for such Ziegler pairs to exist.
proof_strategy: For d ≤ 8, the intersection lattice uniquely determines the exponent data (as proven in the paper), which in turn determines the Betti numbers, making the statement trivially hold. For d = 9, exhaustively verify that the only Ziegler pair (the classical pair) has different minimal degrees of Jacobian relations, thus failing condition (MDR), leaving no room for counterexamples.
title: Minimality of Degree 10 for MDR-HF Ziegler Pairs

description: Every finite multigraph admits a linked, componental, rooted tree-cut decomposition. This serves as the finite graph base case and direct analogue of the main theorem (Theorem 1.1) from the paper, which focuses on infinite graphs. The componental property ensures that each part of the decomposition induces a connected subgraph, and the linked property guarantees that the adhesion sets reflect the edge-connectivity of the underlying graph, extending the finite linked tree-cut decomposition results of Giannopoulou et al.
proof_strategy: Formalize finite multigraphs, tree-cut decompositions, adhesion sets, and the linked and componental properties. The proof would follow the finite combinatorial structure of Giannopoulou et al., using Menger's theorem to establish the linked property and an induction argument on the number of vertices to enforce the componental property.
title: Existence of Linked Componental Tree-Cut Decompositions for Finite Graphs

description: For any uniformity r ≥ 2 and number of vertices n ≥ 4r^2, there exists an r-uniform hypergraph on n vertices with at least (1/32)r^{-3} * (n choose r) edges such that every (r+1)-set of vertices spans exactly 0 or 2 edges.
proof_strategy: Construct the hypergraph explicitly (using an algebraic or probabilistic construction over finite fields/random tournaments as introduced in the paper) and then verify the edge count and the local 0-or-2 constraint via double counting and algebraic arguments.
title: Existence of Dense r-Graphs with 0 or 2 Edges per (r+1)-Set

description: For every continuum F arising as a quotient of a projective Fraïssé limit 𝔽 with Aut(𝔽) dense in Homeo(F), the universal minimal flow M(Homeo(F)) is either a singleton (i.e., Homeo(F) is extremely amenable) or is non-metrizable. This would generalize the pseudo-solenoid result and establish that no intermediate case exists where the universal minimal flow is metrizable but non-trivial.
proof_strategy: Assume for contradiction that M(Homeo(F)) is metrizable and non-trivial. Use the projective Fraïssé structure of 𝔽 to approximate the minimal flow by finite combinatorial data. Apply the approximate Ramsey property characterization: if the category lacks ARP, construct a witness to non-metrizability of the universal minimal flow via a Veech-type argument adapted to the non-locally-compact setting. The key step is showing that failure of ARP forces the universal minimal flow to have uncountable weight, leveraging the projective Fraïssé approximation hierarchy.
title: Dichotomy for Universal Minimal Flows of Homeomorphism Groups of Projective Fraïssé Limits

description: Conjecture that there are no two dice whose numbers of sides are distinct perfect squares (e.g., 4 and 9) whose generating functions multiply to the square of the standard 6‑sided dice generating function.
proof_strategy: Analyze the factorization of the standard sum generating function into cyclotomic polynomials and show that any factorization yielding perfect‑square side counts forces the side counts to be equal, contradicting the distinctness condition.
title: Non‑existence of square‑sided dice pairs for the 2‑dice standard sum problem

description: The paper proves that for every odd base B > 3, every nonconstant four-digit string reaches the triangular region T_B in at most 3 iterations of the Kaprekar map. This conjecture asserts that the bound of 3 is sharp: for every odd base B > 3, there exists a nonconstant four-digit string whose orbit requires exactly 3 iterations to enter T_B. This would complete the characterization of the pre-periodic behavior by showing no uniform improvement on the bound of 3 is possible across all odd bases.
proof_strategy: Construct, for each odd base B > 3, an explicit nonconstant four-digit string whose orbit under the Kaprekar map stays outside T_B for exactly 3 iterations. This requires a detailed analysis of the pre-periodic region (the complement of T_B in the space of sorted four-digit strings) and how the Kaprekar map acts on it. The projective doubling conjugacy on T_B may help characterize which pairs {r, s} lie outside T_B and how many iterations they need to reach T_B. A likely approach is to identify a family of strings parameterized by B (e.g., strings of the form (B-1, k, 0, 0) for suitable k) that systematically require 3 iterations.
title: Sharpness of the Kaprekar Pre-period Bound in Odd Bases

description: For every integer k ≥ 3 and integer s ≥ 2, there exists a finite family of k-graphs F = {F_1, ..., F_s} such that the positive codegree Turán density of F is strictly positive and strictly less than the minimum of the positive codegree Turán densities of the individual k-graphs in F. That is, 0 < γ⁺(F) < min_{i ∈ [s]} γ⁺(F_i).
proof_strategy: Generalize the size-2 construction to arbitrary size s by iteratively adding forbidden configurations that strictly decrease the positive codegree Turán density without driving it to zero, adapting the techniques used for standard and codegree Turán densities in prior work.
title: Strong non-principality of positive codegree density for arbitrary family sizes

description: Formalize Conway's surreal numbers as a universally embedding ordered field containing the reals and the ordinals, with recursive definitions of arithmetic (+, x, order), the birthday construction, and the embedding of dyadic rationals. (Conway, On Numbers and Games 1976)
title: Conway Surreal Numbers: The Universal Ordered Field

description: Find an Euler brick whose space diagonal is also an integer, or prove none exists. Formalize the parametric families of near-misses and connect to Diophantine equations on algebraic surfaces.
title: Perfect Cuboid (Euler Brick)

description: Extend results on quadratic forms to arbitrary algebraic number fields. Formalize the Hasse-Minkowski theorem and explore the classification of quadratic forms over number fields via class field theory.
title: Hilbert 11: Quadratic Forms over Algebraic Fields

description: Prove that for every finite union-closed family of sets (not all empty), some element belongs to at least half the sets. Formalize the lattice-theoretic reformulation and known partial results.
title: Frankl's Union-Closed Conjecture

description: Characterize numbers representable as a sum of three squares of primes. Formalize the circle method approach to ternary Goldbach-type problems for squares.
title: Legendre's Three-Square Theorem Extension

description: Prove that for every polynomial with all roots in the closed unit disk, every root has a critical point within distance 1 of it. Formalize known partial results and the connection to Gauss-Lucas.
title: Sendov's Conjecture

description: Formalize the Euler-Mascheroni constant γ = lim(H_n - ln n). Prove key integral representations and series accelerations. Establish Apéry-like sequences that provide good rational approximations. Explore connections to the Stieltjes constants.
title: Euler-Mascheroni Constant: Irrationality Approaches

description: Formalize Frankl's conjecture and prove it for families of size ≤ 50 (Bošnjak-Marković). Prove the conjecture for families with a 3-element universe. Formalize the lattice-theoretic reformulation and Reimer's entropy approach.
title: Frankl's Union-Closed Conjecture: Partial Results

description: Formalize the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis: all non-trivial zeros of every Dirichlet L-function (and Dedekind zeta functions) have real part 1/2. Derive its consequences (primality in P, deterministic Miller, class-number bounds). (Riemann 1859, generalized)
title: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH)

description: Formalize a mathematically consistent framework for quantum gravity: reconcile general relativity (a classical Lorentzian geometric theory) with quantum field theory, e.g., via loop/LQG discreteness, AdS/CFT holographic correspondence, or string-theory compactifications. (open)
title: Mathematical Framework of Quantum Gravity

description: Formalize the smooth 4D Poincare conjecture: every smooth compact 4-manifold homotopy-equivalent to S^4 is diffeomorphic to S^4. Distinguish from the topological case (Freedman, true) and study exotic 4-sphere candidates. (Freedman 1982; smooth case open)
title: Smooth 4-Dimensional Poincare Conjecture

description: Formalize Valiant's algebraic complexity classes VP and VNP, prove the permanent is VNP-complete, and attack the conjecture that the permanent requires super-polynomial-size algebraic circuits (VP != VNP), the algebraic analogue of P != NP. (Valiant 1979)
title: Permanent vs Determinant: VP != VNP (Valiant)

description: Determine whether Lehmer's polynomial has the smallest Mahler measure among non-cyclotomic polynomials. Formalize the Mahler measure and its connections to heights, entropy, and algebraic dynamics.
title: Lehmer's Mahler Measure Problem

description: Prove that every tree admits a graceful labeling. Formalize known results for paths, caterpillars, and olive trees. Explore connections to decompositions of complete graphs.
title: Graceful Tree Conjecture

description: Formalize Asimov's psychohistory as a law-of-large-numbers theorem for large agent populations: under suitable aggregation, macroscopic population trajectories become predictable with variance shrinking in population size, analogous to the kinetic theory of gases. (Asimov, Foundation 1951)
title: Asimov Psychohistory: Statistical Mechanics of Large Populations

description: Formalize the BSS model of computation over the reals: define P_R and NP_R, and prove NP_R-completeness of deciding whether a system of real polynomials of degree 4 has a real root (the BSS analog of SAT). (Blum-Shub-Smale 1989)
title: Blum-Shub-Smale Real Computation: P_R, NP_R, and 4th-Degree Roots

description: Formalize Egan's Dust Theory from Permutation City: the thesis that consciousness is an abstract computable pattern whose scattered information states, embedded anywhere in spacetime, suffice for continuous subjective experience — a substrate-independence theorem for computational patterns. (Egan, Permutation City 1994)
title: Egan Dust Theory: Consciousness as Substrate-Independent Pattern

description: Formalize Hamkins-Lewis infinite-time Turing machines (ITTMs): computation through transfinite ordinal stages with limit-rules, prove ITTMs decide all hyperarithmetic sets and solve the classical halting problem, and characterize the decidable sets (semi-decidable / decidable) of ITTM theory. (Hamkins & Lewis 1998)
title: Infinite-Time Turing Machines: Transfinite Computability

description: Find a formula for the probability that two elements chosen uniformly at random generate the symmetric group S_n. Formalize known asymptotic results and connect to the theory of random permutations.
title: Symmetric Group Generation Probability

description: Resolve whether the general 7th-degree equation can be solved using functions of only 2 variables. Formalize Kolmogorov's superposition theorem and explore its implications for approximation theory.
title: Hilbert 13: 7th-Degree Equations via 2-Variable Functions

description: Formalize Hilbert's 12th problem: generalize the Kronecker-Weber theorem (every abelian extension of Q is in a cyclotomic field) to explicit generators of abelian extensions of arbitrary number fields (complex multiplication for imaginary quadratic; open for real/quadratic+). (Hilbert 1900)
title: Hilbert 12th: Explicit Class Field Theory

description: Formalize the inverse Galois problem: every finite group occurs as the Galois group of a Galois extension of Q. Prove it for solvable groups (Shafarevich) and attack non-solvable families (e.g., sporadic groups, M23). (Dedekind/Hilbert 1892)
title: Inverse Galois Problem: Every Finite Group over Q

description: Formalize the Kakeya conjecture: any subset of R^n containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff (and Minkowski) dimension n. Prove the partial Dvir finite-field analogue and the known n >= 5 results. (Besicovitch 1919; Dvir 2008)
title: Kakeya Conjecture: Dimension of Direction-Containing Sets

description: Formalize Schanuel's conjecture: for Q-linearly independent z_1,...,z_n, the transcendence degree of Q(z_i, e^{z_i}) over Q is at least n. Derive its consequences (Lindemann-Weierstrass, Gelfond-Schneider, e and pi algebraic independence). (Schanuel 1966)
title: Schanuel's Conjecture: Transcendence Degree of Exponential Fields

description: Prove that for every integer n ≥ 2, the fraction 4/n can be written as a sum of three unit fractions. Formalize computational verification and parametric families of solutions.
title: Erdős–Straus Conjecture

description: Formalize the consciousness-upload thought experiment (Black Mirror 'White Christmas'): Parfit's psychological-continuity criterion for personal identity across substrate transfer, the copy-divergence problem (two replicas diverge post-copy), and identity-persistence under state forks. (Black Mirror 2014, Parfit)
title: Black Mirror 'Cookie' Upload: Parfit Psychological Continuity

description: Formalize the Conway-Kochen Free Will Theorem: from the SPIN, TWIN, and FIN axioms of quantum mechanics, prove that if an experimenter is free to choose measurement settings, then particles possess free will (non-deterministic response). (Conway-Kochen 2006)
title: Conway-Kochen Free Will Theorem

description: Formalize the Cubitt et al. result that the spectral-gap problem for translation-invariant local quantum many-body Hamiltonians is algorithmically undecidable in the thermodynamic limit, by reducing the halting problem to gap-vs-gapless via aperiodic tiling encodings. (Cubitt-Perez-Garcia-Wolfson 2015)
title: Spectral Gap Undecidability (Cubitt-Perez-Garcia-Wolfson)

description: Formalize Hilbert's 16th problem (second part): bound the number and relative positions of limit cycles of a planar polynomial vector field of degree d (Hilbert number H(d)). Establish the known quadratic bound and attack the general bound. (Hilbert 1900)
title: Hilbert 16th: Limit Cycles of Polynomial Vector Fields

description: Formalize the matrix multiplication exponent omega (inf over exponents achieving O(n^omega) multiplication); verify the current bound omega < 2.371339 and attempt the moonshot omega = 2 via laser/_group-theoretic methods. (Le Gall-Urrutia, Alman-Williams 2024)
title: Matrix Multiplication Exponent omega: Prove omega = 2?

description: Formalize Mulmuley's Geometric Complexity Theory program: represent determinant and permanent orbit closures via representation theory of GL_n, and construct explicit representation-theoretic 'obstructions' proving VP != VNP. (Mulmuley 2001)
title: Geometric Complexity Theory: Obstructions Separating VP and VNP

description: Formalize Schinzel's Hypothesis H: any finite set of irreducible integer polynomials with no fixed prime divisor simultaneously take prime values for infinitely many n (the twin-prime and Sophie-Germain conjectures are special cases). (Schinzel 1958)
title: Schinzel's Hypothesis H: Simultaneous Prime Values

description: Formalize Woodin's Ultimate-L program: an inner model compatible with large cardinals that would decide the Continuum Hypothesis, and the hierarchy of large cardinal axioms (measurable, Woodin, supercompact) gaugeing consistency strength. (Woodin)
title: Woodin's Ultimate-L and Large Cardinal Axioms
