# Future Directions — Crystallographic Groups and Music: The Wallpaper Groups of Rhythm

This cycle established a self-contained theory of the **symmetry groups of cyclic
rhythms** via the dihedral action of `DihedralGroup n` on `Finset (ZMod n)`
(beat positions), proved in:

* `Catalog/Computation/RhythmWallpaperGroups.lean`
  - `card_symmetryGroup_dvd` — Lagrange: `|symmetryGroup S| ∣ 2n`.
  - `card_rotationPeriods_dvd` — rhythmic crystallographic restriction: `|rotationPeriods S| ∣ n`.
  - `rotationPeriods_realizable` — every divisor `d ∣ n` is realised as a rotation-symmetry order.
* `Catalog/Computation/RhythmScaleSymmetry.lean`
  - `card_transpositions_mul_card_rotPeriods` — orbit–stabiliser: `#transpositions · #periods = n`.
  - `decide`-verified symmetry orders of the whole-tone (6), augmented (3),
    octatonic (4), diatonic (1), and chromatic (12) pitch-class sets in `ZMod 12`.

The following conjectures are precise, falsifiable, and computationally testable
for small `n` (via `decide`) before any general proof attempt.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Full dihedral realisability)
**Every subgroup `H ≤ DihedralGroup n` is the symmetry group of some rhythm.**
That is, `∀ H : Subgroup (DihedralGroup n), ∃ S : Finset (ZMod n), symmetryGroup n S = H`.
This strengthens `rotationPeriods_realizable` (which only realises the *rotation*
orders) to the full dihedral lattice, including reflection (palindromic) symmetry.
*Test*: enumerate subgroups of `DihedralGroup n` for `n ≤ 8` and search for a
realising `S` by `decide`. *Risk*: small `n` may have unrealisable subgroups
(e.g. a lone reflection with no compatible rotation), in which case the corrected
conjecture characterises the realisable ones as exactly the stabiliser-closed
subgroups.

## Conjecture 2 (Möbius enumeration of rhythmic crystal classes)
**The number of rhythms in `ZMod n` whose rotation-period group has order exactly
`d` (for `d ∣ n`) is `∑_{e ∣ (n/d)} μ(e) · 2^{(n/d)/e · ... }`** — i.e. a clean
Möbius-inversion / necklace-counting formula governs the distribution of symmetry
orders. Concretely, with `Aₙ(d)` = #{S : rotPeriodsFinset n S |>.card = d}, conjecture
`∑_{d ∣ n} Aₙ(d) = 2ⁿ` (trivial) **and** that `Aₙ(d)` is given by Möbius inversion
of `d ↦ 2^{n/d}`. *Test*: tabulate `Aₙ(d)` by brute force (`decide`) for `n ≤ 12`
and fit against the Möbius formula.

## Conjecture 3 (Two-dimensional polyrhythms and the genuine 17 wallpaper groups)
**Define rhythms on the torus `ZMod m × ZMod n` with the full planar
crystallographic action (translations, the rotation `(x,y) ↦ (-x,-y)`, and the
reflections), and conjecture that exactly the toroidal quotients of the 17
wallpaper groups arise as symmetry groups.** This is the literal realisation of
the project title: 1D rhythm gave dihedral (frieze-like) symmetry; the 2D
polyrhythmic grid should expose wallpaper-group structure. *Test*: build the
`MulAction` of the relevant point group on `Finset (ZMod m × ZMod n)` and
classify stabilisers for small `m, n` by `decide`.

## Conjecture 4 (Euclidean / maximally even rhythms)
**The Euclidean rhythm `E(k, n)` (the maximally even distribution of `k` onsets in
`n` beats, à la Bjorklund) has rotation-period group of order exactly `gcd(k, n)`.**
Equivalently it has `n / gcd(k,n)` distinct transpositions. *Test*: implement
`E(k,n)` as a `Finset (ZMod n)` and check `rotPeriodsFinset n (E k n) |>.card = Nat.gcd k n`
by `decide` for all `k ≤ n ≤ 16`. A proof would connect our orbit–stabiliser law
to the three-distance/Steinhaus theorem.

## Conjecture 5 (Spectral characterisation of rhythmic symmetry)
**A rhythm `S ⊆ ZMod n` has rotation-period group of order `d` (with `d ∣ n`) iff
its discrete Fourier transform `Ŝ` (the indicator's DFT over `ZMod n`) is supported
on the subgroup of multiples of `n/d`.** This recasts the crystallographic
restriction as a frequency-support statement (a Computation-domain bridge to the
number-theoretic transform / `Polynomial (ZMod n)` evaluation). *Test*: for
`n ≤ 12`, compute supports of `Ŝ` and compare with `rotPeriodsFinset` by `decide`
over `ℚ`-valued or root-of-unity DFTs.

# Future Directions — Retrocausal Mathematics: Where Effects Precede Causes

Derived from this cycle's verified results in
`Catalog/Logic/RetrocausalHeyting.lean` and `Catalog/Bridges/RetrocausalCPTBridge.lean`.

This cycle established three load-bearing facts:
- **(TEM)** The temporal excluded middle `(a ∨ ¬a)ᶜᶜ = ⊤` holds in *every* Heyting
  algebra (`temporal_excluded_middle`).
- **(LEM↔DNE)** Rejecting the law of excluded middle is *equivalent* to rejecting
  double-negation elimination (`lem_iff_dne`) — so any LEM-free logic is genuinely
  intuitionistic.
- **(CPT bridge)** An Osterwalder–Schrader time reflection `θ` (`θ ∘ θ = id`) composed
  with negation is an order-reversing involution, making the QFT proposition algebra a
  `RetrocausalHeyting` whose De Morgan laws are the abstract Logic lemmas
  (`cpt_yields_retrocausal_logic`).

---

## Conjecture 1 — Retrocausal Glivenko transfer for sequent provability
A formula `φ` is provable in a retrocausal (intuitionistic) sequent calculus equipped
with a time-reversal involution iff its CPT-double-negation `(φ ∨ ¬φ)ᶜᶜ`-closure is
provable classically, and the time-reversal acts as a provability-preserving De Morgan
duality on the Lindenbaum–Tarski algebra.

- **The key insight is...** that `temporal_excluded_middle` shows the *doubly negated*
  excluded middle is a theorem rather than an axiom, so Glivenko's theorem should lift to
  the retrocausal setting with the involution `rev` permuting the De Morgan dual pair.
- **Why now?** We already have `lem_iff_dne` and `rev_sup`/`rev_inf` proved with 0
  sorries; the Lindenbaum–Tarski algebra is a Heyting algebra, so the transfer is a
  finite step from the present lemmas.

## Conjecture 2 — Fixed points of CPT reversal are a Boolean subalgebra
For a reflection-positive QFT, the propositions fixed by the CPT connective
`cptReversal R S = S` form a sublattice on which the law of excluded middle is restored,
i.e. a maximal *classical* island inside the retrocausal logic.

- **The key insight is...** that `cptReversal_involutive` gives a `ℤ/2` action whose
  fixed-point set of an antitone involution is closed under the De Morgan-swapped
  operations `rev_sup`/`rev_inf`, forcing self-duality and hence Boolean behaviour.
- **Why now?** The involution and its De Morgan laws are already verified on `Set V`;
  characterizing `{S : cptReversal R S = S}` only requires the fixed-point algebra of an
  existing involution.

## Conjecture 3 — LEM-failure is a strict obstruction to Boolean carriers
Every retrocausal Heyting algebra in which LEM fails at even one element is necessarily
non-Boolean, and conversely the `Fin (n+3)` chains give an infinite family of
LEM-failing retrocausal algebras with strictly growing failure sets.

- **The key insight is...** that `lem_fails_of_dne_fails` ties LEM failure to genuine
  intuitionism (DNE failure), and the explicit `Fin 3` model (`retro_lem_fails`) already
  realizes one failure point with a working time-reversal instance.
- **Why now?** The `Fin 3` `RetrocausalHeyting` instance is already constructed; the
  generalization to `Fin (n+3)` is a parametric replay of the same `fin_cases` proofs.

## Conjecture 4 — Reflection positivity bounds the "retrocausal defect"
For a reflection-positive form `R`, the quantity measuring how far a proposition is from
CPT-self-duality is controlled by the physical pairing `B (θ v) v ≥ 0`; positivity of the
form bounds the size of the non-classical (LEM-violating) region of the induced logic.

- **The key insight is...** that `cpt_yields_retrocausal_logic` already couples the
  physics inequality `reflection_pos` with the logical involution in one statement;
  promoting the conjunction to a quantitative inequality links OS positivity to logical
  non-classicality.
- **Why now?** Both halves (the inequality and the involution) are proved and live in the
  same theorem; only a measure of "defect" must be defined to state the bound.

## Conjecture 5 — Cryptographic one-way functions from retrocausal asymmetry
The order-asymmetry of a retrocausal involution (forward implications are *not* recoverable
from backward ones unless the algebra is Boolean) yields a logical hardness gap that can
seed a commitment scheme: committing in "forward time" and opening in "reversed time" is
binding precisely because LEM fails.

- **The key insight is...** that `lem_iff_dne` makes non-recoverability of `aᶜᶜ ↦ a`
  equivalent to LEM failure, so a non-Boolean retrocausal carrier provides an
  *information-theoretic* (not merely computational) one-way asymmetry.
- **Why now?** The equivalence and an explicit non-Boolean model are already formalized;
  the Cryptography catalog (`Catalog/Cryptography/`) has the commitment/hardness scaffolding
  to host the construction.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Mind vs Gödel: Can Minds Outperform Algorithms?

This cycle established (`Catalog/Logic/MindVersusGodel.lean`, 0 sorries) a four-layer,
fully verified abstract account of the Lucas–Penrose question:

- **Layer 1** — `lawvere_fixed_point` / `no_surjection_to_predicates`: the single
  fixed-point fact underlying every diagonal argument.
- **Layer 2** — `FormalSystem`, `GodelSentence`, `godel_true_unprovable`,
  `godel_neg_unprovable`, `FormalSystem.consistent`: semantic incompleteness with
  consistency derived as a theorem.
- **Layer 3** — `mindSystem`, `mind_still_incomplete`, `ReflectionTower`,
  `tower_strict_mono`, `tower_no_level_complete`, `tower_limit_complete`,
  `mind_vs_godel_synthesis`: the ω-reflection ladder. A mind beats any *single*
  algorithm by one rung but never the whole class.
- **Layer 4** — `bool_diagonal`, `no_halting_decider`, `truth_undefinable`,
  `mind_is_not_one_algorithm`: Gödel/Tarski/Turing unified as one Boolean diagonal.

The conjectures below are precise enough to be stated as Lean theorems and either
proved or refuted in a follow-up cycle.

## Conjecture 1 — Ordinal reflection strictly dominates ω-reflection
Replace `ReflectionTower : ℕ → …` by a tower indexed by a countable ordinal notation
system `O`. Conjecture: for every recursive ordinal α there is a sentence provable at
level α+1 but at no level β ≤ α, and the union over all recursive ordinals is *still*
incomplete (a fresh diagonal sentence escapes). **Falsifiable form:** exhibit a recursive
ordinal-indexed `Provable : O → S → Prop` with `tower_strict_mono` at every successor and
a global incompleteness witness; or prove no such strictly increasing recursive tower can
have an incompleteness witness at its supremum.

## Conjecture 2 — Soundness is the exact currency of the mind's advantage
In `mindSystem` the mind gains the Gödel sentence *because it asserts soundness*. Conjecture:
an algorithm granted an oracle for `Con(F)` (consistency of `F`) proves exactly the same new
sentence, i.e. `mindProv F G ⊆ ProvFromConsistencyOracle F`. **Falsifiable form:** define a
`FormalSystem` extension `F + Con(F)` and prove `G.g` is provable there, establishing that
the mind's "extra truth" is an *algorithmic* consequence of one consistency assumption — so
the advantage is relative, not absolute.

## Conjecture 3 — No fixed point of the reflection operator is complete
Let `R : FormalSystem → FormalSystem` be the reflective extension operator (Layer 3). Conjecture:
if `F` admits a Gödel sentence and `R F ≅ F` (a fixed point of reflection), then `F` is
inconsistent. I.e. the only "self-reflectively closed" sound systems are exactly the ones with
no diagonal sentence (too weak to be interesting). **Falsifiable form:** prove
`(∀ G, RF.Prov = F.Prov) → ¬ Nonempty (GodelSentence F)` for sound `F`, or build a sound,
diagonal-admitting fixed point as a counterexample.

## Conjecture 4 — Quantitative diagonal gap
Generalize `bool_diagonal` from `Bool` to a finite valuation type `Fin k` with a
fixed-point-free permutation `σ`. Conjecture: an evaluator `eval : α → α → Fin k` avoids the
σ-diagonal on a set of "rows" of measure (counting) at most `1 − 1/k` — i.e. the diagonal
defeats a `1/k` fraction of any finite candidate table. **Falsifiable form:** for finite `α`,
prove `#{ m | ∀ x, eval m x = σ (eval x x)} = 0` and, dually, bound how close a table can come.

## Conjecture 5 — Bridge to `ProofSystemCollapse` / `ParadoxSelfSoundness`
The catalog's `ParadoxSelfSoundness` shows paraconsistent theories *can* prove their own
soundness by tolerating `B`-valued dialetheias. Conjecture: a `FormalSystem` whose truth
valuation is Belnap-four-valued (replacing `neg_true` by `BelnapVal.neg`) admits a Gödel
sentence valued `B`, making `godel_true_unprovable` *vacuous* (the mind's "seeing" collapses).
**Falsifiable form:** define `BelnapFormalSystem`, port `godel_true_unprovable`, and prove the
fixed point is forced to `B`/`N` — formally connecting the Mind-vs-Gödel ladder to the
inconsistency-tolerance spectrum and the `DiagonalSystem` of `ParadoxSelfSoundness`.

# Future Directions — Counterfactual Number Theory: What If Primes Were Random?

This cycle formalized the **Cramér random model of the primes** as a genuine finite
probability space (a Bernoulli "random sieve" on a candidate window), and proved the
foundational expectation identities used as heuristics in cryptography:

- `cramer_total_mass` / `cramer_weight_nonneg` — the sieve is a probability distribution;
- `cramer_subset_indicator` — **independence**: `P(A ⊆ S) = ∏_{i∈A} p i`;
- `cramer_single`, `cramer_pair` — marginal and pairwise corollaries;
- `cramer_expected_count` — expected random-prime count `= ∑ p i` (model of `π(N) ≈ Li(N)`);
- `cramer_expected_pairs` / `cramer_expected_twin_count` — expected twin/`k`-tuple counts
  (Hardy–Littlewood heuristic skeleton).

All identities turned out to be **purely algebraic** in the weight family `p : ι → ℝ`;
positivity (`0 ≤ p ≤ 1`) is needed only to certify the distribution is genuine. The
entire theory collapses onto `Finset.prod_add`. The conjectures below build on this base.

## Conjecture 1 — Variance and second-moment concentration of the random prime count
Define `Var(|S|) = E[|S|²] − E[|S|]²` for the Cramér sieve. Conjecture (and formalize):
`Var(|S|) = ∑_{i∈s} p i (1 − p i)`, exactly (independence kills cross terms). Corollary:
under `p n = 1/log n` on `Icc 2 N`, the standard deviation is `Θ(√(N/log N))`, so the
random model concentrates: `|S| = (1+o(1)) ∑ 1/log n` almost surely. **Testable**: prove the
exact variance identity via `cramer_pair` + `cramer_single`; it is a finite computation.

## Conjecture 2 — Expected number of prime `k`-tuples (singular series skeleton)
Generalize `cramer_expected_twin_count` to arbitrary admissible offset patterns
`H = {h_1,…,h_k}`. Conjecture: the expected number of `n ∈ [2,N]` with all of
`n+h_1,…,n+h_k` random-prime equals `∑_n ∏_{j} p(n+h_j)`, and under Cramér's `p`
this is asymptotic to `∫ dt/(log t)^k`. **Testable**: the exact finite identity is a direct
iteration of `cramer_subset_indicator` with `A` of size `k`; the asymptotic is a separate
analytic lemma. Note the *deviation* of this from the true Hardy–Littlewood constant
`𝔖(H)` measures exactly how the genuine primes fail to be Cramér-random.

## Conjecture 3 — Maximal prime gap in the Cramér model (Cramér's conjecture, finite form)
Let `G_N` be the largest gap between consecutive random primes in `[2,N]`. Conjecture:
`E[G_N] = Θ((log N)²)` and `P(G_N > c (log N)²) → 0` for large `c`. **Testable first step**:
formalize, for the sieve, the exact probability that a fixed window `[m, m+L]` contains
*no* random prime: `∏_{n=m}^{m+L} (1 − p n)`, and prove the union-bound upper tail
`P(∃ gap ≥ L) ≤ ∑_m ∏ (1−p n)`. This is provable now from the weight definition.

## Conjecture 4 — Counterfactual divergence: where real primes beat the coin flips
Formalize a quantitative "non-randomness detector". For residue classes mod `q`, the
Cramér model predicts the random primes equidistribute with no bias, i.e.
`E[#{n∈s : n ≡ a (q), n random-prime}] = ∑_{n≡a} p n`, *independent of `gcd(a,q)`*.
Conjecture: the genuine primes deviate from this by exactly the factor `q/φ(q)` on the
coprime classes (and `0` otherwise). **Testable**: prove the model's class-count identity
(immediate from `cramer_expected_count` restricted to an arithmetic-progression subset),
then state the divergence as a separate, falsifiable comparison theorem against `Nat.Prime`.

## Conjecture 5 — Cryptographic key-generation success probability (Bernoulli sieve bound)
RSA key generation samples until it hits a prime. Model: in a window of `L` candidates each
prime with prob `p`, the probability of failing to find any prime is `∏ (1 − p n)`.
Conjecture: with `p n = 1/log n`, `O(log N)` independent samples suffice to find a prime
with probability `≥ 1 − ε`, and formalize the explicit bound
`P(failure in m samples) ≤ (1 − p_min)^m`. **Testable**: provable now from
`cramer_total_mass` and `cramer_weight_nonneg`; gives a verified, model-level justification
for the practical efficiency of probabilistic prime generation.

# Future Directions — The Spectral Gap of Sudoku

These conjectures extend the formalization in `Catalog/Novelty/SudokuSpectralGap.lean`,
which establishes (general order `n`): the Sudoku graph is `(3n²−2n−1)`-regular, its
adjacency spectrum is confined to `[−d, d]` with the all-ones Perron eigenvector at the
top, its chromatic number is exactly `n²`, and the partial-grid completion functor is
antitone with a sharp SAT (nonempty)→UNSAT (empty) dichotomy.

Each item below is stated to be **falsifiable** and **formalizable** in Lean.

## C1. Exact second eigenvalue and the spectral gap formula
**Conjecture.** The Sudoku graph of order `n` is a graph with exactly four distinct
adjacency eigenvalues, and its second-largest eigenvalue is `λ₂ = 2n − 1`, giving a
spectral gap `d − λ₂ = 3n² − 4n = n(3n−4)`. Equivalently, the gap grows quadratically in
`n` so the normalized gap `(d − λ₂)/d → 1`.
*Test:* compute the spectrum for `n = 2, 3, 4` by `decide`/`native_decide` on the
adjacency matrix and check the count of distinct eigenvalues and the value of `λ₂`.

## C2. The Sudoku graph is strongly regular iff `n = ... `
**Conjecture.** The order-`n` Sudoku graph is **not** strongly regular for any `n ≥ 2`
(unlike its building blocks: rows/columns/boxes individually give complete graphs).
Precisely, the number of common neighbours of two adjacent cells is *not* constant across
all adjacent pairs. *Test:* exhibit two adjacent pairs (same-box vs. same-row-different-box)
with different common-neighbour counts; formalize as a `∃`-counterexample to
`G.IsSRGWith ...`.

## C3. Phase-transition threshold for unique completion
**Conjecture.** There is a sharp clue-count threshold `m(n)` such that a uniformly random
clue set of size `< m(n)` almost never has a unique completion while one of size `> m(n)`
almost always does; and `m(n) = Θ(n²)`. As a first formal milestone (deterministic):
*any* clue set whose support meets every row, column, and box still need not pin the
solution, but a clue set equal to a full solution minus one cell always has a unique
completion. *Test:* prove the deterministic milestone via `completions_antitone` plus the
local cancellation already used in `sudokuColor_valid`.

## C4. Hoffman bound is tight ⇒ a fractional-relaxation rigidity
**Conjecture.** Hoffman's lower bound `χ ≥ 1 − λ_max/λ_min` is *tight* for the Sudoku
graph, i.e. `1 − d/λ_min = n²`, forcing `λ_min = −d/(n²−1)`. Combined with `C1` this
over-determines the spectrum and should pin all four eigenvalues. *Test:* once `λ_min` is
formalized, verify `1 − d/λ_min = n²` symbolically and cross-check against the spectra of
`C1`.

## C5. Tensor/Kronecker structure of the Sudoku operator
**Conjecture.** The Sudoku adjacency operator decomposes as a sum of Kronecker products of
all-ones and identity blocks: `A = (J⊗I + I⊗J + J⊗J)_{rows,cols,boxes} − 3·(I⊗I) − ...`
over the `Fin n × Fin n × Fin n × Fin n` factorization, so its eigenvalues are explicit
integer combinations of `{n, 0}` eigenvalues of `J` and `I`. This would make `C1` and `C4`
corollaries of a single tensor-eigenvalue lemma. *Test:* formalize `A` as such a Kronecker
combination on `Cell n` and prove the eigenvalues factor accordingly; the all-ones
eigenvalue `d = 3n²−2n−1` should drop out as the `(n,n,n)` corner, matching
`sudoku_top_eigenvalue`.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Phantom Topologies (Combinatorics)

Cycle-1/2 results live in `Catalog/Speculative/PhantomTopologies.lean`, where we proved that
on a finite carrier the topology is a *phantom* of its specialization preorder:

- `topology_eq_of_specializes_iff` — a topology is determined by the bare `⤳` relation;
- `specPreorder_bijective` — `topology ↦ specialization preorder` is a **bijection**
  `TopologicalSpace α ≃ Preorder α` (the classical "finite spaces = preorders");
- `continuous_iff_specializes` — continuity *is* specialization-monotonicity (morphisms are
  phantoms too);
- `phantom_asymmetry` — the realized preorders are genuinely directional.

The conjectures below are bold, falsifiable next steps. Each comes with a concrete Lean target.

---

## C1. T0 rigidity: phantoms collapse exactly onto partial orders
**Conjecture.** The observation map `specPreorder` restricts to a bijection between the
`T0` topologies on a finite `α` and the **partial orders** on `α`.
**Why plausible.** `specializationOrder` already upgrades the preorder to a partial order under
`T0Space`; antisymmetry is exactly the `T0` (Kolmogorov) condition.
**Lean target.**
```
theorem specPreorder_T0_bijective [Finite α] :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun (t : {t : TopologicalSpace α // @T0Space α t}) => (specialization partial order))
```
A corollary would be a *counting* statement: `#{T0 topologies on Fin n} = #{partial orders on Fin n}`
(OEIS A001035), complementing the full count A000798.

## C2. Homeomorphism is an order-isomorphism of phantoms
**Conjecture.** For finite spaces, `Homeomorph α β` is in natural bijection with order-isomorphisms
of their specialization preorders: `(α ≃ₜ β) ≃ (Specialization α ≃o Specialization β)`.
**Why plausible.** `continuous_iff_specializes` gives the arrow-level dictionary; a homeomorphism is
a continuous bijection with continuous inverse, i.e. a monotone bijection with monotone inverse.
**Lean target.** Build the explicit `Equiv` and prove both round-trips; specialize to deduce that
two finite spaces are homeomorphic iff their preorders are order-isomorphic.

## C3. Connectivity is a phantom (combinatorial connectivity)
**Conjecture.** A finite space is topologically connected **iff** its specialization preorder is
connected as a graph under the comparability relation `x ≤ y ∨ y ≤ x` (zigzag-connected).
**Why plausible.** In an Alexandrov space the minimal open set of `x` is its up-set; topological
components match equivalence classes of the reflexive–symmetric–transitive closure of `≤`.
**Lean target.**
```
theorem connected_iff_preorder_connected [Finite α] [TopologicalSpace α] :
    ConnectedSpace α ↔ (∀ x y : α, Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b => a ⤳ b ∨ b ⤳ a) x y)
```

## C4. McCord/Möbius bridge: Euler characteristic = Möbius number
**Conjecture.** For a finite `T0` space `X` with specialization poset `P`, the reduced Euler
characteristic of the order complex `Δ(P)` equals the Möbius number `μ(P̂)` of `P` with adjoined
`⊥`/`⊤` — a strict identity between a topological invariant and a purely combinatorial one.
**Why plausible.** This is the finite-space shadow of McCord's weak-homotopy equivalence
`|Δ(P)| ≃ X`; the alternating face count of `Δ(P)` is the order-complex Euler characteristic, which
Philip Hall's theorem identifies with a Möbius value.
**Lean target.** Define `orderComplex P` (chains of `P`), its Euler characteristic, and prove the
identity for the partial order produced by `specializationOrder`.

## C5. Asymptotic dominance of asymmetric phantoms
**Conjecture.** The fraction of topologies on `Fin n` that are `T0` (genuinely asymmetric phantoms,
cf. `phantom_asymmetry`) tends to `1` as `n → ∞`; equivalently `A000798(n) / A001035(n) → 1`.
**Why plausible.** A random preorder is asymptotically almost surely a partial order, since the
number of nontrivial inseparability classes is negligible for large `n`.
**Lean target.** A clean intermediate, fully finitary milestone: prove the *exact* small-case
counts agree with the phantom bijection, e.g. that there are exactly `4` topologies and `4`
preorders on a 2-element type, and exactly `3` of them are `T0`, by transporting the count along
`specPreorder_bijective`.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — The L-Function Oracle (Probability)

Derived from this cycle's verified Lean results:

- `Probability/SatoTateMeasure.lean` — the Sato–Tate law is a probability measure
  (`satoTate_total_mass = 1`) with verified `cos`-moments `(mean 0, second moment 1/4)`.
- `Probability/FactoringOracle.lean` — a single-split oracle factors `n` in `≤ log₂ n`
  calls (`SplitOracle.factor_bounded`), the burden concentrated in one `reduce` step.
- `Probability/SelbergOracle.lean` — degree/conductor conservation along functoriality
  towers (`nfold_degree`, `nfold_conductor`) plus an oracle⇒decidability collapse, built on
  the catalog file `Shared.SelbergClassCensus`.

The central methodological lesson: the grandiose "oracle implies RH/BSD/Langlands" claims
are, once formalised, either *tautological* (the oracle is asserted to output the answer) or
*conditional on an explicit reduction*. The genuinely load-bearing mathematics is elsewhere —
in the moments of the target measure, in the `log`-depth of the factoring recursion, and in
the conservation laws of the invariants. The conjectures below target that real content.

---

## Conjecture 1 — All Sato–Tate moments are the Catalan/central-binomial sequence

**Statement.** For every `k`, the `2k`-th `cos`-moment under `μ_ST = (2/π) sin²θ dθ` equals
`Catalan k / 4^k`, i.e. `∫₀^π cos^{2k}θ · (2/π) sin²θ dθ = C_k / 4^k` where
`C_k = (2k choose k)/(k+1)`; all odd moments vanish.

**The key insight is** that the Sato–Tate measure is exactly the spectral measure of the
`SU(2)` Haar trace, so its even moments count noncrossing pairings — the Catalan numbers —
which makes the whole moment sequence a *single closed-form arithmetic object* rather than a
list of unrelated integrals. This cycle verified the `k = 0, 1` cases (mass `1`, second
moment `1/4 = C_1/4`); the conjecture is the uniform generalisation.

**Why now?** We already have the integral machinery (`integral_sin_pow`,
`integral_sin_pow_mul_cos_pow_odd`) working end-to-end in Lean on this exact density, so the
inductive recurrence `M_{k} ↦ M_{k+1}` is within reach with the tools just exercised.

---

## Conjecture 2 — The factoring reduction is depth-optimal, not just depth-bounded

**Statement.** The `≤ log₂ n` bound in `SplitOracle.factor_bounded` is tight in the worst
case and tight on average: for `n = 2^m` every split oracle needs exactly `m` calls, and the
*expected* number of calls over uniformly random `n ≤ N` is `Θ(log log N)` (Erdős–Kac shape:
the number of prime factors `Ω(n)` concentrates at `log log n`).

**The key insight is** that the recursion tree of `factor_bounded` is precisely a binary tree
whose leaves are the prime factors *with multiplicity*, so the call count is `Ω(n) − 1`; the
deterministic bound is `log₂ n` but the *typical* value is governed by the Erdős–Kac law, a
genuinely probabilistic statement about the cost of the L-function oracle.

**Why now?** The leaf-counting identity is already implicit in the verified proof
(`length = Ω(n)`), so the deterministic optimality is a short additional lemma, and it sets up
the bridge to the catalog's number-theory files (`Applications/Fibonacci*`, Carmichael
material) where `Ω` of structured integers is studied.

---

## Conjecture 3 — Functoriality towers force a degree/conductor uncertainty bound

**Statement.** For any `SelbergDatum S` with `S.degree ≥ 1` and `S.conductor ≥ 2`, the
`n`-fold tower satisfies `(nfoldProduct S n).degree · log₂((nfoldProduct S n).conductor)`
grows like `n² · d · log₂ q`; equivalently the "analytic complexity"
`degree × log-conductor` is *super-additive* along towers, never sub-additive.

**The key insight is** that `nfold_degree` (linear) and `nfold_conductor` (exponential)
combine multiplicatively, so the analytic conductor — the quantity controlling the length of
the approximate functional equation, hence the true cost of evaluating the L-function —
*explodes quadratically* along a tower. An O(1) oracle would have to be uniform across this
explosion, which is exactly why a literal oracle is implausible.

**Why now?** Both growth laws are already proved in `SelbergOracle.lean`; multiplying them is
a one-step corollary, and it converts the vague "oracles are too powerful" intuition into a
concrete, falsifiable growth inequality on catalog `SelbergDatum`.

---

## Conjecture 4 — Oracle collapse is provably non-vacuous only with a length-bounded encoding

**Statement.** The decidability collapse `reduction_collapses` upgrades to a *complexity*
statement iff the encoding `f : X → SelbergDatum` has polynomially bounded conductor: if
`f x` has conductor `≤ poly(|x|)`, then `L` is decidable in time polynomial in the oracle
cost; without such a bound the collapse is logically true but computationally empty.

**The key insight is** that the only smuggled cost in "reduce to one L-query" is the *size of
the datum you hand the oracle*, measured by its conductor — Conjecture 3 shows this size can
blow up, so the honest collapse theorem must carry a conductor budget as a hypothesis.

**Why now?** `reduction_collapses` and `selberg_oracle_decidable` are already in place as the
unconditional (decidability-only) skeleton; adding a conductor-budget field to the encoding is
a natural refinement that makes the "polynomial hierarchy collapse" claim precise and testable.

---

## Conjecture 5 — A second-moment certificate distinguishes CM from non-CM curves

**Statement.** Define the empirical second `cos`-moment of the first `N` Frobenius angles of
an elliptic curve `E/ℚ`. For non-CM curves it converges to `1/4` (the Sato–Tate value proved
here); for CM curves it converges to `1/2`. Hence a single converging moment statistic, output
by the oracle, certifies the CM/non-CM dichotomy.

**The key insight is** that the verified value `1/4` is the *fingerprint* of the full `SU(2)`
Sato–Tate measure, whereas the CM case is governed by a `U(1)` measure with second moment
`1/2`; the gap `1/4 vs 1/2` is a clean, decidable separating observable rather than a full
equidistribution statement.

**Why now?** `satoTate_second_moment_cos = 1/4` is verified; the companion `U(1)` computation
`∫₀^π cos²θ · (1/π) dθ = 1/2` is an even simpler interval integral, so the separating
certificate is one short lemma away and turns the abstract Sato–Tate dichotomy into a finite
statistical test.

# Future Directions — CSS Codes as Cohomology

This cycle established the dictionary **CSS code = homology of an `F₂`-chain
complex** (`Core.lean`), *refuted* the hypercube conjecture for the 1-skeleton
cycle code (`CubeCode.lean`), and anchored the refutation with a fully explicit
`[[4,1]]` code on `C₄ = Q₂` (`RingCode.lean`). The surviving topological
invariant is the cyclomatic number `β₁(Q_n) = (n−2)·2^{n-1} + 1`, which equals
`1` **only** at `n = 2`. The directions below grow out of exactly those findings.

---

## Conjecture 1 — The cube becomes a `[[·,1,·]]` code only after filling 2-cells

For the *cubical* complex `Q_n` (vertices, edges **and** square 2-faces), the
homological code has `k = dim H₁(Q_n; F₂) = 0` for `n ≥ 2` (the cube is simply
connected), so to recover a single logical qubit one must quotient/identify
faces into a closed surface. Concretely: there is a surface `Σ` obtained from
`Q_n`'s 2-skeleton with `dim H₁(Σ; F₂) = 1` and code distance equal to the
girth `4`, **not** `2^{n/2}`.

- **The key insight is** that the mission's "1 qubit" claim silently assumes a
  *surface* (2-complex) where 2-cells kill all but one homology class, while the
  literal `Z₁/B₁` cycle code on the 1-skeleton has `B₁ = 0` and therefore
  over-encodes by the full cyclomatic number `(n−2)2^{n-1}+1`.
- **Why now?** `CubeCode.numLogical_graphCode` already isolates the `d₂ = 0`
  (no-2-cell) case; adding a nonzero `d₂` for the square faces is a direct,
  mechanical extension of the same `Core` dimension formula, so the surface vs.
  graph dichotomy is immediately testable in the existing framework.

## Conjecture 2 — Homological distance is governed by Hamming weight, and the cube saturates only the trivial Singleton bound

Define the code distance `d` as the minimum `hammingWeight` (already imported
from the catalog's `vecSupport`) over nonzero homology representatives. Then for
the `C₄` code `d = 4`, and every cube 1-skeleton code has `d = girth = 4`,
giving `k + d = β₁ + 4`, which violates the quantum Singleton bound
`k + 2d ≤ n + 2` for large `n` — i.e. the 1-skeleton codes are **bad** codes,
the opposite of the conjecture's "achieves the Singleton bound" claim.

- **The key insight is** that distance is a *minimum-weight* invariant of the
  cohomology class, so the catalog's `vecSupport_card_pos_of_ne_zero` is the
  exact primitive needed, and the constant girth `4` forces asymptotically
  vanishing relative distance `d/n → 0`.
- **Why now?** `RingCode.ker_boundary` shows the homology class explicitly as a
  single weight-4 vector; computing `hammingWeight` of a kernel basis is already
  `decide`-feasible at small `n`, so the Singleton-violation can be certified
  before any general theory is built.

## Conjecture 3 — `β₁(Q_n) = 1 ⇔ n = 2` is the only finite-qubit cube; tori are the right family

Replacing `Q_n` by the discrete torus `(C_m)^{×2}` (product of two `m`-cycles)
as a 2-complex yields `dim H₁ = 2` (the toric code) with distance `m`, the
genuine `[[2m², 2, m]]` family. Conjecture: among all "graph-cube-like" 1-complexes,
`β₁ = 1` characterizes `C₄` uniquely, and the *only* way to keep `k` bounded
while growing `n` is to add 2-cells (move to a surface).

- **The key insight is** that `cube_one_qubit_iff` pins `k = 1` to `n = 2` for
  the cube, so bounded-`k` code families must come from *surfaces of fixed
  genus*, not from growing graphs — exactly the toric-code construction.
- **Why now?** The closed form `cyclomatic_closed_form` makes the `k`-growth
  exact, so contrasting it against the constant `k = 2` of a torus 2-complex is a
  clean, fully arithmetic comparison reusing the present `cyclomatic` machinery.

## Conjecture 4 — Euler characteristic is the universal qubit budget

For any bounded `F₂`-chain complex `0 → Cₖ → ⋯ → C₀ → 0`, the alternating sum of
homology dimensions equals the alternating sum of chain dimensions
(`∑ (−1)ⁱ dim Hᵢ = ∑ (−1)ⁱ dim Cᵢ = χ`). Hence the *total* logical-qubit budget
across all degrees of a chain-complex code is the topological Euler
characteristic, a single integer invariant.

- **The key insight is** that `Core.finrank_homology` already expresses one
  homology dimension as a difference of ranks; iterating rank–nullity up the
  complex telescopes into `χ`, so "qubits = Euler characteristic" is a
  rank–nullity identity, not new analysis.
- **Why now?** `Core` proves the single-spot case with `finrank_quotient_add_finrank`;
  the multi-degree version is the same lemma applied inductively, well within the
  subagent's reach.

## Conjecture 5 — Every classical `[n,k]` `F₂` code is the degree-0 homology of a length-1 complex, making CSS ↔ classical functorial

For a parity-check map `H : F₂ⁿ → F₂^r`, the length-1 complex `F₂ⁿ →H F₂^r` has
`H₀ = coker H` and `H₁ = ker H = ` the classical code, with `dim H₁ = n − rank H`.
Conjecture: the assignment `(C₁, C₂) ↦ (chain complex)` and back is an
equivalence of categories between CSS codes and bounded `F₂`-chain complexes up
to chain homotopy.

- **The key insight is** that `numLogical_eq_css` is precisely the object-level
  half of this equivalence (`k = n − rank H_Z − rank H_X`); promoting it to a
  functor only requires tracking chain maps, which Mathlib's `HomologicalComplex`
  already supports.
- **Why now?** With the dimension dictionary proved and the cube/`C₄` examples in
  hand, the remaining work is purely categorical bookkeeping on top of existing
  `Core` definitions — no new hard analytic input is needed.

# Future Directions — Transreal Arithmetic & the Wheel Collapse

Derived from this cycle's verified findings in
`Catalog/Algebra/Transreal/{Basic,RingFails,Wheel,TropicalBridge}.lean`.

Cycle summary (what is now machine-checked, 0 sorries):

* `(𝕋, +, 0)` and `(𝕋, ·, 1)` are commutative monoids; `Φ` is absorbing.
* `𝕋` is **not** a ring: `+∞` has no additive inverse (`no_add_inverse_pinf`),
  distributivity fails (`distrib_fails`), `+∞` has no multiplicative inverse
  (`mul_inverse_axiom_fails`).
* `𝕋` is **not** a Carlström wheel: the involution `//x = x` fails at `-∞`
  (`recip_recip_ninf`) and the reciprocal is not multiplicative
  (`recip_mul_fails`).  Both failures are caused by the *two-signed* infinity.
* The projective collapse `±∞ ↦ ∞` gives `ℙ = ℝ ∪ {∞, ⊥}`, a genuine wheel:
  involution (`precip_precip`), reciprocal homomorphism (`precip_pmul`),
  modified distributivity (`wheel_distrib`), and `wheel_W7`, `wheel_W9` all hold.

---

## Conjecture 1 — The wheel obstruction is *exactly* the sign congruence

**Statement.** Let `~` be the smallest congruence on `𝕋` (w.r.t. `+`, `·`, `/`)
making the reciprocal an involution. Then `𝕋/~ ≅ ℙ`, and `~` identifies precisely
`+∞` with `-∞` (fixing every other point). In particular `ℙ` is the *initial*
wheel quotient of the transreals.

**The key insight is** that the only law-breaking in `𝕋` is sign-blindness of
`/0 = +∞`, so quotienting by the single relation `+∞ ~ -∞` must repair *all* wheel
axioms simultaneously — no further identifications are needed or allowed.

**Why now?** Both `𝕋` (`Basic.lean`) and `ℙ` (`Wheel.lean`) are formalized with
their full operation tables, so the quotient map and its universal property can be
built and verified directly rather than argued on paper.

---

## Conjecture 2 — Only two wheel axioms fail for the transreals

**Statement.** Equip `𝕋` with its (two-signed) operations. Then the commutative
monoid laws, `⊥`-absorption, modified distributivity (`(x+y)z + 0z = xz + yz`),
and the `0·y`-correction laws hold verbatim; the *only* wheel axioms that fail are
the reciprocal involution and the reciprocal homomorphism.

**The key insight is** that every wheel axiom not mentioning `/` is sign-agnostic,
so it cannot detect the `+∞ / -∞` distinction; only the two reciprocal laws probe
the sign of `1/0`.

**Why now?** We already have `TReal.mul_assoc'`, `add_assoc'`, and the absorbing
lemmas; the remaining `+`/`·`-only wheel axioms are within reach of the same
case-bash automation, making this a concrete, finite verification target.

---

## Conjecture 3 — A transreal survives iff it lives in the cancellation-free fragment

**Statement.** A first-order identity over `(+, ·, 0, 1)` that is a theorem of `ℝ`
remains true for **all** transreal substitutions if and only if it is derivable
without additive or multiplicative cancellation (equivalently, provable in the
theory of commutative semirings minus distributivity-with-subtraction).

**The key insight is** that the transreal failures are all instances of lost
invertibility (`∞ + x ≠ 0`, `∞·(1/∞) ≠ 1`); an identity transports to `𝕋` exactly
when its proof never inverts an element that can become `±∞` or `0·∞`.

**Why now?** `RingFails.lean` pins the exact obstructions to invertibility, giving
a precise syntactic boundary to test: instrument candidate `ℝ`-identities and check
transreal survival against cancellation-usage in their proofs.

---

## Conjecture 4 — `𝕋` differs from Mathlib's `EReal` at a single point

**Statement.** There is an injection `ℝ ∪ {±∞} ↪ 𝕋` under which transreal `+` and
`·` agree with `EReal` addition and multiplication **except** at the indeterminate
`(+∞) + (-∞)`: `EReal` returns `-∞` (its `⊥`-wins convention) while `𝕋` returns
`Φ`. This single discrepancy is exactly what costs `EReal` its associativity-with-a
two-sided identity that `𝕋` trades for totality-with-`Φ`.

**The key insight is** that both systems totalize `±∞` arithmetic, but `EReal`
makes an *arbitrary* choice at `∞ - ∞` whereas `𝕋` introduces a *new* value `Φ`;
comparing them isolates the price of each design decision.

**Why now?** `EReal` is fully developed in Mathlib and `𝕋` is now formalized here,
so the comparison map and the exact-disagreement-locus theorem can be stated and
checked immediately, turning a folklore remark into a verified statement.

# Future Directions — Cellular Automata as Algebraic Geometry over GF(2)

These conjectures are distilled from the v16a research cycle in
`Computation/ECAFixedVariety.lean` and `Computation/ECALinearSubspace.lean`.

The cycle established two anchor facts:

* **Refutation.** The Turing-complete Wolfram Rule 110 has a *single* fixed point
  (the all-zero configuration) for every length `n ≥ 1`, hence fixed-point-variety
  dimension `0` — the *minimum* among nonempty varieties — directly falsifying the
  conjecture "Turing-complete ⇒ maximal fixed-point dimension"
  (`complexity_dimension_conjecture_false`).
* **Structure.** For *linear* (additive) rules the fixed-point set is literally the
  kernel of `step − id`, a `GF(2)`-subspace, so it always has `2^k` points
  (`linearFixed_card_pow_two`); Rule 110 is provably nonlinear (`g110_not_linear`).

The fixed-point variety is therefore a real GF(2) scheme, but its dimension is the
*wrong* complexity invariant. The directions below propose the right one.

---

## Direction 1 — Spacetime entropy, not fixed-point dimension, tracks complexity.

**Conjecture.** Define the *spacetime subshift* `Σ_r` of rule `r` as the set of valid
bi-infinite orbit diagrams, an SFT over the de Bruijn graph. Its topological entropy
`h(Σ_r) = lim (1/n) log #(period-n columns)` separates Wolfram's classes:
`h = 0` for Class 1/2, `h > 0` for Class 3, and Class 4 (e.g. Rule 110) sits exactly
at the `h = 0` boundary while supporting unbounded transients.

**The key insight is** that Turing-completeness lives in the *transient orbit
structure* (gliders, collisions), which the static fixed-point variety throws away;
the spacetime SFT retains it and its entropy is the genuine invariant.

**Why now?** This cycle proved the fixed-point count of Rule 110 is constantly `1`,
so any complexity invariant *must* be orbit-based, not equilibrium-based. The
transfer-matrix machinery for counting period-`n` configurations (`tr(T^n)`) is
already formalizable in Mathlib (`Matrix.trace`, `Matrix.pow`), giving an immediate
attack route.

## Direction 2 — Fixed-point count is `tr(Tᵣⁿ)` for a 4×4 GF(2)-transfer matrix.

**Conjecture.** For every rule `r` there is an explicit `0/1` matrix `T_r` indexed by
2-cell windows such that `Nat.card {s : Config n // isFixed (g r) s} = trace (T_rⁿ)`,
and the asymptotic growth rate equals the Perron eigenvalue `ρ(T_r)`; the variety
"dimension" is `log₂ ρ(T_r)`, a rule-intrinsic real number.

**The key insight is** that the fixed-point set is a *subshift of finite type*, so its
cardinality is governed by a transfer matrix exactly as in statistical mechanics —
turning a combinatorial count into linear algebra.

**Why now?** We verified the pattern computationally (Rule 90: `1,1,4,1,1,4,…`,
period-3 because `ρ` has a cube-root-of-unity spectrum; Rule 204: `2^n` because
`ρ = 2`). Proving `#fix = tr(Tⁿ)` for the five formalized rules is a finite, bounded
target that would convert every numeric observation in the Lab Notes into a theorem.

## Direction 3 — `3 ∣ n ⇔ Rule 90 has a nonzero fixed point`.

**Conjecture.** The Rule 90 fixed-point subspace `linearFixed 1 0 1` over `Config n`
has dimension `> 0` if and only if `3 ∣ n`; equivalently the circulant operator
`x ↦ x_{i-1} + x_{i+1} − x_i` is singular over `GF(2)` exactly when `3 ∣ n`. More
generally the dimension equals `deg gcd(t² + t + 1, tⁿ − 1)` in `GF(2)[t]`.

**The key insight is** that a linear ECA's fixed-point dimension is a *cyclotomic*
quantity: it counts roots of the rule's characteristic polynomial among the `n`-th
roots of unity, so number theory (orders mod small primes) governs the geometry.

**Why now?** We proved a nonzero fixed point exists at `n = 3`
(`rule90_nontrivial_fixed_three`) and `linearFixed_card_pow_two` already exposes the
dimension as `finrank`. Mathlib's `Polynomial.cyclotomic` and circulant-matrix
support make the gcd characterization directly reachable.

## Direction 4 — Linearity is *decidable from the variety* up to the converse gap.

**Conjecture.** A rule `r` is GF(2)-linear iff its fixed-point variety is closed under
addition for *all* lengths `n` simultaneously; a single length can fail (the converse
gap noted by the Critic: Rule 0 and Rule 110 both give count `1 = 2⁰` yet only Rule 0
is linear). Precisely: `(∀ n, IsSubmodule (fixed r n)) ↔ r ∈ {0,60,90,102,150,170,204,240,…}`
(the 8 additive rules and their reflections).

**The key insight is** that linearity is a *global* property of the whole tower of
varieties `{V_n}`, not of any single `V_n` — closure-at-one-`n` is necessary but not
sufficient, which is why our safe-direction lemma (`g110_not_linear`) certifies
nonlinearity pointwise rather than from a single count.

**Why now?** This cycle isolated the exact converse counterexample (count `1` is
realized by both a linear and a nonlinear rule), so the precise boundary is known and
ready to be formalized as an `Iff` over the finite catalogue of additive rules.

## Direction 5 — Affine rules give *cosets*; the empty variety detects an inhomogeneity.

**Conjecture.** A rule with affine ANF `f = ℓ(a,b,c) + 1` (a linear part plus the
constant `1`, e.g. Rule 51 `= b + 1`) has fixed-point variety either empty or a
*coset* of `linearFixed ℓ`; it is empty exactly when `1 ∉ image(ℓ − id)`. Thus the
empty variety (`rule51_not_isFixed`) is the GF(2) shadow of an unsolvable affine
system, and `#fix ∈ {0} ∪ {2^k}`.

**The key insight is** that the constant term in the ANF turns the *kernel* (subspace)
into an *affine* solution set, so the dichotomy "empty vs. power-of-two coset" is the
Rouché–Capelli theorem over `GF(2)` applied to cellular automata.

**Why now?** We already proved Rule 51's variety is empty for all `n`; recasting that
as the inconsistency of an affine GF(2) system, via Mathlib's `LinearMap.range` and
coset API, would unify the linear (Direction 1–3) and degenerate cases under one
solvability criterion.

# Future Directions — The Mathematics of Jigsaw Puzzles: NP-Completeness and Topology

This cycle produced `Catalog/Logic/JigsawPuzzles.lean`, a self-contained, fully
verified (0 `sorry`) theory of edge-matching jigsaw puzzles connected to the
existing complexity framework in `Catalog/Logic/PvsNPFoundations.lean`. It
covers: the ℤ/4 rotational symmetry of a piece (`rotate_order_four`,
`rotate_bijective`), the discrete Euler/handshake identity for the board
(`board_handshake`), the local matching constraint with monochromatic solvability
(`monochromatic_solvable`), brute-force decidability over finite palettes
(`solvable_decidable`), abstract NP membership of the solvability language
(`puzzle_inNP`), NP closure under reductions / union / intersection
(`inNP_of_reducible`, `inNP_union`, `inNP_inter`), and the hardness bridge
(`inNP_of_hard`).

The following conjectures are precise, falsifiable targets for follow-up cycles.

## Conjecture 1 (Karp reduction: 3-Partition ↪ edge matching)
Formalize a many-one reduction `ManyOneReducible PARTITION_LANG (SolvableLang Color m n)`
for an explicitly constructed color alphabet and gadget pieces, where
`PARTITION_LANG` is a Lean-formalized NP-hard partition/packing language. Combined
with the existing `puzzle_inNP` and the `inNP_of_hard` bridge, this would yield a
machine-checked statement that edge matching is NP-complete relative to that base
language. Testable milestone: prove the reduction's forward direction
(`x ∈ PARTITION → Solvable`) via an explicit placement.

## Conjecture 2 (1D puzzles are tractable — Eulerian path characterization)
A single-row board (`m = 1`) is solvable **iff** the multiset of available pieces
admits an Eulerian-trail ordering of the "color transition" multigraph whose
vertices are colors and whose edges are pieces `(west, east)`. Formalize this
equivalence and conclude that 1-row solvability is decidable in polynomial time,
in sharp contrast to the 2D case. The catalog identity `interiorAdj_single_row`
(`= n - 1`) is the combinatorial seed: a row is a path with `n-1` constraints.

## Conjecture 3 (Topological lower bound on color count)
If an `m × n` board with `m, n ≥ 2` has a **unique** valid placement up to the
trivial symmetry, then the number of distinct edge colors used is at least
`interiorAdj m n / 2 + 1`. Intuition: uniqueness forces interior edges to be
"keyed" distinctly enough to break the grid graph's automorphisms. A first
formal step is to bound, for a fixed valid placement, the number of *alternative*
placements by the number of repeated interior colors.

## Conjecture 4 (Certificate-complexity / counting hierarchy)
Define `#Solutions C m n` as the cardinality of `{P : Placement C m n // Valid P}`
(finite by `solvable_decidable`). Conjecture: the map `(m, n) ↦ #Solutions` over a
fixed `k`-color palette satisfies a transfer-matrix recurrence in `n` of order
bounded by `k^k` (a "puzzle transfer matrix"). Formalizing the transfer matrix and
proving the recurrence would place the counting version `#EDGE-MATCH` in `#P` and
give exact generating functions for fixed-height strips.

## Conjecture 5 (Rotation-quotient and the dihedral upgrade)
The current model fixes orientations. Extend `rotate` (the ℤ/4 action,
`rotate_order_four`) to the full dihedral action `D₄` by adding reflections, and
conjecture that allowing free rotation of pieces strictly enlarges the solvable
language but preserves NP membership: `InNP (SolvableUpToRotation C m n) (Placement C m n × (Fin m → Fin n → ZMod 4))`.
The added `ZMod 4` component is the per-cell rotation certificate; proving the
verifier remains decidable upgrades `puzzle_inNP` to the oriented-piece setting.

# Future Directions — *Isomorphisms of Meaning: When Structures Collide*

This cycle established two anchor results (see `Catalog/Bridges/StructuralCollisions.lean`
and `Catalog/Bridges/BooleanLogicField.lean`):

* **A1.** A bare ring satisfying the single law `x*x = x` is *forced* to have
  characteristic two and to be commutative, and its multiplication **is** the
  greatest-lower-bound (meet) of the order `a ≤ b ↔ a*b = a`. (Algebra ⇒ Order.)
* **A2.** Propositional logic `(Bool, xor, and)` **is** the field `ZMod 2`, via an explicit
  `RingEquiv Bool (ZMod 2)`; `&&` is simultaneously the ring product and the order meet
  (cross-linked to A1). (Logic ≅ Algebra.)

The following conjectures are concrete, falsifiable next targets for the same theme.

---

### C1. Symmetric difference is an 𝔽₂-vector space (Set ≅ Algebra)
For any type `α`, the powerset `Set α` with symmetric difference `△` as addition and
intersection `∩` as multiplication is a *Boolean ring*: `s ∩ s = s`, `s △ s = ∅`, and the
order induced by A1 is set inclusion with `s ⊓ t = s ∩ t`.
**Testable form:** instantiate the A1 abstractions (`add_self`, `mul_comm'`, `mul_isGLB`)
at `Set α`/`Finset α` and prove `StructuralCollisions.le s t ↔ s ⊆ t`, identifying the
A1-meet with `∩`. Predicts every finite Boolean algebra is an 𝔽₂-module of dimension
`= #atoms`.

### C2. Stone-type rigidity of the collision
The isomorphism `Bool ≃+* ZMod 2` is the *unique* ring isomorphism, and more generally any
ring homomorphism `R → S` between Boolean rings is automatically a lattice homomorphism for
the A1-induced orders (`a ≤ b → f a ≤ f b`), and conversely a bounded-lattice hom of finite
Boolean algebras is a ring hom.
**Testable form:** prove `Subsingleton (Bool ≃+* ZMod 2)`, and prove
`f (a*b) = f a * f b → (StructuralCollisions.le a b → StructuralCollisions.le (f a) (f b))`
for a `RingHom` between Boolean rings.

### C3. Idempotence is the *exact* boundary of the collapse
The forced-commutativity phenomenon (A1) is special to the exponent law `x^2 = x`.
**Conjecture:** for each fixed `n ≥ 2`, a ring with `∀ x, x^n = x` is commutative
(Jacobson's theorem). The cases `n = 2` (done) and `n = 3` should be provable by elementary
expansion; general `n` is the deep target.
**Testable form:** prove the `n = 3` case `(∀ x, x*x*x = x) → ∀ a b, a*b = b*a` from scratch
(no Mathlib `Jacobson` import), then attempt `n = 4`.

### C4. The order/algebra collision lifts to a categorical equivalence
The constructions of A1 should assemble into an equivalence of categories between *finite
Boolean rings with ring homs* and *finite Boolean algebras with bounded-lattice homs*, with
object map `R ↦ (R, ≤_{a*b=a})` and inverse given by symmetric difference (C1).
**Testable form:** build the two functors on objects + morphisms in Lean and prove the
round-trips are identities on `Bool`, `ZMod 2`, and `Set (Fin n)`.

### C5. A "no-collision" obstruction in characteristic ≠ 2
The collision in A1/A2 is a characteristic-two miracle. **Conjecture:** there is *no*
nonzero ring `R` with `∀ x, x*x = x` and `(1 : R) + 1` a unit; equivalently, idempotence
forbids odd characteristic.
**Testable form:** prove `(∀ x : R, x*x = x) → (2 : R) = 0`, and deduce that a Boolean ring
that is also a field must be `ZMod 2` (so `Bool`), pinning A2 as the unique field-collision.

# Future Directions — The Fermi Paradox as a Pigeonhole Principle

Derived from the verified results in this cycle:

* `FirstMoment.lean` — the first moment method over finite weighted spaces
  (`exists_zero_of_expectation_lt_one`, `prob_zero_ge_one_sub_expectation`).
* `DrakeBound.lean` — the conservative Drake inequality (`drake_expected_lt_one`,
  `prod_le_pow_of_forall_le`) and its fusion with the pigeonhole
  (`fermi_alone_under_conservative_drake`).
* `Bridge.lean` — the cross-domain `fermi_resonant_listening_window`, combining
  the Pythagorean averaging lemma with the Fibonacci strong-divisibility law.

Each conjecture below is falsifiable and stated so it can be formalized next.

---

## C1. The empty-set lower bound is *tight* up to the integrality gap.

**Conjecture.** For every finite weighted space with expectation `E < 1`, the
total weight of the zero set satisfies `1 − E ≤ w(Z) ≤ 1`, and the lower bound
`1 − E` is attained exactly when the nonzero outcomes all equal `1` (a Bernoulli
support).  Conversely, if `w(Z) = 1 − E` then `X` is `{0,1}`-valued on its
support.

*The key insight is...* that `prob_zero_ge_one_sub_expectation` only used
`X i ≥ 1` on the complement, so equality forces `X i = 1` there — the slack in
the bound is exactly `∑_{X≥2} w_i (X_i − 1)`, a nonnegative "over-counting" term.

**Why now?** We already proved the inequality in `prob_zero_ge_one_sub_expectation`;
characterizing its equality case is the immediate next refinement and needs only
a careful `Finset.sum_eq_zero` argument on the slack term.

---

## C2. A "second moment" companion forces *non-empty* outcomes when `E > 1`.

**Conjecture.** If `E = ∑ wᵢ Xᵢ > 1` and the variance is controlled
(`∑ wᵢ Xᵢ² ≤ C·E²`), then `w({X ≥ 1}) ≥ E²/(C·E²) = 1/C`: with civilizations
expected *and* not too clustered, contact is likely.

*The key insight is...* that the first moment method is one half of a dichotomy;
the Paley–Zygmund inequality is its mirror, turning `E > 1` into a positive
probability of a *non-empty* cosmos.

**Why now?** Our `FirstMoment.lean` machinery (finite weighted sums in `ℚ`,
`Finset.sum_le_sum`) is exactly the substrate needed for Cauchy–Schwarz over a
`Finset`, so the second-moment bound is a natural sequel rather than new theory.

---

## C3. The Drake bound is *dimension-robust*: hurdles, not values, decide it.

**Conjecture.** For any list of independent hurdle probabilities each `≤ 1/10`,
`Nplanets ≤ 10¹⁰`, and at least `11` hurdles, the expected number of
civilizations is `< 1` — regardless of the precise per-hurdle values.

*The key insight is...* that `prod_le_pow_of_forall_le` bounds the product by
`(1/10)^(#hurdles)`, so the *count* of independent filters, not optimistic
tuning of any single one, is what drives `E` below `1`.

**Why now?** `prod_le_pow_of_forall_le` is already proved; combining it with
`drake_expected_lt_one` via `pow_le_pow_right_of_le_one` closes the conjecture
with no new infrastructure.

---

## C4. Resonant listening times are *stable under window perturbation*.

**Conjecture.** If two dense families `F`, `F'` over `U` differ in at most `k`
windows, then they share a resonant listening time whenever
`8k < |F|` — the pigeonhole witness of `fermi_resonant_listening_window`
survives small observational noise.

*The key insight is...* that the averaging lemma's slack (`miss ≤ |F|/4`) leaves
room: removing or adding `k` windows shifts the incidence count by `≤ k`, so the
`3/4` majority is preserved while `8k < |F|`.

**Why now?** `fermi_resonant_window_coverage` already exposes the `3·|F| ≤
4·hit` margin; a perturbation lemma is a direct `omega`-style consequence of that
inequality plus `Finset.card_union_le`.

---

## C5. Fibonacci signal resonance yields a *shared detector frequency*.

**Conjecture.** At the resonant time `a` of `fermi_resonant_listening_window`,
if every active civilization's epoch is divisible by a common `d`, then `fib d`
divides the gcd of *all* their Fibonacci signals — a single divisor witnesses
universal resonance.

*The key insight is...* that `IsStrongDivSeq.dvd_gcd_index_iff` lifts pairwise
divisibility to the whole active family by induction on the window set, turning
the bridge's pointwise meet law into a global one.

**Why now?** Both ingredients — the resonant witness and the meet law
(`StrongDivSeq.IsStrongDivSeq.dvd_gcd_index_iff`) — are imported and proved in
`Bridge.lean`; the global statement is a `Finset.induction` away.

# Future Directions — Hypergraph Ramsey Theory: Beyond Graphs

This cycle formalized, with zero `sorry`, a self-contained 2-color Ramsey theory
for `r`-uniform hypergraphs over the `Finset (Fin n) → Bool` coloring model:

- **Structural laws** (`Defs.lean`): color symmetry, monotonicity in the vertex
  count (via an embedding transport), monotonicity in clique size, and the
  vacuous degenerate regime `k < r`.
- **Probabilistic lower bound** (`LowerBound.lean`): the Erdős first-moment
  argument `2·C(n,k) < 2^{C(k,r)} ⟹ R_r(k,k) > n`, with concrete instances
  `R_3(5,5) > 11` and `R_3(6,6) > 29`.
- **Growth separation** (`Separation.lean`): the explicit floor
  `R_3(k,k) > 2^m` whenever `k·m + 1 < C(k,3)` (giving `2^{Ω(k²)}`), the tower
  function `tower 2 k = 2^{2^k}`, and the strict separation
  `2^{k²} < 2^{2^k}` for `k ≥ 5`.

The findings below are derived directly from what survived (and what resisted)
the team loop.

---

## Conjecture 1 — The explicit floor is `2^{⌊(C(k,3)−1)/k⌋}`, and it is the best the first moment can give

**Statement.** For every `k ≥ 3`, `R_3(k,k) > 2^{m_k}` where
`m_k = ⌊(C(k,3) − 2)/k⌋`, and no first-moment argument over the uniform random
coloring yields any larger floor (the threshold `2·C(n,k) < 2^{C(k,3)}` is
violated for `n = 2^{m_k+1}` once `k` is large).

**The key insight is** that the affordable exponent in `R3_exp_lower_bound` is
budgeted by `k·m + 1 < C(k,3)`, so `m` can grow only like `C(k,3)/k ≈ k²/6` —
the quadratic exponent is a *hard ceiling* of the first moment, not a loose
constant.

**Why now?** `R3_exp_lower_bound` already isolates the budget inequality as a
single hypothesis, so the optimization `max m s.t. k·m+1 < C(k,3)` is a finite,
fully formal arithmetic problem — provable today by `omega`-style reasoning.

---

## Conjecture 2 — A formal stepping-up lemma closes the floor–ceiling gap to a true double exponential

**Statement.** There is a constant `c > 0` and a Lean-provable inequality
`R_3(k+1,k+1) ≤ 2^{R_2(k,k)} + 1`, which composed with `R_2(k,k) ≤ 4^k` yields
`R_3(k,k) ≤ tower 2 (c·k) = 2^{2^{c·k}}`.

**The key insight is** that `single_exp_lt_double_exp` already certifies
`2^{k²} < tower 2 k`: the floor we proved lies *strictly inside* the conjectured
ceiling, so the open problem is precisely to raise the floor or lower the ceiling
across this verified gap.

**Why now?** The `tower` function and its double-exponential identity
`tower_two` are in place, so an Erdős–Rado stepping-up formalization can be
stated against a concrete, already-proved target rather than informal asymptotics.

---

## Conjecture 3 — Off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers are polynomially skew

**Statement.** For fixed `r` and `l`, `R_r(k,l)` grows only polynomially in `k`
(degree `≈ l − 1`), in sharp contrast to the double-exponential diagonal — i.e.
`R_3(k,l) = k^{Θ(l)}` for fixed `l`.

**The key insight is** that `hyperRamsey_color_symm` makes the two clique sizes
interchangeable, so the asymmetry must come entirely from the *smaller* side `l`
controlling the C(k,r) edge budget; the counting bound degrades to a polynomial
when one side is bounded.

**Why now?** `hyperRamsey_counting_lower_bound` is already stated for the general
diagonal and `hyperRamsey_color_symm`/`hyperRamsey_mono_clique` give the
off-diagonal scaffolding for free; only the asymmetric counting estimate remains.

---

## Conjecture 4 — The uniformity hierarchy is strict: each extra layer adds one exponential

**Statement.** `R_{r+1}(k,k)` is bounded between `tower (r-1) (Ω(k))` and
`tower (r-1) (O(k))`; equivalently, increasing the uniformity `r` by one raises
the tower height by exactly one for every `k` large enough.

**The key insight is** that the tower height in `single_exp_lt_double_exp`
already encodes "number of exponentials," so a strict hierarchy is the statement
that the height in the lower bound and upper bound agree level-by-level with `r`.

**Why now?** `tower` is defined for arbitrary height and `R3_exp_lower_bound`
generalizes verbatim to `R_r` (the proof only used `C(n,k) ≤ n^k` and the
`C(k,r)` budget), so the `r`-indexed hierarchy is one induction away.

---

## Conjecture 5 — Constructive (derandomized) colorings match the probabilistic floor

**Statement.** There is an explicit, polynomial-time-describable family of
2-colorings of the 3-subsets of `Fin (2^m)` (e.g. via a finite-field or
binary-string "stepping-up" construction) with no monochromatic
`k`-clique whenever `k·m + 1 < C(k,3)` — matching `R3_exp_lower_bound`
without invoking the averaging/pigeonhole step.

**The key insight is** that the current proof is *existential* (pigeonhole over
all `2^{C(n,r)}` colorings); the same floor should be witnessed by a *named*
coloring, turning an averaging argument into a verifiable construction.

**Why now?** The model `Finset (Fin n) → Bool` is already computable, so a
candidate explicit coloring can be `#eval`-tested against small `k, m` before
attempting the general proof — the experiment loop is immediately runnable.

# Future Directions — The Prime Number Crossword

This cycle established the two boundary facts of the prime crossword in
`Cryptography/PrimeGaps/`:

* `exists_consecutive_composites` / `gaps_unbounded` — gaps are arbitrarily wide;
* `gaps_unbounded_cofinal` — arbitrarily wide gaps occur arbitrarily far out;
* `nextPrime_sub_le` — every gap above a prime `p` is at most `p` (Bertrand).

Below are falsifiable conjectures for the next cycle. Each is stated so that it
can be formalized directly as a Lean theorem about `PrimeGaps.nextPrime`.

## C1. A quantitative Bertrand gap bound, sharpened
**Conjecture.** For every prime `p ≥ 5`, `nextPrime p - p ≤ p / 2`, and more
strongly the relative gap `(nextPrime p - p) / p → 0`.
*Formalization target:* prove `∀ p, p.Prime → 5 ≤ p → nextPrime p - p ≤ p / 2`
using Nagura-type explicit estimates (prime in `(n, 6n/5]` for `n ≥ 25`).
*Falsifiable:* a single prime with gap exceeding `p/2` refutes it.

## C2. Average gap matches the logarithm (Prime Number Theorem flavor)
**Conjecture.** The mean gap up to `x`, `x / π(x)`, grows like `log x`. A first
formal milestone: `∀ x ≥ 2, π(x) ≤ x` paired with a lower bound
`π(x) ≥ c · x / log x`. *Target:* connect `nextPrime` iterates to `Nat.primeCounting`
in Mathlib and prove `nextPrime p - p` has Cesàro average `Θ(log p)`.

## C3. Maximal gap function is well defined and unbounded but slowly growing
**Conjecture.** `G(x) := max { nextPrime p - p : p prime, p ≤ x }` satisfies
`G(x) ≤ x` (immediate from Bertrand) and `G(x) → ∞` (immediate from
`gaps_unbounded_cofinal`), while conjecturally `G(x) = O((log x)^2)` (Cramér).
*Target:* formalize `G` as a `Finset.sup`, prove the two unconditional bounds,
and state Cramér's `O((log x)^2)` bound as an open hypothesis.

## C4. Twin-gap dichotomy / Polignac
**Conjecture (Polignac, open).** Every even number `2k` is a gap between
consecutive primes infinitely often: `∀ k ≥ 1, {p : nextPrime p - p = 2k}` is
infinite. *Target:* state precisely with `Set.Infinite`; as a tractable
sub-result prove the *finite* version — for each `k` there is at least one prime
gap of size `≥ 2k` (already implied by `gaps_unbounded`) and search for explicit
small-`k` witnesses via `native_decide`.

## C5. Cryptographic safe-prime spacing
**Conjecture.** Safe primes (`p` with `(p-1)/2` also prime) exhibit the same
gap-unboundedness: `∀ N, ∃ p, p` safe-prime `∧ nextSafePrime p - p ≥ N`.
*Target:* define `SafePrime` and `nextSafePrime`, then transport the factorial /
bracketing construction. This directly models the cost of safe-prime search in
Diffie–Hellman parameter generation.

# Future Directions — Category Theory as a Universal Language (Bridge cycle)

Derived from the Stage 3 (Analysis) and Stage 4 (Critique) findings of this
cycle. Each conjecture is bold, falsifiable, and Lean-checkable.

## FD-1. The regular subobjects of a topos form a Boolean algebra.

**Conjecture.** For every `Order.Frame α`, the fixed points of the double-negation
nucleus (`{a | ToposDoubleNegationLattice.IsRegular a}`) carry a
`BooleanAlgebra` structure whose meet is `⊓`, whose top/bottom are `⊤`/`⊥`, and
whose complement is `aᶜ`, with join given by `a ⊔' b := (aᶜ ⊓ bᶜ)ᶜ`.

The key insight is... that meet-preservation (`dneg_inf`) plus idempotence make
`dneg` a *nucleus*, and the sheafification `a ↦ aᶜᶜ` collapses intuitionistic
logic to classical logic exactly on its fixed points — Booleanness is forced, not
assumed.

Why now? We already proved closure under `⊓` (`isRegular_inf`) and the bounds
(`isRegular_bot/top`); only the (de Morgan) join and complement laws remain, all
expressible with the same `compl`/`himp` API verified in this cycle.

## FD-2. The Yoneda iso-corollary upgrades to an equivalence of groupoids.

**Conjecture.** The map `X ↦ yoneda.obj X` induces an equivalence between the core
groupoid of `C` and the full subcategory of representable presheaves, and
`iso_iff_representable_iso` is its object-level shadow.

The key insight is... that full faithfulness (the single fact powering
`isoPreimage` and `endEquiv`) is exactly the data of an equivalence onto the
essential image, so the `Nonempty (· ≅ ·)` biconditional is the π₀ of a deeper
categorical equivalence.

Why now? `Yoneda.fullyFaithful` is in scope and `endEquiv_comp`/`endEquiv_one`
already show the hom-level functoriality; the essential-image construction is the
only missing ingredient.

## FD-3. `dneg` is the unique non-trivial Lawvere–Tierney topology on a chain.

**Conjecture.** On a totally ordered frame (a chain) `α`, every nucleus
`j : α → α` (monotone, extensive, idempotent, meet-preserving) other than the
identity equals the double-negation nucleus `dneg` collapsed onto `{⊥, ⊤}`; i.e.
chains admit only the trivial and the double-negation topologies.

The key insight is... that on a chain `aᶜ` is `⊤` for `a = ⊥` and `⊥` otherwise,
so `dneg` is the indicator of "`> ⊥`", and any idempotent extensive monotone
self-map respecting `⊓` is pinned by its values at the two bounds proved regular
here (`dneg_bot`, `dneg_top`).

Why now? The nucleus axioms are all formalized in this file; the chain case is a
finite/order-induction argument (`omega`/`rcases` on comparisons) well within
reach.

## FD-4. Knaster–Tarski computes sheafification of any nucleus, not just `dneg`.

**Conjecture.** For an arbitrary nucleus `j` on a frame, the least fixed point
`sInf (KnasterTarskiBridge.preFixed j)` above an element `a`, i.e.
`sInf {x | a ≤ x ∧ j x ≤ x}`, equals `j a`, exhibiting sheafification as the
Knaster–Tarski least-fixed-point closure relative to `a`.

The key insight is... that a nucleus is precisely a meet-preserving closure
operator, so its image is the set of fixed points, and the catalog's
`knaster_tarski` already delivers those fixed points constructively — we proved
the `a = ⊥` and `a = ⊤` extremes (`lfp_dneg_eq_bot`, `gfp_dneg_eq_top`).

Why now? The bridge between `dneg` and `KnasterTarskiBridge` is already wired
(`dneg_knaster_tarski`); generalizing from `dneg` to an abstract nucleus reuses
the identical fixed-point lemmas.

## FD-5. The frame of opens detects regularity geometrically.

**Conjecture.** For `Opens X`, `IsRegular U ↔ U = interior (closure U)`, and the
regular opens are exactly the complemented elements of the Heyting algebra
`Opens X`; hence `X` is extremally disconnected iff every open is regular.

The key insight is... that `Uᶜᶜ` in `Opens X` is interior-of-closure, so
`dneg`-fixed points are the classical *regular open sets*, linking the abstract
nucleus to a checkable point-set condition.

Why now? `opens_dneg_inf` and `opens_isRegular_*` already specialize the nucleus
to `Opens X`; identifying `dneg` with interior∘closure is a single Mathlib lemma
away and turns regularity into a topological invariant.

# Future Directions — BB84 Security Formalization (Cycle 1)

Derived from the Stage-3 Analysis and Stage-4 Critique of this cycle. The cycle
established, in `Catalog/Cryptography/BB84/`:

* `KeyRateThreshold.lean` — the secret-key rate `r(Q) = log 2 − 2·binEntropy Q`,
  its strict monotonicity in the QBER, IVT existence and uniqueness of a critical
  QBER `p* ∈ (1/16, 1/8)` (bracketing the textbook ≈ 11%), with the bracket
  *certified by the integer facts* `7^7 < 2^20` and `2^56 < 15^15`.
* `Protocol.lean` — the intercept–resend attack induces `QBER = 1/4`, which lies
  strictly above `p*`, so `r(1/4) < 0` (detectable).
* `PrivacyAmplification.lean` — the leftover-hash Cauchy–Schwarz bound
  `∑|pᵢ − 1/M| ≤ √(M·∑pᵢ² − 1)`, its exponential-decay corollary, and a catalog
  bridge (`Cryptography.MerkleDamgard.compression_collision_of_card`) showing
  deterministic extractors are never injective.

## Conjecture 1 — The threshold is the unique transcendental certified by `2·H₂ = 1`

**Statement.** The map `p ↦ binEntropy p` restricted to `(0, ½)` has a unique
preimage of every value in `(0, log 2)`, and the BB84 threshold `p*` is the
*algebraically independent* root of `2·binEntropy p = log 2`; no rational `p`
satisfies it.

The key insight is... that the bracket reduction `binEntropy(a/b) ⋛ (log 2)/2 ⟺
(integer power comparison)` means rationality of `p*` would force an exact integer
identity `mᵐ·… = nⁿ·…`, which a 2-adic valuation argument can rule out.

**Why now?** We already have the exact integer-reduction machinery
(`binEntropy_one_eighth_gt` etc.); promoting it from two sample points to a general
`binEntropy(a/b)` lemma makes the irrationality statement directly attackable.

## Conjecture 2 — Tightening the bracket is purely arithmetic, to any precision

**Statement.** For every `ε > 0` there are rationals `q₁ < p* < q₂` with
`q₂ − q₁ < ε` whose verification reduces to a single `norm_num`-checkable integer
inequality (no `log` bounds).

The key insight is... that `binEntropy(a/b) ⋛ (log 2)/2` is equivalent to
`(b−a)^{(b−a)}·??? ⋛ b^{b}·2^{…}`, an integer comparison whose size grows only
polynomially in the denominator, so arbitrary-precision brackets stay decidable.

**Why now?** The current `(1/16, 1/8)` bracket already demonstrates the reduction;
the generalization is a finite-template lemma the subagent can grind once stated.

## Conjecture 3 — The Cauchy–Schwarz leftover bound is order-optimal

**Statement.** The constant in `∑|pᵢ − 1/M| ≤ √(M·∑pᵢ² − 1)` cannot be improved
to `c·√(M·∑pᵢ² − 1)` with `c < 1`: there is a family of distributions (two-point
spikes) making the ratio LHS/RHS → 1.

The key insight is... that equality in finite Cauchy–Schwarz requires `|dᵢ|`
constant across the support, which the balanced two-point distribution
`p = (½+t)δ₀ + (½−t)δ₁` realizes in the limit, pinning the optimal constant at 1.

**Why now?** `statDist_le_collision` is proved via `Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq`,
whose equality case is characterized in Mathlib; the optimality proof reuses exactly
that characterization.

## Conjecture 4 — Composable security: the entropy gap adds across stages

**Statement.** If error correction leaks `λ` bits and privacy amplification extracts
to `ℓ = k − λ − 2s` bits (smooth min-entropy `k`), then the final statistical
distance is `≤ 2^{−s}`, and these bounds *compose additively in the exponent* over
sequential protocol stages.

The key insight is... that the leftover-hash exponent `(ℓ − k)/2` is linear in the
entropy gap, so chaining stages multiplies the small `√` factors, i.e. adds the
exponents — exactly the structure of the catalog's `HybridTelescope` advantage sums.

**Why now?** `privacyAmplification_exp_bound` already exposes the gap `ℓ − k` as a
`zpow`; bridging to `Cryptography.Security`'s hybrid/telescope advantage lemmas
would yield an end-to-end composable BB84 security statement.

## Conjecture 5 — Intercept–resend is the worst *symmetric* individual attack at fixed QBER

**Statement.** Among individual (non-collective) eavesdropping strategies that induce
a given sifted QBER `Q ≤ p*`, intercept–resend maximizes Eve's mutual information,
and the protocol stays secure exactly while `Q < p*`.

The key insight is... that for symmetric individual attacks Eve's information is a
monotone function of the disturbance, so the single-parameter trade-off `Q ↦ I_E(Q)`
crosses the reconciliation cost `H₂(Q)` precisely at the `2·H₂ = 1` threshold.

**Why now?** We have the threshold `p*` characterized and the intercept–resend QBER
`1/4` formalized; quantifying `I_E(Q)` for the symmetric family turns the qualitative
"detectable" result into a sharp optimal-attack theorem.

description:
# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Average-degree shattering for uncrowded hypergraphs

This cycle established the *deterministic core* of the average-degree independence
theory for `k`-uniform hypergraphs:

- handshake identity `∑_v deg v = k·|E|` (`sum_degree_eq_kuniform`),
- the deletion/transversal independence bound `α(H) ≥ n − |E|` and its
  average-degree form `α(H) ≥ n·(1 − d/k)` (`exists_independent_avgDegree`),
- the linear edge bound `|E|·C(k,2) ≤ C(n,2)` and the average-degree upper bound
  `d ≤ (n−1)/(k−1)` for uncrowded hypergraphs (`avgDegree_le_of_uncrowded`).

The deep `log d / d^{1/(k−1)}` regime remains open at the formal level. The
following conjectures are falsifiable extensions derived from the patterns above.

## Conjecture 1 — Average-degree AKPSS with the log factor (grand challenge)

For every `k ≥ 2` and `0 < ε < 1` there is `d₀` such that every uncrowded
`k`-uniform hypergraph on `n` vertices with average degree `d ≥ d₀` has an
independent set of size `≥ (1−ε)·n·(log d / ((k−1)d))^{1/(k−1)}`.

The key insight is that the average-degree hypothesis can be reduced to the
maximum-degree theorem by a *degree-pruning + weighting* argument: delete the few
high-degree vertices (they carry a vanishing fraction of the edge mass because
the linear edge bound `d ≤ (n−1)/(k−1)` caps the total), leaving an almost-regular
sub-hypergraph to which the semi-random/nibble method applies.

Why now? The deterministic core (this cycle) already gives the matching *upper*
bound `d ≤ (n−1)/(k−1)` that controls the high-degree tail, so the only missing
ingredient is a formal Rödl-nibble lemma — a self-contained, reusable target.

## Conjecture 2 — Tightness of the linear edge bound forces design structure

If an uncrowded `k`-uniform hypergraph attains `|E|·C(k,2) = C(n,2)`, then every
pair of vertices lies in exactly one edge, i.e. `H` is a Steiner `2-(n,k,1)`
system.

The key insight is that equality in the pair double-counting forces the edge
pair-sets to *partition* the C(n,2) vertex pairs, which is precisely the defining
incidence property of a Steiner system.

Why now? Our proof of `card_le_of_uncrowded` already exhibits the injection of
edge-pairs into vertex-pairs; equality analysis of that exact injection is the
direct next step and needs no new machinery.

## Conjecture 3 — Deletion bound is asymptotically optimal without uncrowdedness

For each `k`, there is a sequence of `k`-uniform (not necessarily uncrowded)
hypergraphs with average degree `d → ∞` whose independence number is
`Θ(n·d^{−1/(k−1)})`, with no `log d` factor; hence uncrowdedness is *necessary*
for the AKPSS improvement.

The key insight is that random `k`-uniform hypergraphs concentrate edges on
shared pairs, destroying the "spread" that the nibble exploits, so the plain
deletion bound `n·(1 − d/k)` (and its `d^{−1/(k−1)}` optimization) is best
possible there.

Why now? The deletion bound is already formalized here; pairing it with an
explicit random/algebraic construction turns "the log factor needs uncrowdedness"
from folklore into a verified separation.

## Conjecture 4 — Weighted (fractional) average-degree bound

Assign nonnegative weights `w_v` to vertices; then there is an independent set
`S` with `∑_{v∈S} w_v ≥ (∑_v w_v)·(1 − d_w/k)`, where `d_w` is the
weight-averaged degree.

The key insight is that the transversal-complement construction is *weight
oblivious*: replacing counting by weighted counting in the handshake identity and
the deletion step carries the whole argument through verbatim.

Why now? The current `exists_independent_card_ge` is the unweighted instance;
generalizing its handshake and `Finset.card_biUnion` steps to weighted sums is a
mechanical, high-value upgrade that unlocks LP-duality style applications.

description: Formalize Conway's combinatorial game algebra (games as surreal numbers, nim-values, the Sprague-Grundy theorem that every impartial game is a nim-heap), and solve classic games (Hackenbush, Blue-Red-Green). (Conway, Berlekamp, Guy, Winning Ways)

description: Formalize and compare hypercomputational models — accelerating (Zeno) Turing machines, infinite-time Turing machines, and Putnam-Gold trial-and-error predicates — proving strict containment relations and identifying which physical 'axioms' each requires. (Putnam, Gold, Hamkins-Lewis)
title: Hypercomputation Taxonomy: Zeno, Infinite-Time, and Trial-and-Error

description: Formalize Khot's Unique Games Conjecture: it is NP-hard to distinguish whether a unique-game constraint graph is (1-eps)-satisfiable or eps-satisfiable, and derive its consequences for tight hardness-of-approximation of MAX-CUT, vertex cover, etc. (Khot 2002)
title: Unique Games Conjecture (Khot)

(Asimov)
title: Three Laws of Robotics as Deontic Logic

description: Formalize BQP and QMA, the Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm, and the first oracle separation between BQP and BPP, establishing that quantum polynomial time is genuinely stronger than classical probabilistic polynomial time relative to an oracle. (Bernstein-Vazirani 1997)
title: Quantum Complexity: BQP, QMA, and BQP-vs-BPP Oracle Separation
